records.description:
For those who have forgotten your leisure time in your busy daily life, we introduce a romantic travel course that you can enjoy comfortably in the city center. This course is also a travel destination open to all, including men and women of all ages, people with disabilities, pregnant women, and pets. If you dream of a healing trip where you can walk around leisurely all day, do not hesitate to go to Gupo this weekend. A satisfying day will unfold before your eyes, enough to make you feel cool even in the scorching midsummer heat.

Recommended courses for a romantic trip to Gupo

Gupo Obstacle-Free Trai
Golden Sunset Bridge
Samnak Eco Park
Printze

Gupo Mujangaesup Forest Trail
 Gupo Mujangaesup Forest Trail is a gentle deck path for people with disabilities, pregnant women, and old people to use comfortably.

At the entrance, there is a parking lot that can accommodate about ten cars, including an 'automatic pest repellent sprayer,' and a parking lot for people with disabilities. A 'power assist device charger for people with disabilities' has been installed for people using electric wheelchairs or electric scooters, showing careful consideration for people with disabilities or old people who use this place.

The length of the Gupo Mujangaesup Forest Trail deck is 2km from the entrance to Haneulbaram Observatory, and it takes about 40 to 50 minutes on foot, but it is recommended to set aside more time when using a wheelchair. There are shortcuts to the top of the stairs across the deck, so it seems very useful for those who want to go to the top quickly.
The trail has a zigzag pattern to the top, and there are separate spaces for wheelchairs and strollers to pass through, so you can use it without any inconvenience. The shade created by the dense forest along the trail allows you to move without difficulty, even in the middle of the day, full of hot sunlight, and the fresh air provided by trees makes your body and mind healthy.

In the middle of the way to the summit, there are two observatory points where you can take a break while looking at the Nakdonggang River. On the way to the summit, there are also strangely shaped rocks, such as Geobukbawi Rock and Jeongsangbawi Rock, so it would be a fun experience to look for them one by one. At Haneulbaram Observatory, on the top, you can look down at the open city of Busan and the Nakdonggang River through telescopes. If you take a photo there with the wonderful scenery, you will feel a sense of achievement after the hard work.

Golden Sunset Bridge
The Golden Sunset Bridge, located at the entrance of Gupo Market, is a pedestrian bridge that connects Gupo and Hwamyeong Eco Park. As the name suggests, it is located in an excellent location to watch the sunset across the Nakdonggang River toward Gimhae.

Golden Sunset Bridge operates elevators at three locations: Gupo Market, the midway point of the bridge, and the observatory where the Buk-gu tourist information center is located. So people using wheelchairs or strollers can use the bridge comfortably. The braille blocks at the entrance to the elevators for the visually impaired, and the braille marked on the elevator buttons allow more people to use this place comfortably.
If you go up the bridge and walk toward Hwamyeong Eco Park, you can feel the different scenery of the Gupo railroad and the riverside road. Walking to the end, you can see an observatory with a tourist information center and simple seats where you can sit and relax. Hwamyeong Eco Park, which you can view from the observatory deck at a glance, makes your eyes feel comfortable thanks to its unique green area and abundant plants.

In particular, if you visit this place at sunset, you can enjoy the fantastic scenery of the Nakdonggang River turning red as the sun sets, making it a popular sunset spot in Busan. At night, you can see the wonderful night view with the lighting, so if you have time, be sure to watch both the sunset and the night view.

Samnak Eco Park
Samnak Eco Park is a representative space for sports and rest in Busan and is widely spread on the left and right sides of the Nakdonggang River bank. It is also located close to Hwamyeong Eco Park, connected to Golden Sunset Bridge. It has many attractions, such as sports facilities, walking trails, and flower colonies, where you can meet various flowers every season.

Large parking lots are located throughout the park, and each has a separate parking area for people with disabilities. The entire park is flat, and the trails are well-designed to make it easy to move around with a wheelchair or stroller, so it's good for families to visit comfortably with pregnant women, older adults, and people with disabilities.

When traveling by public transportation, you can go directly to Samnak Riverside Park using the Gangbyeonnadeulgyo Bridge connected to Gwaebeop Renecite Station on Busan-Gimhae Light Rail Transit in Sasang. There are elevators with braille blocks and braille, so wheelchairs, strollers, or people who enjoy riding can easily use them.
Trees and benches are placed throughout the green area in the park, so you can rest under the shade even in the middle of the day, and thanks to its spacious size, it is perfect for families. Furthermore, thanks to the well-equipped various sports facilities where you can enjoy basketball and soccer, people who like sports continue to visit throughout the day.

At Samnak Riverside Park, you can use various convenience facilities, including benches where you can rest and sinks where you can wash your hands. In particular, some portable toilets with wheelchair lifts are located here and there so that people with disabilities or older people using wheelchairs can use all facilities without any inconvenience.

Between early July and early August, it is recommended to visit the large lotus colony near Samnak Riverside Park. During this time, you can see the lotus flowers in full bloom, and their unique beauty is so attractive that many people visit, even in the scorching heat.

Printze
 You can taste special food at the Spanish restaurant ‘Printze’ near Gupo Station. Its first floor is a restaurant, and the second is a gallery. It is a place that is in line with the recent trend of the increasing population raising pets; pets are allowed on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays.

When you enter the store, the tables with different vibes catch your eye. The soft lighting on the tables harmonizes well with the props placed throughout the store, creating a comfortable atmosphere. The space on the second floor where the gallery is located draws attention to its interior, which starts with a typewriter and consists of unique props and frames. Typewriters that work provide a special experience to those who like analog vibes thanks to the unique feeling at their fingertips and the distinctive typing sound.
In Printze, you can taste a variety of Spanish food, and as recommended by the manager, I chose ink paella, tomato pasta, gambas, sangria, and white wine. The ink paella with clams and shrimp adds a rich flavor by combining the strong scent of squid ink and the savory taste of the rice, and the rich sauce of tomato pasta is excellent.

Gambas, a combination of soft shrimp and spicy garlic flavor, captivates the taste buds. Especially it goes very well with white wine. If you want to experience an exotic atmosphere and food in Busan, stop by ‘Printze,’ a Spanish restaurant near Gupo Station.

records.description:
As more and more people think of their pets as family, more and more people want to travel with their pets. However, it’s not easy to find a travel destination you can visit with them. Have you ever wondered where you can have a good time with your pet in your chosen travel destination? If so, read on! The following is a list of excellent places for you to visit in Busan with your pet. Let’s have a look together!

Shinho Park
Shinho Park is famous for its tidal flats, which you might think would be impossible to find in Busan. There is also a pine forest and walking paths around Galmaet Trails, so it is a park that nearby residents often use. The park has soccer fields, basketball courts, and various exercise equipment, making it a great place to exercise or take a walk. There is also a water park for children to cool off in the summer heat.

If you walk around the park, you can find wide lawns everywhere. People enjoy gateball or park golf in the morning, and in the afternoon, when the park is crowded, you can see many residents with their dogs. Seeing the puppies happily running around on the wide lawn is so cute and refreshing.
There is also a stage in the park, and sometimes you can hear musicians playing their instruments and singing, so you can spend time enjoying the music surrounded by the natural greenery.

Although the park has well-established walking paths inside, there is a long trail along the side of the park, so you should take a walk with your dog and look at the sea and Gadeokdaegyo Bridge in the distance. When the weather is hot, you can take a pleasant walk with your pet on the tree-shaded trail inside the park.

Artificial Migratory Bird Habitat Myeongpum Dulle Trails
 I think many people still don't know about this place. Originally, it was a place where the general public was prohibited from entering because it was a military operation area, so it is preserved as an internal wetland, its natural state. It has been open as a trail since July 2022.

Myeongpum Dulle Trails are neither too long nor too short, so they are perfect for a leisurely walk. Since it was a military operation area, the trail starts after passing through the iron gate. The trail that starts near Sodam Park continues right near Sinhodaegyo Bridge. However, please remember that there is no entrance near the bridge, so you have to go out the same way you came in.
The Dulle Trails start right next to the sea, so you can enjoy a walk while feeling the natural sea air. Thanks to the flooring laid on the ground, it is soft and comfortable, so you can walk without feeling tired on your feet. Also, a wetland is right next to it, so you can feel a little further away from the city center. Unfortunately, however, it is not yet possible to enter the wetland. The Myeongpum Dulle Trails are also connected to Galmaet Trails, and there is a small forest trail beside the road, so enjoy a walk there with your pet.

Forest 3002
 Finding a cafe where you can go with your pet is also something many pet owners have to consider. There is a cafe worth visiting with your pet not far from Artificial Migratory Bird Habitat Myeongpum Dulle Trails. The cafe has a large yard where you can run and play freely with your pets.

As soon as you enter the cafe, a spacious yard welcomes you, which is the perfect space to enjoy various games with your pet. Enjoy the cafe in the yard when the weather is nice or stay inside when the heat is at its peak.
When you enter the cafe, it is fun to see the furniture arranged differently for each space, and the light comes in brightly through the wide windows, giving it a very cozy feeling. Various products you will want to own are on display, and small exhibitions are held on certain days. It’s fun to look around. 

Above all, the sunlight coming through the wide window is really bright, so if you take a picture with your pet, it is a photo spot where you can get hundreds of the pics of the day. Take pictures with your beloved pet and enjoy a relaxing time.

records.name: Enjoy healing holidays in Busan: The city's best wellness destinations
records.description:
Wellness tourism which allows people to experience travel and healing at the same time has attracted a lot of interest recently.

In Busan, which is full of natural scenery and abundant infrastructure, a wellness tourist destination was selected by Busan Metropolitan City and Busan Tourism Organization.

Enjoy wellness tourism in Busan with a variety of themes, from natural resources to beauty, yoga, and meditation!

1) [Nature(Forest&Ocean)] Crazy Surfers (Gwangalli SUP Zone)

Did you know that a wellness tourism experience can be enjoyed at Gwangalli Beach, a calm sea in the middle of the city?

It helps you to keep your body and mind healthy, by adding beautiful sunrise and sunsets to ‘SUP yoga’, which combines the SUP(stand-up paddleboard) experience and yoga.

In particular, after completing your experience at Gwangalli SUP Zone, there are shower areas and rest places, so you can finish the tour conveniently.

For more information, please refer to the Crazy Surfers official website or Instagram (@crazy_surfers).
2) [Nature(Forest&Ocean)] Busan Children’s Grand Park

Is there anyone who only thinks of nature that is distant from the city when it comes to wellness? You can find a forest even in the middle of the city.

There is a healing forest inside Busan Children’s Grand Park located in Busanjin-gu, where you can see a large size of cypress forest. 

Why don’t you enjoy the beauty of nature wherever you go, and visit Seongjigok Valley Reservoir, a national cultural asset located inside Children’s Grand Park?

For more information, please refer to the Busan Children’s Grand Park website.
3) [Nature(Forest&Ocean)] Ahopsansup Forest

Busan’s representative forest, Ahopsansup Forest! This place is equipped with the infrastructure for wellness-related workers, including forest education experts and forest interpreters, and is suitable for wellness tourism.

Ahopsansup Forest, which has maintained its natural appearance for a long time, is famous not only for bamboo colonies but also for abundant ecological resources such as cypress trees and Geumgang pine trees.

If you walk slowly while looking at the beautiful scenery in a dense forest, you will experience that daily stresses are reduced naturally.

For more information, please refer to Ahopsansup Forest's website.
4) [Yoga&Meditation] Naewonjeongsa Temple

Temple stay is one of the representative healing experiences that cannot be missed in wellness tourism. Did you know that it is also possible in Busan?

Naewonjeongsa Temple, located at the foot of Gudeoksan Mountain, has a temple stay living center and an international meditation healing center, allowing for a variety of wellness experiences.

At Naewonjeongsa Temple, where you can breathe clean air in nature while being highly accessible, not far from the city, you can feel the unique charm of a temple stay, where you can escape from daily life and concentrate on yourself.

For more information, please refer to the Naewonjeongsa website.
5) [Yoga&Meditation] Hongbeopsa Temple

Hongbeopsa Temple is the temple where the largest seated Buddha statue in Korea is located. 

In this place, you can have singing bowl healing meditation, and temple stay. The singing bowl, a traditional Tibetan instrument, is one of the representative wellness experiences as the sound resonates when tapping or rubbing the surface to bring comfort.

In particular, Hongbeopsa Temple is equipped with an infrastructure for English interpreters and overseas travel guides, so foreigners can visit and have a wellness experience whenever they want.

For more information, please refer to the Hongbeopsa Temple website.
6) [Beauty&Spa] ClubD Oasis

Haeundae ClubD Oasis, a new hot tourist attraction that opened in Jul 2023, is the only beauty and spa-themed wellness tourist attraction among the places selected this year.

ClubD Oasis, which will become a valuable oasis for those looking for relaxation in their daily lives, is equipped with wellness experience elements such as a spa and sauna as well as a water park.

If you take a rest with a beautiful view of Haeundae Beach in a sauna and spa with various themes, you will experience true wellness tourism.

For more information, please refer to the ClubD Oasis website.

records.description:
Now that 2023 is nearing its end, many of us are restless as we wistfully let go of the previous year and anticipate the new one. Despite the restlessness, there are some good things about the year’s end, like light festivals held in many parts of the city. 

We invite you to visit the mecca of Christmas trees, a place full of romance even in the coldest weather. Let's take a picture of the day at photo spots for unforgettable memories!

Gwangbok-ro Winter Light Tree Festival
 Gwangbok-ro in the old downtown area of Busan, is once again lighting up in colors. The Christmas Tree Cultural Festival is held in every December with a different theme for each year. This year’s theme is “Shining Heritage 345,” which reflects the past, present, and future of Jung-gu, and the festival will be lit up with lights until January 14, 2024. They say the event was inspired by Choryangwaegwan, which was a diplomatic post with the Japanese some 345 years ago, and the history is illuminated with the lights.

As you enter Gwangbok-ro on the opposite side of Lotte Department Store, the first thing you will see is a fountain of lights called the Light Fountain of Independence ('Gwangbok' in Korean). 

The street trees along Gwangbok-ro are adorned with colorful lights and ribbons with snowflake images rustle in the wind under the night sky to create a romantic atmosphere. To complete the scene, there are also colorful Christmas trees, snowmen, and Rudolph the red-nosed reindeer in every corner of the streets. Once you get to the main attraction of the festival at the square, there you will find a giant tree, casting light in all directions. The excitement of the Christmas Tree Cultural Festival might just make you forget the cold weather and feel warm inside at the end of the year.

Operating period: November 15, 2024  – February 2, 2025
Lighting time: 18:00~22:00

Busan Citizens Park Mirror Pond Light Festival
Busan Citizens Park, which has always been a popular place of relaxation for the local people of Busan, also hosts its annual winter light festival. This year’s theme is the fantastic Luminarie Island that brings good luck, installed with a sculpture that looks like cascades of light coming down from the sky to the pond. 

A whopping 360,000 light bulbs are installed vertically, creating the illusion of standing in the middle of the starlit outer space. The hundreds of thousands of lights reflected in the pond also gives the illusion of a doorway to another dimension. In the center of the starry sky is a lucky dragon with a lucky pouch, a symbol of good fortune for the upcoming Year of the Dragon. The tree-lined street near Luminarie Island is also something you don’t want to miss. The colors of the lights change every moment, creating a mystical atmosphere. The reflection on the pond is also impressive. Against the backdrop of the still-white western sky, the buildings around the island are lit up one by one, and the trees turn red and blue. 

The cold winter breeze makes the lights stand out even more clearly. You can enjoy Luminarie Island and tree-lined streets from various angles by walking along the deck path that crosses the pond.

Operating period: December 15, 2024 – February 2, 2025
Lighting time: 17:30 - 23:00

Shinsegae Simon Busan Premium Outlets
Located in Gijang-gun, Shinsegae Simon Busan Premium Outlets are a photogenic place for Instagrammers, as it looks like an outlet mall straight out of a foreign country. The exotic scents wafting from the exterior of the building instantly transport you to a foreign city. In December, there's even a colorful Christmas tree, making the space more photogenic than any other. The central square, lit by a giant tree against a backdrop of European-style buildings, could be any city in Europe.

The Christmas tree that fills the round stage has extraordinary details. Divided into gold and silver, the color scheme is simple, but trees are full of the decorations and lights to add a touch of glamor. 

The floor is white, as if it's covered in snow, and there are silver balls and deer of different sizes scattered throughout Christmas markets are spread out on both sides of the square. Here, you can find all sorts of Christmas-related props and decorations. The spirit of Christmas feels even stronger by the cheerful carols coming from everywhere.

Hours: Winter season (November to April) 10:30 - 21:00

Village de Ananti
When asked to choose the most beautiful Christmas tree spot in Busan this year, many people would probably choose ‘Village de Ananti’. 

Recently opened in Gijang-gun, ‘Village de Ananti’ is a reproduction of a European Christmas village with a square installed with over 100 trees overlooking the sea. Centered around a 10-meter tall tree, small and large trees form a small forest, creating an enchanting atmosphere. It can be very pleasant to walk among the trees and see the scenery changing from moment to moment. The visual splendor created by thousands of light bulbs and ornaments cannot be missed. The place may be crowded, but winter in Villages de Ananti is beautiful enough to turn the downside of being in a crowd into the upside of enjoying the holiday excitement.

On weekends, snow is sprinkled twice a day. This is a fun event in Busan, a city where snow is rare. The cool view of the Gijang Coast from the Tree Square is also a highlight of the place. A place where you can enjoy the view of the the sea and twilight sky along with the tree – this is what makes Village de Ananti even more special.

Operating period: November 7, 2024 – December 31, 2024
Lighting time: 08:30 – 24:00

records.name: Specialty teahouses, the magic of a cup of tea to melt away the cold of the winter
records.originalName: 겨울을 녹이는 차 한 잔의 마법, 이색 전문 찻집(한,영,중간,중번,일)
records.description:
If you are looking for a nice cup of tea that will warm up your body and soul during the cold winter months, you are in luck. These teahouses are gems that have the trifecta of authenticity, expertise, and ambiance.

Darakjae
As soon as the door opens, you will be able to feel the warmth from the sweet and pleasant aroma of jujube tea. Located in Hwamyeong-dong, Buk-gu, Darakjae is designed with traditional elements to make it look and feel like a cozy hanok. Its interior alone took more than a year to build, designed by a hanok expert invited by the owner of the teahouse who wanted to share the beauty of hanok. Every cushion, piece of furniture, and accessory was carefully arranged.

The teahouse offers various types of tea, with over 100 different teas, including traditional teas and also those imported directly from overseas. It is also used as a multicultural space for performances and cultural events as well. A large grand piano in one corner of the room adds to the cultural aura. The fragrant aroma, hot tea, and elegant teaware, coupled with the clear notes of the piano, will make you feel a deep sense of calm and relaxation.

Darakjae
Address: 180, Geumgok-daero, Buk-gu, Busan
Contact: +82-51-365-0527
Opening hours: 12:30-22:30 (Sunday 12:30 PM – 9:00 PM), Closed on national holidays
Prices: KRW 6,000 for Darjeeling tea and KRW 7,000 for Dong Ding tea
How to get there: Walk for 4 minutes from Exit 4 of Sujeong Station on Busan Metro Line 2
Parking: If you are driving, use the parking lot in the shopping area

Grenier TEA (Salon de Grenier)
Located in a residential neighborhood in Daeyeon-dong, Nam-gu, Grenier TEA is a charming, calm, and quiet place to enjoy a cup of tea.

The first floor is a teahouse while the second floor is dedicated to tea classes. Both floors have a cozy white interior just like the tearooms in Europe. In addition to tea, it also serves a variety of other tea-inspired beverages to help beginners to get familiar with tea. Each of these subtly flavored drinks is unique in its own way. If you are looking for a more unique tea and beverage experience, Grenier TEA is the place to go. 

Basic tea comes with a teapot and a teacup. For an additional 1,000 won, you can upgrade it to the “English Tea Set,” which includes organic pure cane sugar and milk. Desserts include "Sweet Lemon Red Bean Jelly" and "Classic Scone," the latter of which is a delicacy of this teahouse, served with homemade jam made from five different types of berries and cream.

They have a specialty menu for every season, so it's worth visiting the place once a year to savor the season with a cup of tea. For more information about new menu items, please visit the teahouse’s official website.

Grenier TEA (Salon de Grenier)
Address: 1F, 53, Cheonjedeung-ro, Nam-gu, Busan
Contact: @tea_atelier_ (Instagram DM available)
Opening Hours: 12:00-18:00, Closed every Monday and Tuesday 
Prices: KRW 7,000 for tea (English Tea Set costs an additional KRW 1,000), KRW 10,000 for Single Estate Tea, and KRW 12,000 for Bespoke Tea
How to get there: Exit 5 of Daeyeon Station on Busan Metro Line 2 → Transfer to Village Bus Nam-gu 2 or Nam-gu 6 at Daeyeon Station or Busan Bank → Get off the bus at Sanseong Church Culture Center and walk for 4 minutes towards the teahouse

From Tea
From Tea doesn’t look and feel like any ordinary café or teahouse although it’s located right in the middle of the downtown area. It must be the bamboo garden and glass walls, a combination of which create a calm and cozy atmosphere. It has an Oriental style interior with fine teacups along with other types of tea ware, and decorative objects that make you feel welcome. The second floor, dedicated to tea classes, has a stylish terrace and an eye-catching display of tea-related items.

If you order a house tea, you will be served a cup of black tea with tea ware including a teacup. Taking a moment of break to have a cup of tea with those you love can be a great way to soothe your tired mind and body. Served in an elegant teacup, milk tea is not only rich in flavor, but also appealing to the eye.

From Tea was originally a tea class, but the owner also opened a teahouse after moving to Haeundae. The teahouse makes a point of serving tea in a high-quality cup and distinguishes itself from others by offering tea and food classes where you will see how serious and professional the owner is when it comes to tea and food.

From Tea
Address: 22, Jwadongsunhwan-ro 8beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Contact: +82-51-754-2261
Opening hours: The café will be temporarily closed. Only tea classes will be held during this period.
Prices: KRW 7,000 for house tea, KRW 8,000 for Haeundae milk tea, and KRW 4,000 for Americano
How to get there: Walk towards the teahouse for 4 minutes from Exit 6 of Jung-dong Station on Busan Metro Line 2
Parking: If you are driving, use the Haeundae public parking lot.

Hoshinoa of Suwolgyeonghwa
Hoshinoa of Suwolgyeonghwa is a teahouse located in Yeonje-gu, Busan. As “hoshi” is the Japanese word for “star,” and “noa” is the Hebrew word for "rest,” its name means "shimmering space of rest.” The neatly arranged tables and the bamboo garden outside the window, especially the stunning drone footage of various Japanese landscapes projected on the window, will make you feel as if you were in Japan. 

The teahouse is famous for its refreshingly fruity “Lilong Lilong” to “Matcha Milk” with matcha flavor, both of which can be enjoyed just about everyone. Most of the teas are produced in Korea, Japan, and China. The counter displays a variety of tea leaves so you would know exactly what you are ordering. Japanese desserts based on mochi are also a must-try. In particular, the "chomaemochi," which is tied to a thread, is interesting in that you have to pull both ends of the string to halve the fruit and mochi. The "yakimochi," which comes with a serving of baked mochi and ice cream, is also unforgettably soft and chewy.

Hoshinoa of Suwolgyeonghwa
Address: 1F, 82, Ssangmicheon-ro, Yeonje-gu, Busan
Contact: +82-10-4804-7431
Opening hours: Hours: 11:00 – 19:30 Regular Closed Days: Every Wednesday and Thursday.
Prices: KRW 5,500 for Chomaemochi, KRW 8,000 for house tea (Lilong Lilong), and KRW 7,000 for Matcha Milk
How to get there: Exit 4 of Mulmangol Station on Busan Metro Line 3 → Transfer to Village Bus Yeonje-gu 6 or Yeonje-gu 7 at Mulmangol Station → Get off at Samsung Tower and walk towards the teahouse for 3 minutes
Parking: If you are driving, you can park in front of the cafe

The Romance of Basking Under Clusters of Double-Layered Cherry Blossoms in Mid-Spring
records.originalName: 봄의 한가운데, 겹벚꽃 다발 아래서 즐기는 낭만(한,영,중간,중번,일)
records.description:
By mid-April, the cherry blossoms have fallen and the double-layered cherry blossoms are in full bloom.
The overlapping petals of the double-layered cherry blossoms make them look like a hanging bouquet.
Isn't it romantic to see a naturally formed bouquet?
Why don't you enjoy the romance of feeling like a movie star with the double-layered cherry blossoms at Busan's double-layered cherry blossom spots?
Democracy Park
The park is famous for its double-layered cherry blossoms, which look absolutely stunning when they're in full bloom. The trees are all lined up together to form a tunnel of flowers, which is just breathtaking.

There are so many picnic spots in the park, and it also offers the 'Half-Day Drawing Picnic', where you can rent a picnic cart, coloring paper, art tools, and more. This is a great way to enjoy a picnic while drawing and creating memories.
To make a reservation, just visit the Busan Democracy Park website before 30 and 5 days before your visit in spring and autumn. The picnic deck road in the park is the most famous spot for the double-layered cherry blossoms. You can enjoy a glorious picnic surrounded by the beautiful cherry blossoms and take once-in-a-lifetime photos in your own unique pose. If you have a dog, you can bring it along for a springtime outing.
Democracy Park
Address : 19, Minjugongwon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 3 of Dongdaesin Station on Busan Metro Line 1 → Transfer to Village Bus Jung-gu 1 → Get off at Jungang Park‧Democracy Park and walk for 5 min
Parking : Jungang Park‧Democracy Park Parking Lot
Inquiry : +82-51-790-7400

UN Memorial Cemeter
At the UN Memorial Cemetery, there are double-layered cherry blossom trees in a row. Unlike the Busan Democracy Park, where several trees intertwine to create a beautiful landscape, you can enjoy the sight of each tree bearing its own luscious blossoms. 

The double-layered cherry blossom trees that line the road are perfect for solo photos with the flowers in the background. However, please be sure to enjoy the park in a respectful and quiet manner!
UN Memorial Cemetery
Address : 93, UN Pyeonghwa-ro, Nam-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 1, Daeyeon Station, Busan Metro Line 2 → Bus No. 138 from Daeyeon Station‧Busan Bank Stop  → 8-minute walk from UN Memorial Cemetery ‧Busan Cultural Center Stop 
Parking : UN Memorial Cemetery Parking Lot 
Inquiries : +82-51-625-0625

Daejeo Eco Park
Is Busan Democracy Park too famous to visit? If so, check out Daejeo Eco Park, a hidden gem featuring a stunning tunnel of double-layered cherry blossoms.
Daejeo Eco Park has a short tunnel of double-layered cherry blossoms between the walking paths, making it well worth a visit. Take photos and rent a bike in the park to enjoy the walking trails along the Nakdonggang River!
Daejeo Eco Park
Address : 1-5, Daejeo 1-dong, Gangseo-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 3, Gangseo-gu Office Station, Subway Line 3 → Transfer to Bus 125 at Gangseo-gu Office → Busan Hyewon School, 8-minute walk
Operating Days & Hours : Daily 06:00–21:00
Parking : Daejeo Eco Park Parking Lot
Inquiry : +82-51-971-6011

 Busan Citizens Park North Gate
On the terrace of the ‘Forest Book Cafe,’ located at the North Gate of the Busan Citizens Park, stands a large double-layered cherry blossom tree that blossoms abundantly. The double-flowered cherry blossoms which hang low due to their weight, blending beautifully with the roof of the cafe.

‘The Forest Book Café’ offers a cozy space for reading. Enjoy the romance of spring with a book and a drink of your choice, surrounded by double-layered cherry blossoms.

Busan Citizens Park
Address : 73, Simingongwon-ro, Busanjin-gu, Busan
Directions : Walk for 17 min from Exit 1 of Bujeon Station on Busan Metro Line 1
Parking : Busan Citizens Park Parking Lot (charged)
Inquiry : +82-51-850-6000

records.name: A Tour of No-Fail Vegan Bakeries in Busan, a City of Delicacies
records.description:
Did you know that we consume more animal products than we might think? 
Bread, which is mainly made from grains, also contains animal products such as butter, eggs, cream, and milk.
However, there are many bakeries that sell vegan bread made only with vegan ingredients these days.  
More and more people buy vegan bread because it’s not only delicious and easy to digest, but it can protect the environment and animals as well.
Here are some of the most popular vegan bakeries in Busan that are delicious and environmentally friendly.

Heeso

Vegan rice bread is the signature baked item of the bakery called Heeso, which means “Happy Smile” in Korean. As the name of the bakery suggests, the chewy texture of the bread made only with vegan ingredients will bring smile to your face. In addition to vegan rice bread, their brownies, madeleines, and cookies also also popular. However, because their menu items vary from day-to-day, make sure to check the lineup on Heeso's Instagram (@heeso_vb) before you visit the bakery.

As you will see on their menu, Heeso sells vegan and gluten-free bread, making it a good choice for those who eat vegan food due to health problems such as indigestion.
Looking for breads that are easy to digest? Visit the vegan bakery Heeso!
Heeso
Address : 1F, 16, Jeonpo-daero 186beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan 
Opening Hours : Wed-Mon 11:00 a.m. - 20:00 p.m. 
Holidays : Tuesdays
Transportation Information : Exit 6 of Jeonpo Station on Busan Metro Line 2 → 1-minute by walk
Inquiries : +82-507-1468-4002

 Milhanjum 

Milhanjum is a bakery is run by a master baker who is passionate about vegan bread.
Even before you enter the bakery, you will see that the bakery owner is serious about healthy food. He became known as the “Master of Vegan Bread” since his appearance on the Korean SBS TV show ‘Little Big Masters’, where showed how to make vegan bread while sticking to the basic rules of baking.
Milhanjum is a bakery where you can buy bread you can trust, as it’s free of 10 ingredients: animal ingredients, milk, eggs, butter, white sugar, imported wheat, GMOs, chemical additives, preservatives, and artificial colors.
For the master baker, making bread that is healthy and safe is only the beginning because no matter how healthy it is, no one will eat it if it’s tasteless. So the vegan bread at Milhanjum is safe, healthy, and so scrumptious that you won’t be able to resist the temptation for more.
Want to try something that’s safe and wholesome? Visit Milhanjum for some bread made by a master.
Milhanjum
Address : No.104, 1F, 7, Oncheoncheon-ro 471beon-gil, Dongnae-gu, Busan
Opening Hours : Wednesday through Sunday 10:00~19:30. 
holidays : Mondays and Tuesdays
Transportation Information : Exit 1 of Allak Station on Busan Metro Donghae Line → Transfer to bus 210 or Dongnae-gu 2 at Gangbyeon Tranchae Apt. stop → 3-minute walk from Dongbusan IZoneVil Apt. stop 
Inquiries : +82-51-528-5876

Onhwadang

Onhwadang is a vegan bakery famous for its vegan white bread. It’s so popular that although its opening hours are from 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., all the bread will be either sold out or reserved within just one hour after opening. It’s that delicious.
Besides the bread, Onhwadang also offers a very wide variety of vegan white bread. There are so many different kinds of bread that can match your palate that you might leave the bakery with an arm’s full of bread before you know it.
Onhwadang
Address : No. 116, Residental neighborhood facility, 34, Jungang-daero 1043beon-gil, Yeonje-gu, Busan
Opening Hours : Tuesday through Saturday 11:00~18:00
Holidays : Sundays and Mondays
Transportation Information : Exit 7 of City Hall Station on Busan Metro Line 1 → 5-minute walk 
Inquiries : +82-507-1363-9304

MEAN_DRI

All these cookies, sandwiches, platters, and protein balls are vegan?
MEAN_DRI is a food shop that offers a variety of vegan, organic, and gluten-free bakery items. Thanks to its wide range of baked goods, chances are that you will find something that suits your taste. Before you visit, though, make sure to check their Instagram posts at (@mean_dri) first because their closing days vary.
MEAN_DRI also has a small zero waste shop right next to it. Enjoy environmentally friendly food and accessories while protecting the environment!
MEAN_DRI
Address : 1F, 9, Dongcheon-ro 108beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan (Jeonpo-dong, Gangdong Building)
Opening Hours : Monday through Saturday 11:30 a.m. - 7:00 p.m. / Sundays 11:30 a.m. - 6:00 p.m.

records.name: Unique photos taken in a unique studio for special you
records.description:
Like they say, photos are memories. This shows that most people want to remember a special day for a long time through photos.
You can take pictures in pretty cafes or parks, or even in a photo booth with friends, but it would also be great to leave a unique record of yourself in a conceptual studio at least once.
Below are five unique studios in Busan where you can capture your special portraits on a special day.

Mulbitsaek Studio

Is it true that you can have an underwater photoshoot like a celebrity in Busan too?
Mulbitsaek Studio is Busan’s first underwater photo studio, taking dreamy photos of various concepts such as mermaids and pole dancing, in addition to wedding and maternity photography. The mysterious atmosphere created by the underwater environment is the unique feature of the studio.
In addition to skilled directing, safety and hygiene management is crucial in underwater photography as it is a special type of photography. Mulbitsaek Studio takes the picture of the day underwater by paying great attention to all aspects, including lighting, background, costumes, and waterproof makeup. Customers who are afraid of water are taught to breathe and move naturally in the water. Managing safety and hygiene, including maintaining a warm water temperature and clean water quality, is also a priority. With nice facilities like a waiting room and locker room, it can be considered a high-quality studio you can trust. Even details such as the number of bubbles or the water flow can be adjusted.
There may be some people who are attracted to the mysterious atmosphere that only Mulbitsaek Studio offers but are afraid of underwater photography. In that case, try "aerial photo on water". You can take unique underwater photos that capture the mysterious atmosphere without diving into the water.
Mulbitsaek Studio
Address : 139-28, Cheyukgongwon-ro 6beon-gil, Gangseo-gu, Busan
Opening hours : Every day 09:00 a.m. - 23:00 p.m. 
Fee : 
Aerial shot on the water (Top view): KRW 400,000
SOLO1: 800,000 / SOLO2: KRW 1,000,000
COUPLE1: 1,200,000 / COUPLE2: KRW 1,500,000
Premium Wedding: KRW 2,500,000 
Studio Rental (General Rental, Cosplay): KRW 300,000 for 2 hours/4 people
Studio Rental ({Photographer_Photo Session): Separate inquiry
Website : https://mulbitsaek.co.kr/
Transportation information : Exit 2 of Gangseo-gu Office Station on Busan Metro Line 3 → 6-minute walk from the station/Parking spaces available
Inquiries : +82-507-1393-1179

Nandal 1900

“Did I just travel back to the 1900s?”
Nandal 1900 is a unique studio with five photo spots themed after movies set in the 1900s.
There are five photo spots: ①1930s Independence Activists Photo Spot / ②1950s Ode to My Father Photo Spot / ③1980s Sunny Photo Spot / ④1990s Career Women Photo Spot/ ⑤ 1990s Architecture 101 Photo Spot. Not all retro vibes are the same. What’s even more special is that you can choose a retro background according to your preferences.
The studio has many realistic props that represent each era. The large folding screen reminiscent of the wedding ceremony in the movie Ode to My Father, the nostalgic wooden interior and posters that evoke the 80s atmosphere of the movie Sunny, and the overwhelming photo spots with the theme of independence activists will make you feel like you are in a modern and contemporary history experience center.
In Nandal 1900 you will find many retro outfits for different concepts. Dress in your favorite outfit and take self-portraits acting like you were living in the 1900s. This way you will feel like you are in a retro movie through the photos, which is something you will not find anywhere else.
Nandal 1900
Address : 2F, 8-1, Gwangbok-ro 37beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan
Opening hours : 10:00 a.m. - 22:00p.m.
Fee : 
1. Self-portrait package (for 2 people) – 1 hour: KRW 30,000 / KRW 15,000 for 1 extra person (per an hour)
2. Entire space rental (for 4 people) – 1 hour: KRW 60,000 (at least 2 hours) / KRW 5,000 for 1 extra person

Sarang Obdda

The beauty of Korea!
It may be rare to see people wearing hanboks these days, but hanboks have an elegant beauty of their own. Sarang Obdda is a photo studio where you can take snapshots of the unique beauty of hanbok. There are many hanboks in the studio and you can choose the design and color according to your preference. There is a wide variety of choices, from pastel-colored hanbok to dark-colored, luxurious hanbok. Although it is free of charge, the quality of the hanbok rented from the studio never deteriorates, which makes it more trustworthy.
Sarang Obdda is also has a luxurious and sophisticated interior. The privacy that the studio offers to avoid conflicts with other guests during photo shoots is also noteworthy. For example, you can have your photo taken at a photo spot that matches your hanbok, a garden-themed photo spot, and a folding screen photo spot. The photographer's direction will add details to the hanbok photos.
Both single and group photos are available. You can take your own hanbok profile picture or take pictures with your friends in different poses. Take a carefully choreographed photo like no other in the world in a beautiful hanbok!

Paranmanjang Studio

It is so refreshing!
Should we go star in a Pocari Sweat's commercial right now?
Paranmanjang Studio is a unique photo studio located in Huinnyeoul Culture Village on Yeongdo Island. Photos are taken while sitting on the eaves of a roof. Although there is no photo set, photos with the clear sky and the eaves of Huinnyeoul Culture Village create a unique and refreshing atmosphere.
The highlight of this studio is the photo shooting background. The bright atmosphere, sunlight, and peeling roof of Huinnyeoul Culture Village create a natural beauty that is difficult to replicate in any studio. The editing that brings out the blue tones also maximizes the refreshing atmosphere of the studio. The photo will be even more perfect if you wear pastel color clothing that matches the bright blue color.
You can take more satisfying photos with the various items provided by Paranmanjang Studio. Choose your favorite from a blue paper airplane, a camera, soap bubbles, and flowers, and pose for the camera. You will feel like an actor in a Pocari Sweat commercial.
Panmanjang Studio is a highly recommended place, especially for tourists visiting Huinnyeoul Cultural Village. If you want to cherish the most special moments of your trip in an outdoor studio with a beautiful view of Huinnyeoul Culture Village, be sure to make a reservation before you visit!

We Light

Capture yourself with glowing props!
We Light is a studio where you can take unique photos with the night view of Gwangalli Beach, Haeundae Beach, and Yeongdo Island as a background. With its famously beautiful night view, taking photos in Busan is attractive in itself, but getting high-quality shots taken by a skilled photographer makes it even more valuable. Sometimes you may be disappointed when you try to take a photo of the day with a night view and it doesn't turn out as you expected. In this case, taking pictures of Busan’s fantastic night view with the help of an expert is highly recommended.
We Light's classy light props also add moodiness to nighttime snaps. Create a one-of-a-kind photo using crystal-clear props designed by lighting experts, such as umbrella lights, moon lights, and flower lights. Especially, We Light is the perfect studio for couples taking wedding photography. You can capture the beautiful day with the lights shining against the night view.

records.name: Discover the life of a fisherman in the lush waters of Yeongdo Island
records.description:
It's green everywhere. The bare branches of the trees have turned green and the warm spring sunlight has started to get hot. Yes, it's that time of the year again, the time when you would miss the sea. There are few places where the sea is as varied as in Busan. Haeundae, where shopping, sightseeing and recreation come together; Gwangalli, where neon signs and extravagant nightlife meet; Gijang, which retains the atmosphere of a small fishing village; and Yeongdo, surrounded by the sea on all sides. You'll need a whole week just to explore the sea, which is why Busan is called the city of the sea. Here's how to get the most out of Yeongdo, the island that showcases the pristine beauty of the city's sea.
Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall

Haenyeo fishing is a unique and rare maritime culture in the world. The haenyeo fishing industry began in 1887 when the first Jeju haenyeo arrived in Yeongdo, an island in Busan. At that time, Busan was a golden fishing ground for agar and seaweed, and the market for these products flourished, making it a base for haenyeo who left Jeju for the mainland.

Later, in the early to mid-1970s, many haenyeo from Jeju moved to Busan in response to their husbands' jobs, and the haenyeo culture settled in Yeongdo. With the rise of the export industry during the industrialization period, husbands were away from home for long periods of time, and the haenyeo worked in Yeongdo as breadwinners and heads of households. This background has led to the opening of the Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall and the erection of a haenyeo statue. The Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall provides a vivid insight into the history of the fishing industry and the life of the haenyeo in Yeongdo. 

Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall
Address : 2-36, Jungninam-ro, Yeongdo-gu, Busan
Opening hours : Tuesday – Sunday 09:00~18:00
Holidays : Every Monday
Transportation information : Exit 8, Nampo Station, Busan Subway Line 1 -> Transfer to Bus No. 508, 71, 7, or 5 at Yeongdodaegyo·Nampo Station → Get off at Namgogyo Station, 7-minute walk
Parking : Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall Public Parking Lot
Inquiry : +82-51-419-4505

Yeongdo Haenyeochon

Haenyeochon is located on the first floor of Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall. Seventeen Yeongdo haenyeos spend six hours every day, from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., scouring the waters for seafood to serve immediately. From sea pineapple, turban shells and sea cucumber to abalone and octopus, the seafood is fresh from the waters off Yeongdo. The instant noodles with octopus and other seafood are also not to be missed. With the crashing waves of the Yeongdo Sea as a backdrop, you can't ask for much more than a slice of seafood and a chilled glass of soju. If you visit in the evening at sunset, you'll be in for an emotional experience and probably cry out for another bottle.

Another characteristic of Yeongdo Haenyeochon is the gimbap served with the seafood. In addition to the haenyeo, there is also a couple who owns a gimbap shop, and thanks to the TV show, the image of a plate of seafood and gimbap has become a trademark that comes to mind when you think of Jungni Haenyeochon. Even now, when you visit the place, you can experience the unique taste of gimbap and seafood together.

Yeongdo Haenyeochon
Address : 1F, Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall, 2-35, Jungninam-ro, Yeongdo-gu, Busan 
Opening hours  : Monday - Sunday 09:00~18:00
Transportation information : Exit 8, Nampo Station, Busan Subway Line 1 → Transfer to Bus No. 508, 71, 7, or 6 at Yeongdodaegyo·Nampo Station → Get off at Namgogyo Station, 7-minute walk 
Parking : Yeongdo Haenyeo Culture Exhibition Hall Public Parking Lot

Yeongdo Sea Fishing Site

Now that you're in Busan, why not try your hand at fishing? The Yeongdo Sea Fishing Site in Ha-ri, Dongsam-dong, Yeongdo-gu, makes it easy for beginners to enjoy fishing. It costs KRW 20,000 per person and you can also rent a fishing rod for KRW 5,000. Bring your own bait and board a boat that departs every hour from 5 a.m. and drops you off at the sea fishing spot, which is two to three minutes away from the marina.

This raft-like sea fishing site is actually quite large, despite what it looks like from a distance. The spacious yard is well equipped with shade, dining tables, toilets and other amenities, and you can even cook your own meals. In between casting your line into the sea and waiting for your catch, take time to explore the surrounding seascape. The contrast between the quiet fishing village and the towering apartment buildings is strange. The rock formations along the shore are a wonder to behold. Fishing is fishing, but it's also great fun to see the island from the water.

Yeongdo Sea Fishing Site

records.name: Immerse yourself in the rich, warm tone of LP Music at LP bars and cafes
records.description:
With winter approaching, don’t’ miss the calming emotions that only this only this season can bring.
Why not enjoy the warm tones of an LP record that will soothe your body and mind in the chilly weather?
Spend a special moment immersed in music and atmosphere at LP bars and cafes in Busan, brimming with analog charm.
Muse On Haeundae

Isn't the atmosphere of a place just as important as the songs? 
Muse On Haeundae is an LP bar with an antique vibe that will touch your heart.

As soon as you enter the bar, you'll notice that the interior is filled with records, speakers and other music equipment. It's not just decorative, it's real working equipment. Muse On Haeundae has over 10,000 vinyl records, so you could say it's an LP bar that takes music seriously. There are sheets of paper on every table so you can write down the songs you want to hear and ask them to play them for you. Some of the LPs are available for sale, so it's the perfect place for LP music lovers.

The furniture, lighting and props are also decorated with high quality dark wood to match the store's classic atmosphere. This beautifully decorated bar with a cool vibe is also the location for some celebrity photo shoots such as singer Suji, model Joo Woo-jae and Korean drama Cheese In The Trap.

Seating in the shop ranges from tables for large groups to single seats at the bar for any number of people. The window seats are particularly popular as you can open the windows and feel like you're enjoying a drink outside.

There's plenty of food and drink to tempt your palate, including wine, whiskey, cocktails, highballs and snacks. 
With staff on hand to help with bottle openings and tastings, this is also a great place for first-time drinkers.

MuseOnHaeundae
Address : 2F, 39, Jungdong 1-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Opening hours : Daily 18:00~02:00
Homepage : https://www.instagram.com/museon_haeundae
Directions : Exit 1, Haeundae Station, Busan Metro Line 2 →7-minute walk (No parking)
Inquiries : +82-507-1404-4549

Mangmi Blues

If you’re a retro-obsessed hipster, Mangmi Blues is the place to be!

Retro music posters line the walls from the entrance to the inside of the bar. In keeping with the hip vibe of the posters, the layout and decor are nostalgic. Bookshelves filled with vinyl records and the LP DJ area add to the romantic atmosphere.
At Mangmi Blues, the DJ spins music directly from vinyl, without any digital sources. As the DJ spins his own selection of vinyl records, song requests are not accepted. You can just sit back, relax and immerse yourself in the analog world of the DJ's recommendations.

Mangmi Blues has a long bar table, two-to-three-seater tables and window seats. The bar table is great for solo drinkers, while the window seats are perfect for a nightcap with a view of the alleyways lined with the bars. 

The variety of highballs and food is also impressive. In particular, the basic anju (food consumed with alcohol) is served in sufficient quantities, so if you are unsure what to eat with your drinks, just try the basic accompaniments first before deciding what to order. 

MangMiBlues

Listen Page

If you're in the mood for some warmth, head to Listen Page, a café where you can warm up to the sounds of vinyl music.

Listen Page has a quiet exterior with a mysterious sign. Known for its great atmosphere, the cafe is said to be sometimes crowded with many customers. While Muse On Haeundae has a heavy and dark antique interior, Listen Page has a warm and soft antique feel. The accessories, such as the wall clock, bookshelves and speakers, are also made of light wood to match the tone and manners.
There are a variety of seating options here, from group to solo seats. Due to the unusual layout of the room, there are also seats inside the arched door. You can choose depending on whether you're in a group or not, or what kind of atmosphere you're looking for.

Their signature drinks include chestnut latte, almond cream latte and wormwood latte. With your drink, you'll also receive a postcard with a heartwarming message. Drinks are served on a wooden tray, which adds to the warmth of the atmosphere.

Listen Page has its own adorable mascot: a cat named Bami. You’ll notice Bami’s presence everythere, from the glasses you're served in to the menu. Bami merchandise is also available for purchase, and you can even ttake home a free Bami-themed sticker. If you're a cat lover, this spot is a must-visit. While you’re seated, Bami might come up to your table and meow at you. However, please avoid from pulling her toward you or touching her, as it may cause her stress.

There's always a soothing soundtrack playing in the LP Café. Staying true to the cafe's heartfelt concept, there's even a space dedicated to sharing your own playlists. Customers can leave post-it notes with their favorite tracks, creating a vibrant display of shared musical worlds. If you have a song in mind, you can ask the staff to play it for you.

Since Listen Page is a cafe that is open until midnight, it is a good place to go when you suddenly feel the need for LP music and a warm atmosphere.
Listen Page stays open until the late hours of midnight, making it a perfect spot if you suddenly crave vinyl music and a cozy atmosphere on a rainy night. If you're not much of a drinker but still want to stay up late and enjoy the vinyl experience, this is the place for you.
ListenPage

Closed days : Every Sunday

 alt.comma 

LP bars are more about the atmosphere than the food? 
Come to alt.comma, a place where the atmosphere, food and drinks are all great. It will be a whole new experience.

alt.comma is a whiskey bar dedicated to vinyl music, with a wall of bookshelves lined with records and beautifully displayed bottles of whiskey. It's a perfect setting without any special props, but what makes it stand out is the attention to detail. There's a sign on the table that says: "We have power banks, lap blankets, cushions and slippers available, please ask our staff if you need them.” It's a nice touch to make sure guests are comfortable and can enjoy every element of the space.
A whiskey bar can be intimidating, so alt.comma offers whiskey recommendations and friendly explanations to help newcomers navigate the bar. They also offer a sparkling water before switching to another whiskey, so you can concentrate on the flavor as much as possible. There are also plenty of light bites to pair with the whiskey, so enjoy!
The whiskey is excellent, as is the menu, which includes grilled octopus. The menu, both food and drink, is all QR coded and you can find detailed descriptions, photos and even reviews of the menu to help you decide what to try.

As a vinyl bar, you can also enjoy great music here. However, they don't take song requests so they can concentrate on bartending and serving customers. Think of it as a place where you can enjoy whiskey and good food with vinyl music.

Due to the small size of the bar, it would be considerate to keep your table for a maximum of two and a half hours to allow as many guests as possible to enjoy the space. Dogs are welcome, subject to pet etiquette. Bring your pooch along for a heartfelt experience on a rainy day.

alt.comma

Jeollamhoe

A cup of coffee by day, a glass of wine by night! 
Jeollamhoe is a charming LP café and bar, open day and night.

Jeollamhoe aims for a quiet atmosphere and does not accept groups of more than four. Although the room itself is small, there are not many tables and the center of the bar is empty, creating a great openness. Water, tissues and chargers are available from the self-service bar. As a vinyl bar, there are LPs and turntables, giving the place a unique atmosphere.
The uniqueness of the Jeollamhoe lies in the QR-coded menu presented between the poetry books. There's something romantic about selecting a menu and then randomly flipping through the poetry book. You can feel your parched sensibility being replenished as you begin to enjoy the space.

Scan the QR-coded menu to see what Jeollamhoe has to offer. There's one part of the menu that really shows the uniqueness of the place: the menu names. The titles of songs from the first three albums by Korean musical duo 'Exhibition' are all incorporated into the menu names of the hand-drip coffees.
The signature item on the coffee menu is the Café Royal, which is served with a spoonful of a sugar cube on top of hot coffee, which is then set on fire and stirred into the coffee when it’s melted. It's a unique experience, and it's a great way to turn heads, so try it if you're an extrovert at heart.

At night it becomes a music bar. During the day it plays vinyl music only and song requests are not accepted. At night, however, it plays music with video, so you can request two songs per table. The requested music is accompanied by videos, making the experience even more enjoyable.

You can bring in outside food for a fee and enjoy the space. It costs 5,000 won per table, and you'll be provided with plates and cutlery to help you enjoy your food. It's a great option if you have food and alcohol ready, but not the space to enjoy it.

records.name: Escape the last of the summer heat in the cool, refreshing valleys right here in the city!
records.description:
Summer is almost over. Want to escape the heat but don’t have time for a long trip? Explore these cool hidden valleys in the heart of Busan for one last summer refreshment.
Banyeo Chorok Park & Jangsan Valley

Spend the rest of your summer cooling off at Banyeo Chorok Park & Jangsan Valley, where kids can play with nature!

Banyeo Chorok Park is especially popular with families, offering a variety of facilities at the Banyeo Recreational Green Space, including a picnic area, a net playground, and a barefoot loess path. Both children and adults can enjoy interacting with nature. To access these facilities and the valley, you'll have to climb a fairly steep path, making it a great place for both fun and a healthy exercise.

The main attraction here is the 43-meter long roller slide, the longest in Busan, offering an exhilarating experience for children. Safety rules are clearly posted, so as long as you follow them, you can enjoy the ride safely. At the end of the slide, you'll find a net playground where toddlers can swing and play, as well as hammocks and wooden chairs for adults to relax in.

Right next to the Recreational Green Space is a shallow stream that's great for wading and playing in, and full of small fish that children will love to catch.
Banyeo Chorok Park & Jangsan Valley
Address : San 111-2, Banyeo-dong, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 1, Busan Wondong Station, Busan-Donghae Line → Bus No. 44, 52 or 144 from Busan Wondong Station → 10-minute walk from Ilshin Bus Final Station
Parking : Banyeo Library Public Parking Lot
Inquiries : +82-51-749-4000 (Haeundae-gu Office)

(Formerly) Daeshin Park Daeshin Valley

Experience the rejuvenating power of nature at Jungang Park (formerly Daeshin Park) and Daeshin Valley—a tranquil inner-city oasis filled with refreshing phytoncides to revitalize your spirit! 

The former Daeshin Park is conveniently located near Dong-A University Hospital and is easily accessible. The park's main attraction is its cypress forest, where you can enjoy the fresh air immediately upon arrival. Well-maintained walking paths wind through the forest, making it easy for visitors to take a leisurely walk. The park also offers various amenities for both residents and tourists, including a flat area for jogging and playing badminton, resting benches, a mineral spring, and basic exercise equipment.

It used to supply drinking water to the Busan area. There are two water sources in Daeshin Park. The first, located near the cypress forest and Daeshin Valley, has been turned into a lake where you can see carp, soft-shelled turtles, and other creatures.

Nestled near a cypress forest, Daeshin Valley offers shallow water that reaches a child's knees, making it perfect for splashing around and cooling off. The valley is teeming with small fish and marsh snails that children can collect and play with, offering a wonderful opportunity for children to connect with nature in a way they may not often experience.
(Formerly) Daeshin Park Daeshin Valley
Address : 59, Bosu-daero 320beon-gil, Seo-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 4, Seodaeshin Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. Seo-gu 5 at Seodaeshin Station → 8-minute walk from Dong-a University Hospital Station
Parking : Daeshin Park Public Parking Lot (charged) 
Inquiries : +82-51-240-4000 (Seo-gu Office)

Gudeok Camping Site Valley

Discover a hidden gem known only to Busan locals! Take the kids to a peaceful valley near Gudeok Camping Site for a relaxing getaway.

Gudeok Camping Site is located next to the former Daeshin Park. If you follow the walking trail that starts at Daeshin Park, you'll discover a beautiful natural area. The most notable nearby attraction is Naewonjeongsa Temple, which is famous for its temple stay program and is the largest temple near the city center. It's a fantastic place to explore and connect with nature.

Since this area supplies drinking water, you’ll notice several large water sources. Near Gudeok, you'll find the 'second water source,' where you can see carp and other aquatic life, as well as a fountain that operates at different times throughout the day. There is also a sports field near the campsite where you can enjoy a quick game of football.

The stream that runs around the campsite is shallow enough for children to splash around in, making it a great place to cool off with a dip in the summer.
Gudeok Camping Site Valley
Address : Gudeok Youth Training Center, 109, Kkonmaeul-ro 156beon-gil, Seo-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 4, Seodaeshin Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. Seo-gu 1 at Seodaeshin Station → 7-minute walk from Gudeok Kkonmaeul Station
Parking : Gudeok Kkonmaeul Public Parking Lot
Inquiries : +82-51-246-4685 (Gudeok Camping Site)

Beomeosa Yongseong Valley

Do you know Yosan Kim Jeonghan, a key figure in Busan's literary history? The reservoir depicted in Yosan's work Sahachon is actually Beomeosa Yongseong Dam. So Yongseong Dam is not only a reservoir in the heart of the city, but also a place of literary significance.

Yongseong Valley has a stream that flows from Yongseong Dam, creating a stunning waterfall that is sure to refresh your mind. However, as shown in the photo, the water upstream from the dam is very powerful, making it unsafe to enter the waterfall.

Consider exploring the valley, where the water is only knee-deep, making it safe for young children to play. The area is also home to many small fish, making it an excellent place to learn about ecology. Nearby, you’ll find a walking trail called Nuri-gil and a rest area, perfect for combining water play with a leisurely walk.

Beomeosa Yongseong Valley
Address : 267, Beomeosa-ro, Geumjeong-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 5, Nopo Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 90 at Beomeosa Ipgu Station → 2-minute walk from Beomeosa Parking Lot Station 
Parking : Beomeosa Public Parking Lot
Inquiries : +82-51-519-4000 (Geumjeong-gu Office)

We've uncovered some of the best hidden valleys in the heart of Busan. While you're free to immerse yourself in nature, please remember to release any fish you catch to help protect the environment.

records.name: The Incomparable 9 Record-Breaking Destinations in Busan
I Booked a Train Ticket to Get Here
Autumn in Busan: A Season for Foliage and Camping
records.description:
Autumn, a season that feels even more precious because there's so little time to enjoy it.
To help you make the most of this precious autumn season, Visit Busan presents four destinations where you can experience the essence of autumn.
Embrace the season of foliage and camping with our carefully selected recommendations for Busan’s top attractions.
Woody Brook 
Street cats in harmony with the autumn landscape

Come enjoy the fall colors and say hello to the cats at Woody Brook, a big forest café in Hakjang-dong, Sasang-gu, Busan. You can relax and enjoy the beauty of nature here!
The space has a different appeal each season: cherry blossoms in spring, lush forests in summer, and colored leaves in fall. 
Woody Brook is spacious, with two floors, a rooftop, and an outdoor garden. It’s a magical café where you can hear the sound of the valley water and admire the well-maintained garden.
Inside, the big windows let in lots of sunlight and make you feel like you’re right in the middle of nature. Another great attraction is the mountain view, which offers a unique opportunity to experience the changing seasons. 
Just a quick note: It’s a no-kids zone, so only high school students and above are allowed. Also, it’s a no-pets zone, so pets aren’t allowed, either.

Outside, you’ll find some adorable stray cats. It’s like a cat’s paradise, and you’ll be able to enjoy some peaceful moments, making eye contact with these cute furry friends.
Please note that you can stay in the café for up to three hours. 

Woody Brook
Address : 2, Hakgam-daero, Sasang-gu, Busan
Directions : A 1-minute walk from Exit 2, Jurye Station, Busan Metro Line 2 -> Bus No. Busan Jin-gu 10-1 from Jurye Station Bus Stop -> Get off at Guhak Elementary School Bus Stop -> An 8-minute walk
Parking : Available
Opening hours : Tuesday–Friday 11:00–19:00 / Saturday–Sunday 11:00–21:00 
Closed days : Every Monday
Website : Shortcut
Inquiries : +82-507-1306-2593

DOMOHEON 
A great place to better yourself in autumn months

DOMOHEON is a space that connects Busan’s past and future in a special way. The former Busan Mayor’s Residence has been remodeled into an open space for the public for walking, relaxation, and intellectual exchange.

The building has a lounge, a lecture hall, a meeting room, a multi-purpose space, a conference room, a shared office, and a children’s space named Deullak Nallak. The idea is to facilitate access to cultural programs and collaborations between local artists and entrepreneurs. 
In addition to the wonderful facilities, there are also high-quality programs. Check out the website for more information on the programs!

Outside the DONOHEON building, you’ll find Sosopung Garden stretched wide and trails. The Sosopung Garden is a public garden created by a public institution, so it’s open for citizens to visit and enjoy a picnic. In autumn, you can enjoy the refreshing breeze and the rustling of leaves in the Sosopung garden. A simple picnic in this idyllic setting comes highly recommended.

The first floor of DOMOHEON is home to the Domoheon Branch of Momos Coffee, Busan’s top coffee brand. After you’ve had a picnic or attended a program at DOMOHEON, you can relax and enjoy coffee and sweets here. 
Visit DOMOHEON, a place where you can relax, connect, and brainstorm new ideas to shape Busan’s future together!

Camping BBQ Clouds
 The perfect setting for a sunny autumn day of camping and relaxation

Longing for the camping vibe but not up for a full outdoor adventure? Head to the Camping BBQ Clouds for a barbecue party!
Camping BBQ Clouds is located in Jeonggwan-eup, Gijang-gun, Busan. Camping tents are arranged in a "ㄷ" shape on a spacious artificial grass field. For families with children or dogs, it's a safe place where you can watch them play on the grass from the tents.

Right next to the tents is a canteen stocked with everything from meat and alcohol to instant noodles, sweets, and more. One of the best features of the canteen is the 'self-bar', where you can help yourself to simple side dishes, vegetables, and sauces to pair with your meat. It's the best of both worlds: the camping vibe with the convenience of a meat restaurant. Each tent is fully equipped with air conditioning, ventilation, and seating for up to eight people, allowing you to enjoy the barbecue in comfort.
The roof is also beautifully decorated with picnic chairs and a simple shade, creating a perfect spot to unwind after your meal. Enjoy a romantic break on the rooftop, relaxing in a picnic chair and taking in the view.

records.description:
If you're looking to combine a café tour with a gallery tour, we've got you covered.
Take a tour of Busan's 'gallery cafes' where you can enjoy art and coffee at the same time.
Casa De Lux 

Introducing Casa De Luk, Busan's first immersive media art gallery cafe! The street lamps and antique chairs, along with pictures of famous works by Van Gogh and the Mona Lisa, will make you feel like you're strolling down an art street in a foreign country! The perfect spot for a photo, right?

The famous "Starry Night", a painting everyone has seen at least once, stretches across the screen, while in another, "Cafe Terrace at Night" comes to life, giving you a taste of what media art is all about.
The all-black, modern and simple interior evokes the feeling of being in the South of France, where Van Gogh worked at the height of his career.
The walls are lined with various works by Van Gogh, making you feel like you're in an art museum. You can enjoy coffee and dessert while you admire the artwork. In other words, it's a feast for both the eyes and the palate.

The artwork on display changes regularly, so it's always fun to come back and see what's new. Be sure to check out their Instagram to see what's on before you visit.
If you're looking for a unique experience and atmosphere while enjoying your coffee, or if you want to capture the best photos of your life, Casa De Lux is the place to be. The entire café is a photo zone, with artwork and museum lighting!

Café Dottori Roasters

Driving, coffee and bakery treats, vibrant artwork - what if you could enjoy all this in one place?
Check out Cafe Tottori Roasters, a spacious cafe in Gijang-gun that is much more than just a gallery cafe!
Gijang-gun, located a bit away from the city center, offers the beauty of nature with its panoramic ocean views and lush green trees around. As you drive through and take in the scenery, you’ll arrive at the cafe before you know it.

Built in the shape of a "D," Cafe Dottori Roasters boasts a unique architectural style and welcomes visitors with an array of stone sculptures at the entrance.
Inside, there’s plenty to captivate the eye. The spacious café features works by world-renowned artists such as Paik Nam-june, Shin Sang-ho, Robert Combas, and David Gerstein, displayed across multiple floors. 
Not only will you find paintings on the walls, but also three-dimensional pieces, giving the space a gallery-like fee. You can admire the colorful artwork while enjoying a variety of baked goods and coffee to suit your taste.

If you’re looking to stroll the outdoor patio overlooking the woods surrounding the cafe while admiring the artwork, Café Dottori Roasters is the place to be! 
With group seating and private spaces, it offers something for everyone – whether you’re visiting with family, friends, or a significant other.

Check out M543 Cafe. Gallery, a spacious gallery café in Mandeok-dong where art and relaxation come together.
More than just a coffee shop, it's a unique space where everyday life meets art. The gallery frequently hosts solo exhibitions, with new works on display each month.
You can experience the art up close, free of charge, through a variety of exhibitions, ensuring inspiration with every visit.

Inside, each section offers a distinctive atmosphere. The gallery is tranquil, while the floor-to-ceiling window side feels lively and open. From the outside, the café's elevated position and large windows provide stunning mountain views. There’s spacious parking area on the first floor, a café and gallery on the second, and a rooftop terrace on the third. On clear days, you can enjoy a cup of coffee with mountain views from the rooftop. In the evening, the space is beautifully illuminated, creating an even more special atmosphere. With Geumjeongsan Mountain behind you and the scenic Mandeok-daero boulevard and Sinmandeok area in front, it’s an ideal spot for a date.

The restaurant also offers signature drinks and a variety of desserts, with snacks and drinks available for children and families. records.name: Busan’s Ultimate Workation Spots♫
Busan On Films : Explore the hidden spots in K-dramas.
Dark Tourism: Walking Through the Fragments of Busan’s Memory
records.description:
At a dark tourism destination tracing Busan's modern and contemporary history, you'll uncover memories and relive history. 
Amid the scars of war, we learn lessons and honor a past that must never be forgotten.

Ilgwang Mining Village

Visit ‘Ilgwang Mining Village,’ a site with a history of forced labor.

Ilgwang Mining Village carries the painful legacy of forced labor during the Japanese colonial period. The scars of this history remain visible today. In the 1930s, Japan's Sumitomo Metal Mining Co, Ltd. developed the Nikko Mine (Ilgwang Mine) to exploit Korea’s copper resources. Mining operations began in 1937, and the mine became one of the country’s top five copper producers. Starting in 1944, many Koreans were forcibly mobilized to work in copper mining and subjected to military training. The working conditions were extremely harsh, leading to immense suffering. As a result, Ilgwang Mining Village gained notoriety as a ‘hellhole workplace.’

At the entrance to the mine, you can still see remnants of the Japanese occupation, including the ruins of Japanese-style offices and houses once used by executives. Structures like laundries, wells, and communal toilets reflect the harsh conditions endured by forced laborers and offer a glimpse into their daily lives. 
Although the village has declined over time following the mine’s closure, it retains much of its original character, providing insight into how our ancestors lived during the Japanese occupation.

Beyond its historical significance, the site is also a picturesque agricultural complex, adorned with pink muhly and silver grass that create a stunning view in every season. Experience the echoes of your ancestors’ footsteps in this mining town where history and nature intertwine.
Ilgwang Mining Village
Address : 663-7, Won-ri, Ilgwang-eup, Gijang-gun, Busan
Direction : Exit 7, Gijang Station, Busan Metro Donghae Line→Bus No. 182 from Gijang Market Station→Get off at Jwacheon Elementary School Station →4-minute walk→Bus No. 8-1 from Gijang-gun 8-1 from Jwacheon Elementary School Station→Mining Village Entrance Station→8-minute walk 
Parking : Available – No designated parking space, parking along the road is possible
Inquiries : +82-51-709-4000

Busan Port Pier 1

From the painful history of displaced people to the economic development of Busan, 'Busan Port Pier 1' symbolizes the beginning of reconstruction.

Busan Port Pier 1 has been a vital trade center since the Joseon Dynasty. Opened in 1876 under the Ganghwa Treaty, it gained historical significance alongside the development of Busan Port. During the Japanese colonial period, the completion of Pier 1 and the opening of the Gyeongbu Line Railway transformed it into a base for Japan's continental invasion and a hub for transporting military supplies.

During the Korean War, Pier 1 served as a vital passageway for evacuees, UN troops, and relief supplies. It became a symbol of hope for evacuees and a starting point for Busan’s rebuilding efforts. Additionally, it holds historical significance as a site for the transfer of North Korean and UN prisoners of war.

Today, Pier 1 is much more than a logistics port – it serves as a major hub for Korea's economic growth and a key link to the Busan New Port. The site, where the pain and hope of the past coexist, is gaining recognition as a cultural heritage site and is being considered for UNESCO listing. The large warehouses at Pier 1 also host international cultural events, such as the Busan International Photo Festival, enhancing its value as a space where tourism and culture converge.

Busan Port Pier 1 stands as a symbol of hope and reconstruction, shaping the city’s identity and development. Visit this historic site to experience its enduring legacy and reflect on its profound historical significance.
Busan Port Pier No. 1
