Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Annex

The area around Jung-gu, Busan, where the Gukje Market, the Bosu Book Alley, and the Provisional Capital Memorial Hall are located, is a living history textbook that fully embraces Busan's modern and contemporary history. In particular, the Busan Modern History Museum, which was used as the Mokpo Branch of the Oriental Development Company during the Japanese colonial period, is a symbolic space of Busan's modern and contemporary history and is the center of Busan's historical excursions.
So let's go to the annex of the Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum, which has been transformed into a cultural complex.

The Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Annex is a revitalized historical space that tells the story of its journey from construction to the present. Originally built in 1929 as the Busan branch of the Dongyang Chucksik Corporation during the Japanese occupation, it began as the former Busan Modern History Museum. This Western-style building, featuring elements of early modernist architecture, was a hub for exploiting Busan's land, sea, and resources until Korea' liberation. After liberation, it served as accommodation for American troops.

Since the establishment of the Korean government, it has been used as the U.S. Cultural Center and suffered an arson incident during the democratization movement in the 1980s, becoming a living witness of Busan's modern and contemporary history. After the building was returned to citizens in 1999, it was reborn as the Busan Modern History Museum. And in 2023, it was transformed into a resting place for citizens and a cultural complex.

When you go up to the 'Daecheongmaru' on the 2nd floor, you will first encounter a small exhibition space that tells the history and structure of this building. A unique feature is the exposed ceiling which reveals the structure of the building can. You can see that three methods—reinforced concrete structures, steel frame structures, and steel frame reinforced concrete structures—were used in combination according to the technical and periodic conditions at the time of new construction.

The Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Annex is a cultural complex that combines various functions such as a library, archives, museum, and resting place. You can stop by and cool off while walking down the street. It is a good place to meet someone and sit by a sunny window and read books leisurely. It can also be used as a place of learning. People of all ages can enjoy the space the way they want.
Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum Annex

Busan Citizens Park History Museum

The Busan Citizen Park History Museum showcases the 100-year history of Busan Citizens Park through exhibits and videos. With a variety of exhibitions and programs, visitors can explore Busan's poignant modern history and experience a journey back in time.

The museum is divided into the Space of Memory and four exhibition halls. Explore the history of Busan in each hall and immerse yourself in the city’s past.

Space of Memory
 The Space of Memory, a reinforced concrete building constructed in 1949, once served as a dining and banquet hall for the U.S. military officers. The markings and stars of the U.S. 8th Army on the ceiling vividly capture the atmosphere of that era. Today, it houses exhibition videos that explore the historical background of Busan Citizens Park.

Exhibition 1
 Exhibition 1 highlights the transformation of farmland in Beomjeon-ri and Yeonji-ri, Busan, which was occupied by the Japanese during the Japanese colonial period. The Beomjeon-dong area was initially operated as a Seomyeon Racetrack for entertainment and military horse training, later becoming a Japanese military base and temporary training center. This exhibition offers insights into the area’s transformation and its historical significance. 

Exhibition 2
 Exhibition 2 focuses on the entry of U.S. forces into the Korean Peninsula after World War II and and the history of Camp Hialeah, which served as the Busan Base Command. Visitors can explore Camp Hialeah’s role as a military supply base through artifacts and models.

Exhibition 3
 Exhibition 3 illustrates how a village south of Camp Hialeah was transformed by the presence of the U.S. military. It showcases the development of the town’s commercial district through its coexistence with the US military and provides a glimpse into the lives of residents during the boom years through detailed models. 

Exhibition 4
 Exhibition 4 explores the efforts of civic groups to reclaim the Camp Hialeah site and transform it into Busan Citizens Park. Through panels, videos, and interactive activities, visitors can learn about the actions taken to make this vision a reality.
Busan Citizens Park History Museum

United Nations Peace Memorial

Visit the United Nations Peace Memorial to delve deeper into the history of the Korean War.

The United Nations Peace Memorial explores a wide range of topics, including the causes and progression of the Korean War, the stories of the UN troops who fought in the conflict, and the United Nations’ vision today. It holds significant historical value, offering visitors a chance to reflect on the contributions of 26 allied countries and the veterans who worked for peace on the Korean Peninsula. Located in Busan, the memorial also features a section dedicated to the city’s role and significance as the ‘war capital.’

The first floor features exhibits detailing the unfolding of the Korean War, along with rooms showcasing preserved military items from the era. It offers a meaningful opportunity to reflect on the events of that time.

The exhibits on the second floor focus on the UN's role in the war and the remembrance of UN veterans. Items used by UN troops during the war are on display, offering visitors a chance to connect with and honor the veterans' legacy.
The magic art on the walls and floors, along with the Sibal car and the Retona - a real military vehicle model in the hallway - are particularly noteworthy, making history more engaging and accessible, especially for children.

The second floor also features the UN Kids Zone, where children can play with toys and read books, ensuring they stay entertained during their visit.

In addition, the museum features detailed exhibits on the meaning and significance of the UN, its current vision, and the role of UNICEF. Visitors can also explore the Peace Message Zone, where they can leave messages of gratitude to the veterans.

The United Nations Peace Memorial is located just a short distance from the UN Memorial Cemetery, making it easy to visit both. After exploring the exhibits at the United Nations Peace Memorial, take a moment to pay your respects to the fallen at the UN Memorial Cemetery. 
United Nations Peace Memorial

UN Memorial Cemetery in Korea (UNMCK)

Visit the UN Memorial Cemetery, a tribute to those who sacrificed their lives in the Korean War and a symbol of hope and peace. Every June, during Korea's Patriots and Veterans Month, flowers bloom here as a symbol of peace a call to end war. These flowers serve as a tribute to the fallen soldiers of the Korean War and a reminder of their sacrifice.
At first, 11,000 graves of the fallen soldiers and war veterans from 21 participating countries in the Korean War were located in this cemetery. However, after the remains of identified people returned to their home countries, there are 2,300 graves from 11 countries including Turkey and the UK.
The United Nations Command (UNC) first created the cemetery to bury the fallen. Later, remains which had been buried temporarily across the country were moved here. The Republic of Korea donated the cemetery to the United Nations in return for the sacrifices of the UN troops who had died far from their home countries.

In the middle of the cemetery is the UN Forces Memorial, with doves carved onto it. The Wall of Remembrance, completed in 2006, has the names of the United Nations casualties (killed and missing) inscribed on marble panels. A tribute to each of the inscribed names was paid, wishing the noble lives of the young men could rest in peace.

The Unknown Soldier’s Pathway, which leads to the UN Memorial Cemetery in Korea, makes visitors feel grateful for their courage and sacrifice. The words inscribed onto the Monumental Tower for Honoring UN Participation in the Korean War convey our appreciation to them.
“Dedicated to the heroic, brave soldiers who sacrificed their lives during the Korean War for world peace and freedom in this country far from their homes.”

UN Memorial Cemetery in Korea (UNMCK)

records.name: Ecotourism with Migratory Birds Under the Autumn Sky
records.description:
Fill your heart with a healing journey to Busan's natural beauty under the clear skies, and enjoy an autumn ecological tour with beautiful migratory birds.
Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory

Visit the Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory, a hidden gem in the Nakdonggang estuary. 
This is a prime birding site where around 150 species of migratory birds come to winter every year, offering a chance to witness the changing seasons alongside a variety of bird species.
From the observatory, you can observe migratory birds feeding on the mudflats up close, with spectacular winter displays by mallards, whooper swans, Saunders’s gulls, and other winter migrants.

Telescopes are available free of charge at the viewing platform, allowing you to get a closer look at the migratory birds. Signs along the path feature photos and descriptions of the birds to enrich your birdwatching experience. This spot is also popular with children, offering a chance to learn about migratory birds and aquatic plants up close. Remember to keep a respectful distance, as the birds can be startled if you get too close!

The Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory is also renowned for its stunning sunset views and attracts crowds on weekends, offering spectacular views of golden mudflats and migratory birds. It connects to the Ocean City Galmatgil Trails, making it a great place for a relaxing stroll. For a quieter experience immersed in nature, theobservatory is a great place to create lasting memories.
Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory
Address : 284, Myeongji ocean city 1-ro, Gangseo-gu, Busan
Direction : 1-minute walk from Exit 5, Hadan Station, Busan Metro Line 1→ Bus No. 171 from Hadan Station Transfer Center→Get off at Myeongji Migratory Bird Observatory Station →2-minute walk
Parking : Available
Inquiries : +82-51-970-4000

Nakdong Estuary Eco Center

Eulsukdo Island is where the main stem of the Nakdonggang River meets the seawater of the South Sea, creating an ecological haven rich in fertile soil and freshwater fish, and shellfish. It also serves as a large winter home for migratory birds in search of abundant food. Let’s explore Eulsukdo Island, one of Busan’s most beautiful islands.
As its name suggests - meaning “clean island with birds” – Eulsukdo Island is widely recognized as Korea’s premier bird sanctuary. In the 1950s, it was even considered Asia’s largest habitat for migratory birds.
The Nakdong Estuary Eco Center, located on Eulsukdo Island, was renovated and opened in May 2024 under the theme ‘Eulsukdo Zoom-in.’ Visitors can now enjoy a more interactive experience of Eulsukdo Island's beautiful four seasons and diverse wildlife, including migratory birds, through educational programs and exhibitions.

The center features a variety of rooms designed to provide an in-depth exploration of Eulsukdo Island’s ecology. Immerse yourself in Eulsukdo's nature with all five senses through the ‘Archive Space,’ which houses ecological data, the ‘Birding Space,’ where you can observe migratory birds up close, and the ‘Bird Experience Space,’ which sparks children's curiosity. Discover the unique beauty of nature and migratory birds at the Nakdong Estuary Eco Center.
Nakdong Estuary Eco Center
Address : 1240, Nakdongnam-ro, Saha-gu, Busan
Direction : 1-minute walk from Exit 3, Hadan Station, Busan Metro Line 1→Bus No. 128-1, 161, 61, 55, 3, 171 or 124 from Hadan Station Transfer →Get off at Eulsukdo Cultural Center Station→13-minute walk
Parking : Available (charged)
Opening hours : Tuesday–Sunday 09:00–18:00
Closed days :  Closed on Mondays
Website : Shortcut
Inquiries : +82-51-209-2000

Amisan Observatory

Downstream the Nakdonggang River is home to numerous migratory birds enjoying rich food and clear water. Visit the Amisan Observatory to view a fantastic landscape where the river meets the ocean. 

Downstream the long and winding Nakdonggang River, Saha-gu and Gangseo-gu, Busan is where the river reaches the ocean. In the area surrounding Saha-gu’s Dadaepo Beach, you can find the Amisan Observatory, where you can see the unique sandy islands downstream the Nakdonggang River along with the low-flying kites against the tranquil backdrop of sunrise and sunset. 

On the second floor of the observatory, you can explore the ecology of the Nakdong estuary and learn about the formation of the delta. 
From the third-floor of the observatory, use the telescope to observe the shifting sand dunes of the Nakdong estuary and take in the breathtaking views of the river and sea. You can also spot sandy islands where migratory birds rest, either through the telescope or with the naked eye.

Don’t miss the Amisan Noeulmaru-gil, a scenic path offering another way to view the downstream stretch of the Nakdonggang River. The moment you step outside and feel the ocean breeze, you’ll experience an even more breathtaking connection to nature. Take the wooden staircases that connect to the observation points below Noeulmaru-gil for stunning views. At sunset, this spot offers a fantastic panorama of the ocean, the setting sun, and the sandy beach. The clouds hovering above the crimson sun over the dark silhouette of Gadeokdo Island resemble a mesmerizing movie scene. It’s also spectacular to watch migratory birds, such as kites and buzzards, soaring over the mouth of the Nakdonggang River.

Amisan Observatory is a place where you can see nature’s magnificent view of the natural sandy beach, the migratory birds, and the sunset’s red glow. 
Need rest from a busy daily life? Need a moment of peace? Climb up the Amisan Observatory to receive the most beautiful comfort that’s out there.
Amisan Observatory

Direction : 1-minute walk from Exit 1, Dadaepo Harbor Station, Busan Metro Line 1→Bus No. Saha-gu 1 from Daedae Nonghyup Station →Get off at Molundae Catholic Church Station→1-minute walk

Artificial Migratory Bird Habitat Myeongpum Dulle Trails

I think many people still don't know about this place. Originally, it was a place where the general public was prohibited from entering because it was a military operation area, so it is preserved as an internal wetland, its natural state. It has been open as a trail since July 2022.

Myeongpum Dulle Trails are just the right length for a leisurely walk. 
However, to protect the migratory birds, it’s important to stay on the designated paths.
In spring and autumn, flocks of greenshanks and plovers rest here, and you may even spot whooper swans feeding occasionally. The sight of migrating birds and the gentle breeze rustling through the reeds create a soothing and relaxing atmosphere.

The nearby mudflats are accessible for an hour before and after low tide, offering a unique experience and a great ecological lesson for children.
The Myeongpum Dulle Trails also connect to Galmaet Trails, and a small forest trail runs alongside the road, making it a perfect spot to enjoy a walk with your pet. Both migratory birds and visitors can find a peaceful rest here.

One of the best things about Busan is the harmony between its bustling city center and serene natural surroundings. This year, Busan has introduced a new opportunity to enjoy the diverse natural scenery at Nakdonggang River Gamdongpogu Port. 
In winter, you’ll also find some special visitors: migratory birds.

The program includes a preliminary briefing on the habits and characteristics of migratory birds in the Nakdonggang River, as well as guidance on the best birdwatching spots in the park and what to look for. Get up close to migratory birds and experience the true beauty of nature!

Enjoy Some Harmless Cuteness! A Collection Of Lovely Places To Relax

If you’re feeling tired, why not embark on a journey filled with heart-warming cuteness?
Here are some of Busan’s “healing” destinations full of adorable charm and tranquility!

PAPER GARDEN

PAPER GARDEN is a charming prop shop filled with various home accessories, including plants, knitted items, and kitchenware. The name reflects the idea of sketching your dream garden on pure white paper. Inside, you’ll find a variety of botanicals, potted greenery, and crocheted plants, all harmoniously blending to create a warm and peaceful ambiance that fits the shop’s “garden” concept.

PAPER GARDEN can be divided into three main areas: one with mats and knitted items, another with a variety of houseplants, and a third with kitchenware and accessories. Among these, the “in-house rugs” are PAPER GARDEN’s flagship product. Designed and made entirely in-house, each rug has an interesting story, making it a much sought-after signature item. If you’re looking for a special home accessory, a PAPER GARDEN rug might be the perfect choice.

The shop is also pet-friendly, making it a great spot for pet owners to visit with their furry friends. Come and experience the little joys of life at this home accessory shop that adds a touch of happiness to your everyday!

A Complete Guide to the Best All-Inclusive Trips for the Perfect Break in Busan
records.description:
When it comes to ‘hocance,’ a portmanteau of hotel and vacance, the company you keep is everything. At an all-inclusive hotel where you can enjoy all your meals, relaxation, and activities, your stay becomes even more enjoyable. Whether you're looking for a family holiday with the kids, a relaxing break with your parents, or a romantic day out with your partner, check out the all-inclusive hotels below to create the perfect getaway experience!

With Children, Ananti At Busan Cove

Ananti At Busan Cove is a place where you can experience a special stay with the blue sea of Gijang. Enjoy a relaxing break in a wonderful atmosphere with excellent facilities and stunning sea views.

The most eye-catching feature of Ananti At Busan Cove is the Infinity Pool. It is the largest outdoor swimming pool among luxury hotels in Korea, and its panoramic view of the sea makes it even more special. The hotel's McQueen's Pool offers the ultimate holiday experience. In addition, the Water House, which combines a hot spring and swimming pool, is unique in that you can enjoy media art while swimming.

Don't miss out on the variety of gourmet experiences. From DAMOIM, an open-kitchen buffet restaurant serving Korean, Western, Chinese, and Japanese cuisine, to McQueen's Grill & Bar, which serves fresh seafood and creative dishes, to Cabinét de Poisson, a bakery-café where you can relax with freshly baked bread and a cup of coffee, there is a choice of dining venues to suit all tastes. Cabinét de Poisson is also home to a spectacular media art gallery, making it a great place to take photos.

The hotel's facilities are also noteworthy, including banquet and meeting rooms for weddings and private functions, an ocean-view sauna and spa, and a state-of-the-art fitness center. It's fun to stroll around Ananti Town, which offers a range of cultural amenities, including a select shop, a bookstore, a gallery, and a craft beer bar.

Within Ananti Cove, there is Ananti at Busan Cove (hotel) and Ananti Cove Penthouse. Ananti at Busan Cove (hotel) is open to anyone who wishes to stay after making a reservation, while Ananti Cove Penthouse is a private residence that can only be booked by members.

Enjoy a premium stay at Ananti Cove, where refreshing ocean views meet world-class facilities!
 Ananti At Busan Cove

With Family, Park Hyatt Busan

Here you can experience unique wellness programs such as Mindfulness Floating SoundZen, where you meditate on the water with the soothing sounds and sound waves of a singing bowl, and ZenCent Pilates, which combines aromatherapy and Pilates for an invigorating day.

The hotel also offers a wide range of comfortable facilities. From the indoor swimming pool overlooking Gwangandaegyo Bridge to the state-of-the-art fitness center, food and beverage services and comfortable rooms, everything about the hotel is first class.

records.name: Values at Your Fingertips: Busan’s Cultural Spaces for Hands-On Experiences
records.description:
There are things you can't fully understand just by looking at them. Here are some special hands-on cultural spaces in Busan where you can engage more deeply with the space and culture through touch and experience.

4233 Mind Space

4233 Mind Space opened in Gwangan-dong, Busan after Seoul. Just as the Yeonnam branch in Seoul is very popular, the Gwangan branch is becoming increasingly popular with visitors.
Have you ever wondered what it is about them that has captured the hearts of so many?

4233 Mind Space is an experiential psychological exhibition space for people who want to get to know about the person of their interest in different relationships and share psychological healing experiences. 
For the unique name of the center, the number 42 represents 'between' people and the number 33 represents the shape of two people, reflecting the nature of the place where you can experience psychological interaction 'between two people'. 
As the name suggests, the space is for two people only and reservations are required as a private experience program is offered. 

Once inside, there are three corners that you must go through in order:
‘Me Next to You’, where you can see yourself from the other person's point of view,
‘My Life Barometer’, where you choose the seven values that are most important to you out of 60,
and ‘Values, Together’, where you prioritize your chosen values and create a character that reflects your values.

Once you've cleared these corners, you'll find yourself in the Heart Square, where you can do the activities in any order you like, but be prepared and patient to wait for people who have already been there.
Once you've completed the experience, you'll be given a key to the Heart Room. We can't reveal the contents of the program here, but there are many testimonials of people being moved to tears during the experience, so be prepared to be emotional.

After all the experiences, you can also have a consultation with an expert, depending on the program you have booked. 
On your way out, take a look at some of 4233 Mind Space's unique souvenirs to make the most of your experience.

Enjoy a special moment of mutual understanding at 4233 Mind Space, Gwangan Branch!

4233 Mind Space, Gwangan Branch
Address : 148, Gwangnam-ro, Suyeong-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 2, Gwangan Station, Busan Metro Line 2 → 13-minute walk (Parking at Gwangan Public Parking Lot in Suyeong-gu)
Opening hours : Everyday 10:00 ~ 21:00(Closed regularly on the 3rd Tuesday of every month)

rocarl

rocarl is a perfume workshop located in AREA6, a cultural complex in Yeongdo. True to its name, which is a Busanized version of the English word 'rocal' meaning 'local,' the shop offers fragrance products themed around various attractions in Busan.

The bright interiors and unique scents that fill the small shop make you feel good from the moment you walk in. In addition to buying finished products, you can take a one-day course to create your own scent.

What's special is that, unlike most perfume workshops, they also offer hand cream customization classes. If you've ever wanted to try your hand at perfume making but haven't had much success, this is the place to be!

rocarl

Bomulsum in Busan

A throwback to the 1970s and 1990s, Bomulsum in Busan is like an exhibition center filled with eye-catching items from the moment you enter. Advertising posters and other retro items fill the steep staircase. Inside, where popular songs from the 80s and 90s play nonstop, you'll find abacuses, old cassette players, tin lunch boxes and all sorts of other items. If you're middle-aged, these are the things you used as a child, and if you're young, these are the things your parents' generation used.

It's not just a pile of old stuff, but it's organized and categorized in a way that makes it easy for people to see and experience. A kitchen with old sweets, condiments, drinks and more. A music room with records, tapes, and old posters. A study room with textbooks, book bags, Boy Scout uniforms, and more. A liquor collection with vintage, exotic and unique liquors. It's a collection so alive that you can feel the nostalgia just by walking through each room. 

Everything is there to touch and buy. You can even put on your old school uniform, try out the items and have your photo taken as if you were back in the day.

Bomulsum in Busan

Music Complex Seoul - Busan

Introducing Music Complex Seoul – Busan: A Special Destination for Vinyl Lovers!

Music Complex Seoul - Busan is known for its red lighting and distinctive high floor. It’s also famous for housing over 20,000 vinyl records, with a wide variety of albums catering to diverse musical tastes. One of its main attractions is that, for an admission fee of 20,000 won per person, you can enjoy unlimited music listening.

On the first floor, you can order drinks and sit down to enjoy vinyl. Each table is equipped with its own turntable and headset, but using the equipment can be a bit tricky depending on the turntable’s features. If you’re unsure, don’t hesitate to ask the staff for help. Also, there are separate LPs for listening and for sale, which can be confusing, so be sure to read the descriptions carefully before making your choice!

On the stairs between the first and second floors, you’ll find a decorative cabinet filled with LP albums, which is also famous as a photo zone due to its unique interior design at Music Complex Seoul - Busan. There is also a DJ booth concept photo zone with an LP album cabinet backdrop. Capture stunning photos in this special photo zone, a feature that you can only find here.

The second floor features a venue for live music performances. Jazz, Latin music, and other genres are performed here. You can check their Instagram page (@music.complex.seoul) for the schedule and more information.

Spend a day indulging your ears at Music Complex Seoul - Busan, where you can relax and enjoy vinyl music in a laid-back atmosphere.

Music Complex Seoul - Busan

Jukseonggrim

Jukseonggrim is a cultural complex that combines the history of Jukseong-ri, Gijang-gun, Busan, with hands-on play. It is run by a couple who were former curators of children's cultural spaces and museums, so it is designed to allow children to enjoy culture in a more friendly way.

Jukseonggrim is 100% reservation-based, allowing you to enjoy a comfortable three-hour experience per time slot. The KRW 7,000 entrance fee, which includes a drink, makes it even more worthwhile. There's also a menu of kid-friendly snacks, such as pizza and bread.

There are various play areas, such as "Coloring Zone," where children can paint freely in a large space, "Moonlight Night," where they can play with props and chalk, "Jukseong Forest," where magnets and blocks are the main tools, and outdoor toy fishing. Each play area has a thematic story that reflects the history and culture of Jukseong-ri, Gijang-gun, so you can let your children have fun and enjoy a cultural experience at the same time.

They also run paid programs, such as “Making a Sea Treasure Jukseong Fish Bowl” and “Making a Gijang Gift Set,” for more unique experiences.
Experience Jukseong-ri with all your senses at Jukseonggrim, a playground for children and adults!

records.name: A Trip to a Hidden Island in Busan: Relaxing and Healing Experiences with Nature and the Sea
records.description:
Enjoy relaxing moments on the islands scattered across the vast sea! Explore 'island destinations' where you can experience Busan's ecology and culture up close while unwinding in lush greenery.

Jungsado Island In Gangseo-gu 

Jungsado Island in Gangseo-gu, Busan offers a panoramic view of the Nakdonggang River. 
It has recently become a popular camping spot. It is a favorite among campers because there are many large areas that make it easy to set up tents. It is also attractive because the unadorned natural scenery has been preserved.

There are many activities to enjoy including camping, riverside walks, and cycling. It is also a popular fishing spot for anglers. It is the perfect place for those who love nature tourism. However, there are no amenities such as supermarkets or convenience stores nearby, so it is recommended to prepare the necessary items in advance.

If you explore the surroundings of the island, you will see several cafes. After camping or hiking, you can stop at a cafe for a unique and relaxing experience. Enjoy a special nature trip to Jungsado, an island with a beautiful river view!
Jungsado Island In Gangseo-gu
Address : Singman-dong, Gangseo-gu, Busan
Directions :Exit 1, Buram Station, Busan-Gimhae Light Rail Transit Line of Busan Metro → Bus From Buram-dong Community Center Stop → 15-minute walk from Simangyo Bridge
Inquiries : +82-51-970-4000 (Gangseo-gu Office)

Gadeokdo Lighthouse Experience

Get a chance to stay at a special accommodation that requires advance reservations! Check out the “Gadeokdo Lighthouse Experience” program, where you can enjoy both the historical significance and the scenery.

Gadeokdo Lighthouse is one of the last structures of the Korean Empire. The entrance with the symbol of the Korean Empire, the plum blossom, and the Gadeokdo Lighthouse Time Capsule buried to commemorate the completion of the new Gadeokdo Lighthouse in 2002, offer a glimpse into the long history of this place.

The lighthouse experience is only available to those who have applied in advance and been selected. You can take a tour of the lighthouse museum and a tour of the lighthouse tower, which is about 40 meters high, with vivid explanations from the lighthouse staff. It is a meaningful opportunity to learn about the history and structure of the lighthouse. The view of Gadeokdo Island from the bell tower is magnificent. One of the highlights is being able to enjoy the sea view of Gadeokdo Island to your heart's content even from your accommodation.
The restaurant is in the basement and does not serve meals, so it is recommended that you bring your own food. Please also remember that this is a military facility, so there are rules to follow, such as restrictions on going out in the evening and restrictions on taking photographs!

Experience the lighthouse on Gadeokdo Island, where history and nature come together for a special day. Want to have a meaningful trip? Apply for this program now! 

Gadeokdo Lighthouse Experience
Address: 10, Oeyangpo-ro, Gangseo-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 3, Hadan Station, Busan Metro Line 1 → Bus No. 2000 (Express) from Hadan Station Transfer Center → Bus No. Gangseo-gu 1 from Cheonseong IC  Dongjung Stop → 39-minute walk from Oeyangpo Stop
Inquiries :+82-51-971-9710

Dongbaekseom Island

Dongbaekseom Island has long been admired for its beauty. Although it has been connected to the mainland by sedimentation over the years, it still retains the name 'island' and traces of its ancient topography. The name “Haeundae” comes from the fact that the Silla-era scholar Choi Chi-won, who admired the beauty of the island, carved his own name on a rock, and the landscape has long been renowned for its outstanding beauty.

There are many historical symbols, so it is fun to look around. There are various attractions, including the legendary Princess Hwangok Mermaid Statue and the Nurimaru APEC House, where the 2005 APEC Summit was held. You can also enjoy the magnificent scenery of camellias in full bloom from winter to spring.

Make many fond memories on Dongbaekseom Island, where you can enjoy its awe-inspiring natural scenery and interesting history together!
Dongbaekseom Island
Address : 710-1, U-dong, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 1, Dongbaek Station, Busan Metro Line 2 → 17-minute walk
Inquiries : +82-51-749-7621

Oryukdo Islets

The emerald sea where the East Sea and the South Sea meet. There are five islands—sometimes six—seen on the brilliant blue rug.
The coastal waters of Oryukdo Islets are enough to fascinate visitors.

Oryukdo Islets, which is well-known as one of the most beautiful islands in Busan, refers to a group of rocky islands off Yongho-dong, Nam-gu, Busan. It has been designated as Busan National Geopark in recognition of its geological value: rock formed through volcanic activities 80 million years ago. In addition, it is a marine sanctuary, where protected marine creatures live, and also state-designated cultural heritage.

Oryukdo Islets are composed of Bangpaeseom Island, Solseom Island, Suriseom Island, Songgotseom Island, Gulseom Island, and Deungdaeseom Island, in order of proximity to the land. The name comes from the five (“o”) islands seen at low tide and the six (“ryuk”) islands at high tide. Deungdaeseom Island, the farthest island, has the Oryukdo Lighthouse, and it is the only one accessible to people among those islands. The Lighthouse serves as a gateway to Busanhang Port, which ships entering Busan must pass by.

Visit the Sunrise Park if you want to enjoy the unobstructed view of Oryukdo Islets. As you climb up the hill above the parking lot, you can enjoy the panoramic view with a cool sea breeze. The presence of ecological wetlands, trails, pavilions, and benches makes it a perfect spot for a picnic. Why not go down the hill and head to Oryukdo Skywalk, where you can see Oryukdo Islets right in front of your eyes? Skywalk, built on the edge of cliffs of unique rock formations, always teems with the laughter of visitors who want to enjoy the thrill of looking down at the sea through the glass plates under their feet.

Travelers feel the sea soak into their minds as they face the open sea, and the worries and stresses of daily life go away. The sea of Oryukdo Islets always looks peaceful.

Oryukdo Islets

records.name: A Passionate City, Busan! A Journey to Sports Destinations
records.description:
Fancy a sports trip to Busan? There, you can watch exciting games, get active, and boost your energy levels. Check out the thrilling sports spots in Busan. Come to Busan in the spring, and get your energy levels up!

 Busan E-sports Arena 

Busan E-sports Arena (BRENA) is an e-sports stadium in Seomyeon where everyone can watch and experience e-sports. It hosts various games, from major e-sports competitions to amateur leagues, and also has a training and research room for professional players, making it a great place for anyone who loves e-sports to visit.

It has a 330-seat main stadium and two auxiliary stadiums, and offers a unique spectator experience with an ultra-large LED display, face-to-face seating, and a pub-style viewing area. It also has a real-time broadcasting system, so you can feel the excitement of the game live on YouTube and other platforms.

The Busan E-sports Arena offers a variety of programs.
The BRENA Tour program, which goes beyond just watching a match and includes a tour of the stadium's interior and experience of its main facilities, and provides an overview of e-sports. Visitors will also be able to play games and take photos in the main stadium's player seats.
In addition, the 'E-sports Experience Program', designed to promote and revitalize e-sports, will allow visitors to try their hand at e-sports in the BLUE SPACE.

The Busan E-sports Arena is the best place for everyone to easily visit and feel the energy of e-sports! If you want a different kind of sports experience, come here, and feel the excitement for yourself!

 Busan E-Sports Arena 
Address : 16F, 15, Samjeong Tower, 672, Jungang-daero, Busanjin-gu, Busan 
Directions : Exit 2, Seomyeon Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> 6-minute walk 
Opening hours : Tuesday – Sunday 11:00~20:00
Website : Shortcut
Inquiries : +82-507-1472-5330

 Hwangnyeongsan Leports Park 

Hwangnyeongsan Leports Park is a great place to enjoy sports in the fresh air. It's a popular place for an everyday workout because of its convenient location close to the city center. It's got all sorts of sports facilities, like a soccer field, wrestling ring, tennis court, badminton court, and a gateball field, so there's something for everyone.

The main place here is the big sports ground, which is 200 meters up in the air. It's the highest soccer field in Busan, and you can enjoy soccer in a unique way while looking down on the Seomyeon area. It also has artificial turf, which makes it safer to play on.

There's also Hwangnyeongsan Eco Play Park, making it a great place to visit as a family. It's got all sorts of fun play equipment like slides, stepping stones, and more, making it the perfect place for children to play outdoors.

Some of the sports facilities require advance reservations, but you can easily reserve your favorite spot via the Busanjin-gu Office website.

If you're looking for an invigorating workout in the middle of nature, Hwangnyeongsan Leports Park is the place to be!

 Hwangnyeongsan Leports Park 
Address : 99, Jinnam-ro 328beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan 
Directions : Exit 2, Bujeon Station, Busan Metro Line 1 -> Bus No. Busanjin-gu 2 from Bujeon Station Stop -> 17-minute walk from Daesan Apt. Stop 
Website : Short cut
Inquiries : +82-51-605-4128

 Celtic Tiger Main Branch

Celtic Tiger is a sports pub where people who love football gather. The interior is decorated with various soccer-related items, and even the staff members wear uniforms, which makes the atmosphere really special.

You can watch live football matches from anywhere, as they’ve installed TVs all around the bar, and the sound is amazing! And for the ultimate experience, you can also take a photo in the special zone with props that symbolize your favorite teams. It really is a special place for soccer fans.

You can get custom beer glasses with soccer players on them! And if you want to get really personal, you can even order a beer in a glass with the player of your team! The menu has a whole host of drinks and food options, so you can enjoy the game while treating your tasting buds. There are also entertainment elements, such as darts games, so you won't get bored before or after the game.

Have fun at Celtic Tiger with your friends who love football. It is the perfect place for football fans!

Celtic Tiger Main Branch
Address : 38, Seomyeon-ro, Busanjin-gu, Busan 
Directions : Exit 7, Seomyeon Station, Busan Metro Line 2 -> 6-minute walk 
Opening hours : Tuesday-Thursday, Sunday 17:00~02:00 / Friday-Saturday 17:00~03:00
Inquiries : +82-507-1337-8013

Sajik Baseball Stadium

Baseball comes first in Busan because its people are unusually big fans of the sport. The Sajik Baseball Stadium—home of the Lotte giants, the most popular baseball club—features a unique cheering culture embodying their one-of-a-kind love for baseball. 

Until the early 2010s, waves of well-known cheering gears, such as newspaper and plastic bags, swept over Sajik Baseball Stadium’s stands. The multitude of Lotte Giants fans shouts the chant “Ma” whenever opposing pitchers make a diversion and use different cheers for each player in addition to cheerleaders’ performances and various events between every inning. The Sajik Baseball Stadium is where you can feel Busan’s burning passion, even if you don’t know anything about baseball. It is only in this stadium that you can experience the lighting show where everyone sings famous old songs together as the lighting towers turn off right after the 5th inning.

For a unique atmosphere, you should be seated in the infield (third base), section C behind home plate, or the outfield. You can feel the stadium’s relaxation and romance, different from the cheering section on the first-base side. There is also an unusual pleasure in watching a small group of away fans cheering. Note that the Sajik Baseball Stadium provides various ticket discounts, so check them out on the Lotte Giants website.

The fervor was said to be too intense, but eyebrow-raising moments have almost gone. Now, the Sajik Baseball Stadium has been completely recognized as a leisure space for families, lovers, and friends to visit together. Waiting to meet the players up close is also an exhilarating experience. Above all, however, you can feel the Busan people’s love for baseball when you watch them cheer for players as if they were popular entertainers.

When it comes to the baseball park, you can’t miss food. Many people buy food at the large shop across the Sajik Baseball Stadium. However, 300 m from the main gate of the baseball park, you can find Gukmin Market with different restaurants selling various dishes such as spicy rice cakes, fish cake, fritters, pig’s trotter, chicken, and glazed fried chicken bites. If you are pressed for time, you can also buy food from the stadium’s snack bars. Although they used to be notorious for overpricing, there’s no need to worry because the food is affordable.

Please come to the Sajik Baseball Stadium, a small Busan, and witness and experience Busan’s enthusiasm, energy, leisure, and romance.

Sajik Baseball Stadium
Address : 45, Sajik-ro, Dongnae-gu, Busan
Opening hours  : Refer to the website
Directions : Walk for 11 min from Exit 9 of Sports Complex Station on Busan Metro Line 3 / Get off Bus 54, 57, 83-1, or 131 at Sajik Swimming Pool and walk for 4 min
Website : Short cut
Inquiries : +82-51-505-7422

 Wave Rock 

Want to feel the joy of challenge and achievement with indoor climbing? Come and try it at Wave Rock in Busan, which climbing fans love for its great facilities and varied route settings!

Wave Rock has two floors. On the first floor, there's a climbing wall, and on the second floor, there's a rest area, lockers, and changing rooms. You can buy various Wave Rock products at the entrance.

Before you start, you will be given instructions and a demonstration of how to climb. The staff will kindly explain the instructions and show you how to climb, so even beginners can feel free to try it. There are various training programs available, including one-day climbing experiences, so you can choose according to your skill level and preferences.

With up to four branches in Busan, it's really convenient because you can use all of them with just one membership. 
If you're up for something a bit different, why not give climbing at Wave Rock a go?

records.name: Your Dogs Would Love It
Finding Calm in Busan: 4 Places Full of Peace and Local Charm
records.originalName: Finding Calm in Busan: 4 Places Full of Peace and Local Charm
records.description:
No matter the season, Busan offers more than just its iconic landmarks and bustling tourist spots. For travelers who prefer to venture off the beaten path, the city is also home to tranquil locations where you can experience authentic K-culture and connect with nature. Whether you're looking to slow down, soak in local culture, or simply escape the crowds, these hidden gems provide the perfect setting for peaceful reflection and cultural discovery. 

Dongbaek Park (Dongbaekseom Island)

Tucked at the southern edge of Haeundae Beach, Dongbaekseom Island offers a peaceful retreat from the city’s fast pace. Once a true island, it is now connected to the mainland through natural sedimentation and serves as a lush coastal park filled with history, culture, and panoramic views.

Encircling the island is a well-maintained trail, just about 1 kilometer long (0.6 miles), making it an easy, scenic walk for visitors of all ages. Along the path, you'll encounter sweeping views of Gwangan Bridge, Oryukdo Islets, and the white sands of Haeundae Beach. These serene landscapes have inspired poets and scholars for generations.

Key sights along the trail include the Dongbaek Lighthouse, the Princess Hwangok Mermaid Statue, and the Haeundae Carved Stone, etched with the name that gave Haeundae Beach its title. But, perhaps the island’s most notable landmark is the Nurimaru APEC House.

Perched at the western tip of the island, the Nurimaru APEC House hosted the 2005 APEC Summit, welcoming leaders from 21 member economies. The venue later served as a key site during the 2019 ASEAN-ROK Commemorative Summit and remains open to the public today. Free to enter, the facility preserves the interior used during the summits, offering visitors a unique glimpse into Korea’s role in global diplomacy.

Its location is unmatched, providing a dramatic vantage point over the full span of Gwangan Bridge and the surrounding coastline. The lighthouse observatory deck, situated next to the APEC House, is one of the best spots to capture a wide-angle photo of the structure against the sea and sky. As day turns to night, the view becomes even more magical with city lights reflecting across the water.

Dongbaekseom has also gained recognition through Korean pop culture. It served as a filming location for K-dramas such as The King: Eternal Monarch and Shopping King Louie. Nurimaru was also featured in the blockbuster Korean movie Haeundae, which dramatizes a fictional tsunami hitting Busan.
Dongbaek Park (Dongbaekseom Island)
Address : 99, Dongbaek-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Directions : It's about a 17-minute walk from Exit 1 of Dongbaek Station on Busan Metro Line 2.

Nurimaru APEC House
Address : 116, Dongbaek-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
 Directions : It's about a 13-minute walk from Exit 1 of Dongbaek Station on Busan Metro Line 2.
Opening hours : 09:00 – 18:00 (Closed on the first Monday of each month)
Website : Open a new window

Jukseong Dream Open Set (Jukseong Church)

If you're seeking a quiet coastal escape with a touch of Korean drama charm, Duho Village in Gijang-gun offers the perfect blend of scenery and storytelling. This peaceful fishing village is home to the Jukseong Dream Open Set, also known as Jukseong Church, a striking film set that has become one of the region’s most photogenic landmarks.
Despite its name, Jukseong Church is not a functioning place of worship. It was originally constructed in 2009 for the Korean drama Dream, and its picturesque architecture, featuring a bold red roof set against the deep blue sea, quickly gained popularity among locals and travelers alike. After filming concluded, Gijang-gun chose to preserve the set, recognizing its value as a cultural and visual icon. Today, the building occasionally hosts small exhibitions by local artists.

The site continues to draw the attention of filmmakers and K-drama fans. More recently, it appeared in the drama Curtain Call, starring Ha Ji-won and Kang Ha-neul.

Just a short walk from Jukseong Church, you’ll find Jukseong Port and the nearby breakwater, both beloved by local fishermen and visitors in search of quiet coastal views. The sight of Jukseong Church from the breakwater is especially captivating.

On the way to Jukseong Breakwater, you’ll come across Hwanghakdae, a small coastal hill where renowned Joseon-era poet Yun Seondo spent six years in exile. Here, he composed sijo, traditional Korean poems, while reflecting on life and nature. The name “Hwanghakdae” means “yellow crane platform,” inspired by the place’s resemblance to a crane spreading its wings.

Across from Jukseong Church, overlooking Duho Village, stands a cluster of ancient black pines known as Gijang Jukseong-ri Haesong. Though they appear to be one large tree, they are actually five black pines growing together, estimated to be between 250 and 300 years old. These living landmarks are easily accessible on foot and add a quiet sense of timelessness to the landscape.

records.name: Picture-Perfect Places in Busan You Can’t Miss Right Now
records.description:
Famous for its state-of-the-art technology, friendly locals, flavorful cuisine, and pop-cultural influence, South Korea is certainly on many people’s travel bucket lists. To be more specific, the city of Busan has quickly emerged as a popular destination that is worth visiting. 

Home to more than 3.48 million individuals, it continues to draw travelers from not only Korea but beyond. This is due to its striking seaside location. Let’s not forget the glorious sandy beaches, vibrant street markets, intriguing museums, and fascinating cultural sites. You’ll also find endless special events and occasions worth celebrating. 

Despite being off the radar of many foreign travelers for a while, the secret is out, and tourists are flocking to Busan to capture memories. This includes clicking the city’s most Instagrammable places and taking part in photography tours galore to savor the splendor. 
What better time to visit than now? So if you’ve got that desire to explore and strike a pose in South Korea’s premier seaside destination, here’s a list of picture-perfect places in Busan you can’t miss. 
Kyungsung University Culture Alley- A Glimpse of Busan’s Evolution 

As a tourist in Busan, getting a glimpse of how the city has revolutionized over the years is possible through the Kyungsung University Culture Alley. The location is rooted deep in tradition, thanks to the ancient-themed residences on display. 

The street provides visitors with a sublime blend of restaurants, photo spots, and streets calling for tourists to explore. It’s always recommended to pay a visit during the afternoon, but the evening hours are even better for that special experience. The place puts forth a silent yet compelling aura to take in, making this perfect for Instagrammable photos. Visitors immerse themselves in Busan’s historical passage on the journey. 

The fun and thrill don’t stop there. If you’re lucky enough to pay a visit during the weekend, you can witness live plays, take a quick bite at the unique ambient cafes, or pop into a pub that awaits your arrival in every alleyway. 

The unique infrastructure is another attractive feature among the youth. You are sure to find some alleys connecting vertically, while others run horizontally. There are four entrances in total, and each one of them provides a different theme.

The alley located right below the Bell Tower gives you the thrill of entering a maze. Another special touch is to find vines climbing across the walls. These blend impeccably with old school bricks and provide a nature-filled experience. All the stand-out exteriors and colorful scenery give visitors the perfect backdrop to pose against. This is why a stop here during photography tours is considered a must. 
Kyungsung University Culture Alley
Address : 36-1, Suyeong-ro 334beon-gil, Nam-gu, Busan
Directions : Exit 1, Kyungsung Univ·Pukyong Nat’l Univ Station (Busan Subway Line 2) → 242 m walk
Operating Hours : Vary depending on whether it's a semester or vacation period. 
- Semester: Mon–Sat 09:00 – 21:00
- Vacation: Mon–Fri 09:00 – 18:00(Closed on public holidays)

Oryukdo Sunrise Park- Immerse Yourself in Scenic Island Beauty

A trip to Busan is incomplete without paying a visit to the Oryukdo Sunrise Park. Located on a hilltop in Busan’s Namgu District, the location offers an incredible view of the Oryukdo Skywalk and the Islets. 
Nature enthusiasts will adore the park, which is very popular during the Spring season. This is when daffodils and Canola flowers bloom, providing the most breathtaking atmosphere for wonderful memories. Those in search of healing can enjoy the glittering sea views against the stunning floral surroundings. Finding a picture-perfect spot here that overlooks the sea isn’t difficult, and what you end up with is a centerpiece for your album. 
Upon climbing the hill, visitors can take in the breathtaking panoramic view and inhale the cool sea breeze nearby. There are many activities to enjoy and places to photograph, including the ecological wetlands, picnic benches, trails, and pavilions. 

For those seeking a little more adventure, the Skywalk offers great thrills, thanks to its design. 
It’s created on the cliff’s edge and features rock formations. Tourists can make the most of their love for photography here with clicks of the sea below that’s visible through the transparent glass plates they’re standing on. This, combined with the sun shining from above and soothing sea breeze, adds that magical touch for an exhilarating experience. 

Visitors can similarly hike along the trail and get close to nature along the park’s 4.7 km stretch. Having the Oryukdo Islets silhouette near the sea is another great Instagrammable photo spot, not to forget the cherry blossoms during the springtime. As you move upward along the wooden road, the trail leads closer to the Igidae Waterside Park. 
Oryukdo Sunrise Park
Address : 137, Oryukdo-ro, Namgu, Busan
Directions : Exit 5, Kyungsung Univ·Pukyong Nat’l Univ Station, Busan Subway Line 2 → Transfer to Bus 24, 27, 131 or Nam-gu 2 → Get off at Oryukdo SK Apartment

Haeundae Songnim Park - One of Busan’s Most Captivating Attractions

The popular Haeundae Songnim Park gets raving reviews for a good reason. The area offers a stellar coastal view, thanks to its location and tons of instagrammable spots, thanks to the hydrangea flowers everywhere. Visitors leave with an unforgettable and aesthetically pleasing experience, ideal for nature lovers and those seeking inner peace.
The best part is its central location near the Haeundae Beach, giving the eco-friendly tourist site the title of the perfect Instagrammable photo spot in Busan. It’s not just the immaculate views but the hiking trails that allow you to soak up nature’s beauty. Every trail leads to different viewpoints and city attractions, so the camera can never stop clicking. 

Haeundae Songlim Park is famous among Koreans and foreigners who come here to try barefoot walking, or "earthing," which is known for bringing tons of health benefits. This activity is so fun, especially if you want to escape the hustle and bustle of city life and want to feel close to nature.
Haeundae Songnim Park is becoming super popular spot lately because of the hydrangeas. The park is really close to the Haeundae beach, so it's easy to stop by while you're in the area. What makes it extra cool is that you can see both the ocean and the hydrangeas at the same time. Trust me, you will fall in love with the view and will end up taking 50+ photos.

records.name: Beat the Heat: Discover Busan's Cool Indoor Art & Culture Scene
records.description:
Summer in Busan is full of coastal charm, vibrant festivals, and sun-soaked adventures. But as temperatures climb, the intense heat and humidity can make outdoor plans feel more exhausting than exciting. Fortunately, the city offers a rich variety of indoor cultural spaces where you can stay cool and still enjoy its creative energy. From immersive art to meaningful heritage sites, these four destinations provide the perfect escape from the heat while offering a fresh perspective on Busan's culture.
F1963

F1963 stands as Busan's premier urban cultural complex, masterfully transforming a former wire rope factory into a dynamic hub for art, culture, and community experiences. This thoughtful recreation of industrial space has become a meaningful cultural anchor for the city.

Originally operating as a wire rope factory for Kiswire from 1963 to 2008, the site was reimagined in 2016 for the Busan Biennale art festival. The distinctive name 'F1963' combines 'F' for 'factory' and '1963,' marking its original opening year. Renowned Korean architect Jo Byeongsu spearheaded the sensitive remodeling process, carefully preserving and repurposing original architectural elements like wooden trusses and iron plates throughout the complex, creating a harmonious dialogue between industrial heritage and contemporary purpose.

F1963 offers an abundance of engaging indoor activities, making it an ideal refuge from the summer heat. The spacious interiors remain comfortably cool, and the complex invites visitors to linger without the discomfort of outdoor heat.
Kukje Gallery Busan, the second location of one of Seoul’s most prestigious galleries, brings world-class paintings, sculptures, and photography exhibitions by globally renowned artists to Busan's cultural landscape. Alongside it, the expansive YES24 Used Bookstore offers a literary haven with over 200,000 titles, including rare out-of-print books. The space also features interactive printing exhibitions, a Crema e-book experience zone, and a dedicated children’s area, making it an ideal destination to enjoy both books and culture in one place.
If you’re in need of a relaxing coffee break, Terarosa Coffee offers a visually stunning setting where industrial heritage blends with art. Inside, tables crafted from original factory iron plates provide unique seating for enjoying freshly roasted coffee and artisanal bread, while wire installation art at the entrance enhances the space's artistic vibe. Nearby, Hyundai Motor Studio Busan stands as an impressive four-story exhibition and experience venue. This free cultural space hosts seasonal themed exhibitions connected to various design content, offering visitors stylish encounters throughout the year.
The F1963 Art Library offers a quiet cultural sanctuary, housing over 11,000 specialized books and materials spanning architecture, music, design, and visual arts. It’s an ideal space for peaceful reflection or immersive reading. After exploring the library and other cultural venues in the area, consider ending your day at Seokcheon Hall, a versatile 600-seat performance venue with flexible seating that hosts a wide range of cultural events and performances.
F1963
Address : 20, Gurak-ro 123Beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan
Transportation : It's about a 20-minute walk from Exit 2 or 4 of Mangmi Station on Busan Metro Line 2. Alternatively, take bus No. 54 and get off at the Kiswire bus stop.
Hours : 09:00 - 24:00 (Each store and facility has different hours. Please refer to the website.)
Website : https://www.f1963.org/en/

Museum 1

When the summer heat becomes overwhelming in Busan, step inside the cool, vibrant world of digital art at Museum 1, South Korea's first and largest museum dedicated entirely to media art. Located in the Centum area, this immersive indoor destination offers a vibrant, air-conditioned space to recharge and explore cutting-edge digital art.
Opened in 2019 by the art agency Kunst 1, Museum 1 was founded with a mission to expand the cultural role of contemporary art by merging technology, philosophy, and aesthetics. It reflects the spirit of the digital era while remaining grounded in artistic tradition.

Spanning over 2,300 square meters across two floors, the museum immediately transports visitors into a surreal environment. LEDs integrated into the floors, ceilings, and walls create an all-encompassing experience where art quite literally surrounds you. As you move through the space, you’ll encounter multimedia installations that blur the lines between traditional and digital expression, making for a dynamic and unforgettable visit.
Currently on view is a large-scale exhibition titled "Myth: The Beginning Story," featuring more than 100 artworks by 18 contemporary artists from five different countries. The exhibition thoughtfully explores universal themes through a variety of genres, including media, painting, sculpture, ceramics, photography, and installation. One of the exhibition's highlights is a massive 8,000-inch LED room showcasing 15 original media artworks. These pieces invite visitors to engage with the philosophical and humanistic ideas at the heart of each artist's vision.
In addition to the main exhibition, a special exhibition space on the second floor provides further opportunities to explore contemporary art.
Recognized by the Korean Tourism Organization as a Korea Unique Venue, Museum 1 offers an interactive and atmospheric experience that truly shines during the peak of summer heat. It’s the perfect place to explore the intersection of art and technology while staying cool, refreshed, and inspired in Busan.
Museum 1
Address : 20, Centum seo-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Transportation : It's about a 5-minute walk from Exit 6 of Centum City Station on Busan Metro Line 2
Hours : 10:00 - 19:00 (Weekdays) / 10:00 - 20:00 (Weekend & Holidays)
Website : https://museum1.co.kr/

Sujeong Cultural Empathy Center

Nestled within Korea's complex historical narrative stands the Sujeong Cultural Empathy Center, housed in a jeoksangaok, a Japanese-style residence from the colonial period. These architectural remnants, whose name, “jeoksangaok,” literally means "houses built by the enemy," tell stories of Korea's modern history through preserved wooden beams and traditional design.
The interior spans two thoughtfully designed floors. The ground level features a media room, library, and self-service café, while the second floor serves as an exhibition space. Traditional elements such as tatami rooms, wooden corridors, and paper screens create an atmosphere that transports visitors back in time while providing respite from the summer heat.
The building gained widespread recognition through popular media, most notably appearing in IU's "Through the Night" music video and the hit drama Mr. Sunshine. It has also served as a filming location for numerous productions, including Voice 3, The General's Son, and AKMU's "Puberty" music video.

On hot summer days, the Sujeong Cultural Empathy Center provides a peaceful and cooling escape from the heat. Inside, the traditional architecture and quiet ambiance offer a perfect setting for reflection. Settling into the serene interior with a warm or iced drink, you can slow down and enjoy a contemplative moment sheltered from the summer sun.
Built in 1943 by Japanese businessman Tamada Minoru, this two-story wooden house is one of Busan's most significant jeoksangaok and is registered as a cultural heritage site. After Korea's liberation in 1945, the building served for decades as the exclusive restaurant Jeongrangak. Recognizing its historical importance, the Cultural Heritage Administration purchased it in 2010. Following several years of restoration, it reopened in 2016 as the cultural space we see today.

While some debate the preservation of colonial-era structures, many point out that places like the Sujeong Cultural Empathy Center hold profound historical value, noting that even painful history we would rather forget must be remembered and shared widely. This space serves as both a window into difficult historical truths and a venue for healing and reflection.

Offering invaluable insight into colonial-era architecture and lifestyle, this building has transformed from a symbol of occupation into a place of cultural dialogue. It is an ideal cool sanctuary for contemplation during Busan's hot summer days.

records.description:
There are times when you crave a moment of tranquility and reflection. Why not discover the artistic side of Busan through travel?
 From contemporary art to digital media, exhibition spaces across the city present art in a variety of ways. Exploring these exhibitions offers an escape from daily life and invites you to pause and reflect.
 Looking for a sense of calm? Let art lead the way as you stroll through Busan’s exhibition spaces.

Museum of Contemporary Art Busan
 
Kim Chae-rin, 27 Voices of One, 2025, Mixed media, 95 × 95 × 110 cm, Supported by the Museum of Contemporary Art Busan, Collaborators - Sound: Seo Hye-min, Text: Hong Seung-taek, Video: Kim Yong-hyeon, Consultant: Lee Seong-su, Production Assistance: Park Hyeong-jo
 
Located in Eulsukdo Island, the Museum of Contemporary Art Busan is a special space where nature and art coexist in harmony. Since its opening in 2018, the museum has captivated visitors with its unique architecture that blends seamlessly with the surrounding landscape.
 
 Wrapping around the building’s exterior is a lush green installation—Vertical Garden by French botanist and artist Patrick Blanc. This living artwork was created to commemorate the museum’s opening and continues to breathe life into the space.
Ten Eyes

The Museum of Contemporary Art Busan presents a wide range of contemporary works, including painting, sculpture, installation, and media art. It features exhibitions by both Korean and international artists, offering a vibrant and diverse program. During major international events such as the Biennale, visitors get a chance to experience artworks by globally renowned artists all in one place.
(Left) Hilma af Klint, No. 7, Adulthood, Group IV, one of ten large paintings, 1907
 Tempera on paper mounted on canvas, 315 × 235 cm. Courtesy of the Hilma af Klint Foundation, HaK 108
 (Right) Hilma af Klint, No. 1, The Swan, Group IX, Part I, SUW series, 1914–1915, Oil on canvas, 150 × 150 cm. Courtesy of the Hilma af Klint Foundation, HaK 149

Since late July 2025, the museum has been hosting Proper Summons, an exhibition by Hilma af Klint, a pioneer of abstract art, offering visitors a deeper and more thought-provoking encounter with the world of art.
 
 In addition to exhibitions, a variety of educational programs are available, making it an ideal destination for families. With interactive spaces for children, a library, and docent-led tours, the museum invites visitors of all ages to enjoy art at their own pace.
(Photo Credit: Museum of Contemporary Art Busan)

Busan Museum of Art

Space Lee Ufan, Exterior View
 
Located near Centum City in Haeundae, the Busan Museum of Art has served as a leading public art museum at the heart of Busan’s contemporary art scene since its opening in 1998.  Blending urban sensibilities with artistic depth, the museum has continually evolved as a cultural platform connecting citizens with art and bridging the local and the global.
(Left) Lee Ufan, Discussion, 2013, Steel plate, basalt
 (Right) Lee Ufan, Relatum – Inside Outside, 2016, Stainless steel plate, natural stone
 
The museum features spacious, comfortable galleries that host year-round exhibitions across a wide range of genres, including painting, sculpture, photography, and media art.
 It also offers an inviting environment for all visitors, with an outdoor sculpture garden, a children's gallery, and a library—making it easy to engage with art at your own pace.
(Left) Lee Ufan, Relatum – Narrow Gate, 2015, Steel plate, natural stone
 (Right) Lee Ufan, Dialogue, 2015, Canvas, natural stone
 
While the main building of the Busan Museum of Art is currently undergoing renovation, the Space Lee Ufan located in the annex is well worth a visit.
 Dedicated to renowned Korean contemporary artist Lee Ufan—celebrated for his philosophy of “the art of relationships”—this tranquil space offers a refined setting to experience his work. Multilingual audio guides (Korean, English, Japanese, and Chinese) are available, making it a popular destination for both local and international visitors.
 
 Currently on view are the exhibitions Collection 99.999 and The Beginning of Busan Art, which highlight the museum’s collection and the origins of the local art scene. These exhibitions offer a valuable opportunity to understand the evolution of Busan’s art and its cultural significance.
(Photo Credit: Busan Museum of Art)

Busan Museum of Art
Address : 58, APEC-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
 Opening Hours : Tuesday–Sunday 10:00–18:00 (Last admission: 17:30)
Closing Days  : Mondays (Closed on the following Tuesday if Monday is a public holiday), January 1
Website : https://art.busan.go.kr/

Directions: 5-minute walk from Exit 5 of BEXCO (Busan Museum of Art) Station, Busan Metro Line 2
Inquiries : +82-51-744-2602
Please Note : The main building is temporarily closed for renovation.

Gallery Playlist

Located in Jung-gu, Gallery Playlist is a private gallery dedicated to showcasing bold and experimental contemporary art. Though small in scale, it continues to draw attention with exhibitions featuring fresh perspectives from emerging artists—and offers an experience that feels anything but small.
An artist introduction and guestbook at the entrance offer a thoughtful starting point, guiding visitors into a more meaningful experience with the artworks.
Gallery Playlist presents a diverse range of exhibitions including painting, photography, installation, and sculpture, offering thoughtful insight into the work of emerging Korean artists.
 
 One of its recent exhibitions, The Quiet Grain of Objects, reflects the gallery’s continued exploration of themes such as materiality, time, and sensory experience. Through such exhibitions, Gallery Playlist has established itself not just as a place for viewing art, but as a quiet, contemplative space for emotional resonance.
 
 Starting August 2, the exhibition The Moment Between will showcase works that visually explore the subtle sensations of “in-between” moments, each captured through the unique perspective of the participating artists.
 
 Gallery Playlist also actively participates in international exhibitions such as the NADA Art Fair in New York, serving as an important bridge that connects Busan’s artistic vision and emerging talents with the global stage.
 If you're looking for a small, thoughtful art space in the heart of the city during your travels, this might just be the perfect place to slow down and take a closer look.
(Photo Credit: Gallery Playlist)

Gallery Playlist)
Address : 3, Daecheong-ro 138beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan
Opening Hours : Wednesday–Saturday 11:00–18:00
Closing Days : Sunday, Monday, Tuesday
Website : https://www.instagram.com/galleryplaylist
Directions : 5-minute walk from Exit 5 of Jungang Station, Busan Metro Line 1
 Inquiries : +82-70-8287-2259

ARTE MUSEUM BUSAN

Located in Yeongdo, ARTE MUSEUM BUSAN is an immersive media art exhibition space that reinterprets the sensory beauty of nature through cutting-edge digital technology. Following its openings in Jeju, Yeosu, and Gangneung, this is the fourth ARTE MUSEUM in Korea and the largest one in the world.
Planned by d’strict, a digital design group, this exhibition explores the theme of ETERNAL NATURE, presenting media artworks that engage the senses through light, sound, and scent.
Signature works include CIRCLE, with endlessly flowing golden sand; WATERFALL INFINITE, a seven-meter-high digital cascade; and STARRY BUSAN, capturing the city’s nightscape and mood. These immersive pieces stimulate all five senses—not only sight and sound, but also smell and touch. In particular, STARRY BUSAN offers a uniquely local experience, blending music, media, and spatial design to express the identity of Busan as a port city.
Currently on view is the special exhibition ARTE MUSEUM: PINK MOON, celebrating the museum’s milestone of 10 million visitors. PINK MOON symbolizes both gratitude and a new beginning, marking the first step forward after reaching this major achievement. Don't miss this limited-time experience, on view through December 12.
(Photo Credit: ARTE MUSEUM)

ARTE MUSEUM
Address : 29, Haeyang-ro 247beon-gil, Yeongdo-gu, Busan
Opening Hours : Daily 10:00–20:00 (Last admission: 19:00)
