records.name: A Summer Day Trip to Yeongdo: Busan’s most underrated Island
records.originalName: 8월 어권특화 영문_여름날의 영도 당일치기 여행: 숨겨진 보석 같은 섬
records.description:
I’ve been to Busan more than 25 times - and every single visit surprises me in the best way. Just when I think I’ve seen it all, this city throws something new at me. On my most recent trip, I decided to skip the usual hot spots like Haeundae and Gamcheon and spend a full summer day exploring Yeongdo, the quiet little island just across the bridge from the bustling city center.

Most people know Yeongdo for Taejongdae, the dramatic cliffs and iconic lighthouse, or for Huinnyeoul Culture Village with its coastal alleys and artsy vibes. But this time, I wanted something different - less touristy, more relaxed, and a little off the radar.
Here’s how my perfect Yeongdo day went.
First stop: Yeongdo Sky Observatory
 
Tucked away on the southern edge of the island, the Yeongdo Sky Observatory doesn’t always make it onto the typical tourist trail - but it really should. 
A glass-floored skywalk juts out over the sea, giving you panoramic views of the coastline and the glittering water below. It’s a peaceful spot, even in the summer, with just the sound of waves and the occasional seagull overhead.
Right next to the observatory, I found a scenic walking path that winds down toward the water. The path leads to a hidden little beach - quiet, clean, and perfect for dipping your feet in or just sitting on the rocks to enjoy the breeze. It felt like I had stumbled across my own private seaside corner of Busan.Yeongdo Sky Observatory
Address : 321 Jeoryeong‑ro, Dong Sam‑dong, Yeongdo‑gu, Busan
Transportation : Walkable via Jeoryeong coastal trail (Haerang‑Gil); reachable by city tour bus via Yeongdo Haneul Park stop
Hours : Open year‑round, 24/7

Relaxation & Adrenaline at one place: Thrill on the Mug Café & Taejongdae Zipline
 
After soaking up the ocean air, I headed to the Thrill on the Mug Café - a spot that’s been getting some buzz lately on social media, and for a good reason. First of all, the view: floor-to-ceiling windows looking out over the open sea, with cozy seating and some seriously photogenic drinks. Apparently they also hold live music events there in the evenings!
But the best part? There’s a zipline right on top of the café! So you can not just sip your iced Americano, snap a few pictures for Instagram, but then also gear up and fly across the water. It’s a short ride but such a fun little adrenaline rush - and the contrast between the calm vibes of the café and the thrill of the zipline makes it a must-try combo. 
Thrill on the Mug Café & Taejongdae Zipline
Address : 55 Haeyang healing‑ro, Yeongdo‑gu, Busan
Transportation : From Nampo Station (Line 1), transfer to Bus 8, 30 or 17 at Yeongdodaegyo, then a ~22‑minute walk to the park. Parking available
Hours : Zipline operation daily 09:00-18:00 & Café operation daily 10:00-21:30
Website : Taejongdae Ocean Flying Theme Park operator

A quiet moment at Bokcheonsa Temple
 
Mid-afternoon, I wanted a change of pace, so I visited Bokcheonsa, a small temple tucked into the hills of Yeongdo.

It’s the kind of place that doesn’t try to impress.. but it still leaves such a memorable impression in the end. Surrounded by trees and soft mountain air, the temple grounds have a gentle atmosphere, with little dogs padding around and monks occasionally passing through.
One of the best photo spots at the higher end of the Temple Grounds overlooks the rooftops, ocean and city beyond - especially stunning around sunset, but honestly, it’s beautiful any time of day. Just remember, Bokcheonsa is a sacred space, so be mindful during your visit: speak quietly, dress modestly, and take a moment to simply enjoy the stillness of it. Bokcheonsa Temple
Address : 41 Sanjeong‑gil, Yeongdo‑gu, Busan
Transportation : From Nampo Station (Line 1), transfer to bus 82 or 85 at Yeongdodaegyo‑Nampo Station, alight at Shinseon Middle School stop and walk ~16 min. Taxi recommended uphill
Hours : Open 24 hours year‑round (popular sunset viewpoint but no fixed closing time)
Website : Bokcheonsa Temple

Sunset Streetfood on Yeongdo’s Pojangmacha Street
 
As the sun began to dip, I made my way to one of my favorite discoveries of the day: Yeongdo’s Pojangmacha Street.
It runs along the harbor with a perfect view of the Busan Tower in the distance. Just as the sky turned orange, I grabbed one of the famous red plastic stools at one of the street tents, ordered some grilled squid and clams - and some soju - and watched the boats drift by.
The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and very local. Groups of university friends were laughing over spicy tteokbokki, older couples sipped makgeolli, and the smell of sizzling seafood made it impossible not to order just one more dish or try to chat with the local ahjummas and ahjussis struggling to understand the strong Busan dialect. Loved every second of it!Yeongdo’s Pojangmacha Street
Address : 42, Bongnaenaru-ro, Yeongdo-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
Transportation : Located along the Yeongdo harbourfront; best reached via Yeongdodaegyo bridge, by bus or taxi from Busan Station
Hours : Typically active from spring through fall, evening until late night (exact hours depend on individual stalls; generally from 17:30)

Final Thoughts
 
Yeongdo might not be the first place that comes to mind when planning a trip to Busan, but that’s exactly what makes it so special. While most visitors rush to the more famous sights, this quiet island offers a different kind of summer magic: peaceful temples, ocean views without the crowds, unexpected thrills, and sunset Streetfood by the harbor.
So if you’re craving a day that feels both refreshing and a little undiscovered: let Yeongdo surprise you. It certainly surprised me and somehow - after all my previous trips to Busan - it still managed to show me something new that made me fall in love with Busan even more.

records.name: Exclusive Events Await in Gwangalli This August
records.originalName: 8월 적시성콘텐츠_8월 광안리에서만 즐길 수 있는 특별한 이벤트
records.address: 219, Gwanganhaebyeon-ro, Suyeong-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
records.description:
Friends Tour IN Gwangalli—Gwangalli Meets Kakao Friends
 
Cute characters everywhere in Busan’s Gwangalli Beach. Hosted by Kakao Entertainment, the “Friends Tour IN Gwangalli” exhibition has been underway here since July 5 and continues until August 31. Set against the stunning backdrop of the ocean and Gwangandaegyo Bridge, this unique experience created by Kakao Friends characters such as Ryan, Choonsik, and Apeach will be a treat for all visitors.
The first thing to catch your eye on the beach is a 6.5-meter-tall Ryan sculpture. You’ll find many photo spots featuring Choonsik on a paddleboard, Kakao Friends figures, and Apeach relaxing by the sea. The exhibition is free to enjoy, and people line up to take photos and have a great time. After sunset, the glowing Gwangandaegyo Bridge and character displays illuminate the night, creating magical moments and picture-perfect scenes.
Alongside the exhibition, the “Choonsik Tour” city tour program will also be a memorable experience. Hop on a Choonsik-themed bus at Busan Station and explore major attractions such as Gwangalli, Dongbaekseom Island, Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, and Songdo Beach. The tour also includes an exclusive guidebook and limited-edition souvenir, making it a perfect keepsake.
“Friends Tour IN Gwangalli” is more than just an exhibition—it's a summer festival at the seaside destination, featuring beloved characters. Strolling along Gwangalli Beach with Kakao Friends, you’ll discover a whole new joy in your journey.
Friends Tour IN Gwangalli
Location : In front of Universal Deck Road, Gwangalli Beach 
Dates : July 5 – August 31

Millac Ocean Cinema, an open-air cinema where waves and lights set the stage

By day, Gwangalli shimmers with blue waves; by night, the lights of Gwangandaegyo Bridge transform the sea into something new. Amid this stunning scenery, a special stage comes to life—Millac Ocean Cinema.
Millak Waterside Park is a popular retreat for both locals and travelers, and from August to December, it transforms into a small open-air cinema every Friday and Saturday night. Unlike indoor theaters, this venue offers an entirely different atmosphere—waves create a gentle soundtrack, and the sea breeze adds its own special effects. Beyond the screen, the gleaming lights of Gwangandaegyo Bridge become part of the backdrop and draw the audience deeper into the story. Here, the sea, the films, and the people come together to create living scenes, turning the park itself into a cultural experience.
Millac Ocean Cinema offers more than just scenic views. Tickets are only 3,000 KRW per person, and with a receipt of 15,000 KRW or more from a restaurant or café in Suyeong-gu, the fee is fully refunded. Here, visitors can enjoy movies alongside Busan’s local flavors and atmosphere, while supporting the vitality of the community.
The coastal hub always offers something new, but Millac Ocean Cinema promises some of the most unforgettable moments by the sea. If you’re visiting the city, make sure this cozy seaside theater is on your list. A night where the waves, lights, and films blend into one will linger in your heart long after the trip is over.
Millac Ocean Cinema
Location : Millak Waterside Park, Gate 3, Shade Rest Area 2 
Hours : Every Friday & Saturday, 8:00 PM
Admission : KRW 3,000 per person
(Full refund with a receipt of KRW 15,000 or more spent at restaurants/cafés in Suyeong-gu)
Reservation : Via profile link on Instagram@suyeongcc or https://zrr.kr/7raHvA

Gwangalli M Drone Light Show—Busan's Shining Nights Over the Sea

Every Saturday night, Gwangalli Beach comes alive with dazzling lights. Thousands of drones paint brilliant patterns across the sky, blending with the sea to create a breathtaking spectacle. The performance can be enjoyed from anywhere along the beach—even while strolling—making it a favorite attraction for countless visitors.
The “M” in the Gwangalli M Drone Light Show stands for "Marvelous." With thousands of drones powered by the latest technology, the night sky above Gwangandaegyo Bridge transforms into a stage for three-dimensional arrangements and messages. Each formation unfolds like a scene from a story, as the sky becomes a vast canvas and the lights reflected on the sea turn the entire beach into a dreamlike space. Visitors capture photos and videos to hold on to these unforgettable moments.
On special occasions, up to 2,500 drones light up the sky. During Seollal and Chuseok holidays, traditional patterns and festive motifs take shape, while the year-end countdown celebrates the New Year with dazzling lights. Each display is newly designed, ensuring a fresh and exciting experience for visitors every time.
The magic lingers long after the demonstration ends. With the cool sea breeze and the sound of waves etched in memory, visitors can lose themselves for a moment in the nightscape where the sky, sea, and city come together. Suitable for all ages, the Gwangalli M Drone Light Show is perfect for family, friends, and couples alike, offering a night of wonder you can only experience in Busan.
Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
Location : Gwangalli Beach 
Showtimes : March–September: 8:00 PM, 10:00 PM / October–February: 7:00 PM, 9:00 PM
* Schedule may change due to weather conditions.

Gwangalli’s Car-Free Cultural Street—Alive with Performances and Experiences
 
In Gwangalli, the streets transform into a no-car zone during certain hours each week. Roads once busy with traffic become pedestrian-only, creating a safe and open space where everyone can walk freely and enjoy the atmosphere.

records.name: Beyond Sun, Sand, and Sea: Busan’s Overlooked History
records.address:
Dongnae Eupseong Fortress: San 48-2, Myeongnyun-dong, Dongnae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
Bokcheon Museum: 63, Bokcheon-ro, Dongnae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
Chungnyeolsa Shrine: 347, Chungnyeol-daero, Dongnae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
1934 Train Dongnae Station: 28, Nangmin-ro, Dongnae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea
records.description:
When people think of Busan, beaches usually come first. And fair enough—they’re perfect. But that also means most itineraries stick to the coastline. Head inland though, and Busan hides historical surprises that break the sun-sand-sea routine. Join me in Dongnae District, where I’ll zoom in on four sites that deserve a spot on any Busan itinerary.

Dongnae Eupseong Fortress: A Final Stand
 
The world remembers Hastings, Waterloo, Normandy, and Stalingrad. Busan remembers the Battle of Dongnae Eupseong. This fortress was the stage for one of Korea’s fiercest fights during the Imjin Wars.

In 1592, 4,000 Korean defenders under Magistrate Song Sang-hyeon faced nearly 20,000 Japanese soldiers. Refusing to surrender, Song and his men held out against impossible odds until the fortress fell. Song himself was killed in battle, leaving behind the words he’s remembered for: “It is easier to die in battle than to surrender.”
Today, you can walk the fortress walls in peace and imagine their final stand.

We entered through the northern gate, where a forest trail hugs the old wall under the shade of pines. The breeze was a welcome relief from Busan’s lingering September heat. The path climbs to Bukjangdae Pavilion, the highest point of the fortress, with sweeping views of the city. Standing there, it wasn’t hard to picture Japanese soldiers storming these walls centuries ago.

On the way back, we stopped at the small history hall, where a giant miniature of the fortress reveals just how vast it once was. After a slightly embarrassing attempt at Tuho—an old Korean throwing game you can play outside of the hall—we decided it was time for a cooling retreat.

Dongnae Eupseong Fortress
Address : San 48-2, Myeongnyun-dong, Dongnae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea 
Transportation : About a 24-minute walk from Myeongnyun Station (Busan Metro Line 1, exit 2); or take village bus 183 or Dongnae-gu 7 to Dongnae Cultural Center stop, then walk ~9 minutes.

Hours : Open Tuesday-Sunday, from 09:00 to 18:00; closed on Mondays.

Bokcheon Museum and Ancient Gaya Tombs
 
Right by the fortress gate sits a museum that caught me completely off guard. I expected fortress relics, but instead I found gold crowns, iron armor, and pottery unearthed from the tombs of the ancient Gaya people.

Gaya was a confederation of small kingdoms—masters of iron tools and weapons—and one of the great underdogs of Korean history. The exhibitions, with clear English explanations, do a great job telling their story. Some of the jewelry they created was so stunning and timeless that it could have been worn today, and no one would have guessed its antiquity. I was impressed!

But the real thrill is outside. In front of the museum, green hills dotted with square-shaped bushes hide the very tombs where some of these treasures were found. During the Korean War, refugee migration to Busan led to homes being built directly on top of them. Only during redevelopment were the tombs uncovered. The walk along the tombs gave a magnificent panoramic view over the Dongnae District.

Bokcheon Museum
Address : 63, Bokcheon-ro, Dongnae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea 
Transportation : By Metro: Walk about 18 minutes from Exit 5 of Suan Station (Busan Metro Line 4) to the museum.
By Bus: Take village bus Dongnae-gu No. 6, get off at the Bokcheon Museum stop.
From Dongnae Station (Line 1), walk or switch to bus No. 6, as the museum is in the same general area.
Hours : Open Tuesday–Sunday, from 09:00 to 18:00 (last admission at 17:00). Closed on Mondays and January 1. 
Admission : Free 
Website : https://museum.busan.go.kr/bokcheon/index 

Chungnyeolsa Shrine: Heroes Remembered
 
Shrines don’t usually make the top of Busan’s travel lists, but Chungnyeolsa deserves an exception. About a 25-minute walk from the fortress, it honors those who died resisting the Japanese during the Imjin War.

We took the western path to the main hall, which felt almost botanical, dozens of unique trees swaying in the wind, locals resting in the shade. Honestly, I was intrigued by all the different trees. Halfway up, the path split in two: one shortcut to the hall, the other a so-called “foot massage path.” I bravely chose the latter, and instantly regretted it as my feet protested with every sharp stone. Healing turned into torture, but at least I earned my way to the shrine.

At the main hall, the view over the city was striking, but what moved me most was watching locals pause to bow in respect. After visiting the fortress, the weight of those lost lives felt heavier here. 

I even came across a smaller shrine dedicated to women fighters, which is a rare sight. It reminded me of a painting I saw earlier at the fortress, depicting two women hurling roof tiles at Japanese soldiers during the battle. I immediately noticed them on the roof in the painting, which quickly became my favorite Korean battle scene. Standing in front of their shrine made that image feel suddenly real. 

Inside the memorial hall, large painted depictions of the battle line the walls. Commissioned in the 1980s, they’re romanticized but still powerful. A kind local guide explained (in English) that the actual battle lasted only a few hours, given how outnumbered the Koreans were—pointing out that these paintings aren’t the most realistic portrayals. I was still impressed, though.

I would have kicked myself if I had skipped this stop. Chungnyeolsa won my heart; it felt like the perfect finishing touch to the story of Eupseong Fortress… or so I thought.

Chungnyeolsa Shrine
Address : 347, Chungnyeol-daero, Dongnae-gu, Busan, Republic of Korea 
Transportation : Accessible via Chungnyeolsa Station on Metro Line 4 
Hours : April through September: 09:00–21:00; October through March: 09:00–20:00; Main hall/souvenir shop: 09:00–18:00 year-round 
Admission : Free 
Website : http://www.busan.go.kr/cys/index

records.name: Festival Shiwol - Busan’s Ultimate Celebration of Art, Culture, and Fun
records.description:
The autumn season has begun, and that means the beautiful city of Busan is all set to welcome locals and foreigners to the most exciting festival of the year - Festival Shiwol. People often say that ‘Busan is Good’ and this festival proves it, and that’s why there was no way I could miss it. I had the privilege and honor of seeing the city transform into a serene playground of vibrancy mixed with culture and immense creativity. 
The popular autumn festival will run from September 21st to October 3rd, and it was amazing to see all of Busan’s most coveted exhibitions and convention projects unite under one platform. As a whole, I got the chance to dive into an enchanting Busan experience while networking with leading professionals in the industry. This is the festival’s second year running, and it certainly went beyond my expectations of putting Busan out there as a cultural hub. 
This year, Festival Shiwol expanded to include up to 26 fun-filled festivals that spread across 10 different sectors. I saw some breathtaking exhibits related to art, architecture, music, technology, food, culture, film, business, and more. Every program expanded across Busan brought an aura of celebration throughout the whole coastal city. 

Even though every program and event of Festival Shiwol can’t be missed, I’ve picked 4 of my absolute favorites this year. So buckle up and fasten your seat belt (if you have one), and let me take you on a little journey through Festival Shiwol.

Busan International Architecture Festival
 
The Busan International Architecture Festival was a treat for the senses, especially for someone like me who adores seeing dream design projects come to life. This was the biggest architectural event to take place in Busan. As I made my way into the grand BEXCO, it was inspiring to see how many fun-filled activities I could participate in. This included design workshops to enhance skills and even a design competition to showcase talent. But that was just the start. 
I was introduced to the work of some of the city’s finest architects. Their physical models stood beautifully on table tops while their dream visions were laid out. This gave me a sense of how much creativity and talent the people of Busan hold, including the determination to put the city on the global map of leaders in this field. 

Other than physical models, I went through architectural displays in the form of pictures, sketches, and intricately detailed architectural plans. It was brilliant to see the addition of interactive installations that really gave a sense of what the final product would look like. Then came the chance to witness immersive virtual environments. There were even some grand projects where I could actually touch or stand inside the real buildings. 
I was educated about various forms of architecture, and that fostered discussions about the impact these can have on Korean culture, society, and daily life. It was also interesting to see an emphasis on contemporary issues that we’re facing in today’s world, like sustainability and the development of urban areas. I was intrigued by the unique modern styles in use today as well as the creative solutions offered to overcome architectural challenges. The fact that I could personally engage with the unique architectural concepts really created that special immersive charm.

Busan Craft Beer Masters Challenge: Local craft beer brands all in one place
 
As I made my way to the BEXCO outdoor plaza for another highlight from the Shiwol Festival, I was treated to the Busan Craft Beer Masters Challenge. The event that expanded five days featured the city’s best local produce for beer. While I don’t personally drink, it was still wonderful to see how competitive the industry is in terms of local produce for this popular beverage. 
Businesses really went the extra mile to compete against one another and enhance sales channels, especially those working on a small scale. Beer has slowly become a popular drink in Korea, especially during celebratory events. And this event celebrates just that.

Since its launch in 2018, each year is known for having a certain theme, and this time around, it was related to the Festival of October. This means you don’t only enjoy beer but also a great mix of food and vast cultural experiences. 
As I walked into the main event, I was excited to see how lively the exhibition was. After the opening ceremony, there was a craft beer evaluation contest that took place. This showcased the talent of businesses that have made a mark in the food and drink industry. Other than that, I witnessed a pop-up beer zone which featured up to ten different breweries. 

I was enchanted by how they were giving citizens the chance to participate as a judge for the competition. This meant they not only could sample but also vote for the beer that they felt was the best to help ensure a deserving brand wins the top prize of being a noteworthy craft brew. Depending on the opinions of the public and expert judge evaluations, a winner was selected. 
As I strolled across the venue, I saw some exciting side programs taking place where small businesses put up stands to display their unique offerings. There were some scrumptious desserts, fun quiz competitions related to beer, and even workshops to help you design a great beer label. I stopped by some lifestyle activity challenges to try my luck, and while I may not have won, it felt great to participate. 

2025 K-Drone to World Festival: a night sky filled with creative drone performances
 
South Korea’s advanced drone tech is second to none, and I personally got the honor of witnessing that live during the Shiwol Festival this year. Held at the North Port Waterfront Park, the K-Drone to World Festival lit up the sky with the most incredible drone performances. I would best describe this as an event packed with fun, excitement, and a complete thrill for the senses. 
The mesmerizing LED-equipped drones gave rise to some of the most unique and dynamic patterns in the sky, including some unforgettable animations. The festival’s highlight for me had to be the stellar and dazzling fireworks drone spectacle. Words fail me to describe the experience of the night sky lighting up in that manner. 
This year’s event theme was Journey Toward Hope. As I looked around, the crowds were just as speechless as me to witness something of this magnitude and greatness live. It’s safe to say that this was a breath of fresh air to see a peaceful and more eco-friendly variant to the classic fireworks display. 

As I sit down to write this article and look back on my time at the Festival Shiwol, I can truly say it was one of the most unforgettable experiences I’ve had in Korea. From the vibrant performances to the diverse cultural events, and the way the entire city happened to come alive, every moment carried something special. What impressed me the most was how beautifully the festival captured the essence of autumn. It felt like the perfect way to welcome the season. 

Creativity shining at the Emerging Artists Art Show, imagination taking shape at the Busan International Architecture Festival, celebration everywhere at the Busan Craft Beer Masters Challenge, and reflection in the skies with the K-Drone to World Festival, every festival was simply superb and I loved every second of it. For me, it stands as the best autumn festival I’ve ever attended. 

Above all, more than just an event, it gave me lasting memories and a deep sense of connection to the city of Busan. So yes, Festival Shiwol made me realize why people love saying “Busan is good.”

records.name: If You Haven’t Walked Refugee Busan, You Haven’t Seen Busan
records.originalName: 10월 어권특화 영문_If You Haven’t Walked Refugee Busan, You Haven’t Seen Busan
records.description:
Busan isn’t just good, it’s a city with soul. A soul shaped by refugees who fled here during the Korean War, making this coastal city their last safe haven. Out of their struggles grew the hillside neighborhoods, the foods, and the culture that still define Busan today. Most visitors come for the skyline and the sea, but I promise you’ll fall for the city even more once you follow the footsteps of those refugees. Just like I did. From a village built on tombstones to a simple bowl of milmyeon, their legacy is still everywhere. Let me show you a few unforgettable places that tell this story.
Ami-dong Tombstone Culture Village

For our first stop we followed a narrow winding road into the valley of Ami Mountain. The colorful houses reminded us of Gamcheon Culture Village, but something felt different. The green village bus rattled by, picking up elderly residents and dropping them at their destinations. Then we spotted the sign: Ami-dong Tombstone Culture Village. That’s how we knew we had arrived—at the very place where refugees finished their long journey south.
The first time I heard of a “tombstone village” I couldn’t quite believe it. But here it was. The first house we saw was wrapped in a protective plastic wall, and underneath its foundation were stones that stood out from the rest. They weren’t just stones—they were tombstones. Yes, the house was literally built on top of them.
Ami-dong had been a Japanese cemetery. After Korea’s liberation from Imperial Japan, the site was abandoned. When refugees poured into Busan, they had nowhere else to go, so they built homes on top of the graves. They used whatever they could find, including gravestones and stone markers. Out of desperation, a neighborhood was born.
Even though a walking route is mapped out for tourists, the real fun is wandering aimlessly through the alleys. The real real fun? Spotting tombstones hidden in walls and floors. At first it’s tricky, but soon your eye sharpens—you’ll find some carved, some painted over, others still inscribed with Japanese characters. Many original residents still live here. In other homes, now vacant, visitors can peek inside and imagine how refugees survived in tiny rooms for decades. It’s a sobering reminder of the past, but also proof that Busan’s hillside refugee villages have become some of its most charming neighborhoods. This is hands down in my top five Busan activities.
Ami-dong Tombstone Culture Village
Address : 49, Ami-ro, Seo-gu, Busan.
Transportation : 
Walk from Toseong Station (Busan Metro Line 1, Exit 8): about 15–18 minutes on foot. 
Village Bus: Take either Saha‑gu 1‑1 or Seo‑gu 2, get off at Sansang Church (Tombstone Culture Village), then a brief walk.
Hours : Open year-round, with no fixed opening hours—freely accessible at all times, and free admission.

Provisional Capital Memorial Hall: When Busan Became Korea’s Capital (for a While)
 
During the Korean War, it wasn’t only ordinary Koreans fleeing south. Government offices, the National Assembly—even President Syngman Rhee himself—were forced to evacuate to Busan. Overnight, the city became the Provisional Capital of Korea. The president moved into the former Gyeongsangnam-do Governor’s Residence, a place you can still visit today. Or so I thought. After leaving Ami-dong, I arrived to find the building wrapped in scaffolding, closed for renovation until December. But luck was on my side. Next door, part of the exhibition was still open.
Inside, a compact but surprisingly rich hall unfolded the refugee story in a way that was simple yet captivating. Displays showed where people settled, what they ate, how they kept schools open, even how they influenced Busan’s art scene. Old photos, drawings, and belongings made it all feel vivid and human. I was disappointed not to step into Syngman Rhee’s wartime office, but the exhibition tied the refugee story together from A to Z. And unlike some museums that lull you to sleep, here I actually read every panel—and wanted more.
And that’s where the food connection appeared: milmyeon. This beloved Busan noodle dish was born out of necessity. Buckwheat for naengmyeon was impossible to find, so wheat flour supplied by the U.S. military filled the gap. Out of hardship came a new comfort food. So if milmyeon isn’t on your Busan food list yet, trust me, it should be.
Provisional Capital Memorial Hall
Address : 45, Imsisudoginyeom‑ro, Seo‑gu, Busan.
Transportation : About a 6-minute walk from Toseong Station (Busan Metro Line 1), Exit 2.
Hours : 09:00 – 18:00, Tuesday to Sunday.
Closed: Mondays (or the following day if Monday is a public holiday); also closed on January 1.

Yeongnam Naengmyeon Milmyeon: A Refugee’s Delicacy
 
After some online searching, we ended up at Yeongnam Naengmyeon Milmyeon, a decades-old restaurant—always a good sign in Korea. Rain had drizzled on and off since morning, the perfect backdrop for a refugee story. My clothes were damp, but as a Dutchie I’ll never complain about rain. It just gave me the perfect excuse for lunch.
On the way, I kept thinking of the refugees. Back home in the North, their comfort dish was buckwheat naengmyeon. In Busan, with no buckwheat in sight, they turned to wheat flour and sweet potato starch. The result was milmyeon, Busan’s own noodle identity.
The staff greeted us with big smiles, a little surprised a foreigner had found their tucked-away spot. (Credit to my wife for that.) We ordered mul milmyeon (cold noodles in broth), bibim milmyeon (spicy cold noodles), and a plate of mandu.
And then—bang. The food arrived almost instantly. At first we thought it was wartime reflexes lingering on, but no—it’s just that popular. Customers streamed in nonstop, and the kitchen never slowed.
We split everything, trading spoonfuls of icy broth for bites of fiery noodles, dumplings disappearing in between. At some point, we stopped talking. The food said enough.
Yeongnam Naengmyeon Milmyeon
Address : 7, Bosu‑daero 201‑beon‑gil, Seo‑gu, Busan.
Transportation : Take Busan Metro Line 1 to Dongdaesin Station (Exit 1), then walk about 10 minutes toward Busan Girls’ High School—the restaurant is in the alley beside Samik Apartment.
Hours : Daily 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM. Closed in winter (approx. November to February); business resumes around March 1. No break time.

Huinnyeoul Culture Village: Korea’s Refugee Santorini

records.address: 63 Gurak-ro 141beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan

records.description:
Written and Photographed by Kim Hui-won, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators

If you’re looking for something a little different to see in Busan, KISWIRE Museum is worth a visit.
You might expect a museum devoted to wire, but the building itself is just as striking as the exhibits. 
Its design draws on the shapes and qualities of wire, inside and out, making it an interesting place to explore together on a date.
	

- A Building That Catches Your Eye

When I arrived at KISWIRE Museum, the first thing that caught my eye wasn’t the exhibition inside but the building’s exterior.
Steel and wire give it a modern, industrial look.
What sets this space apart is that it’s not simply a building that houses exhibits. Wire, one of KISWIRE’s key materials, plays a prominent role in the architectural design.
Walk around the building and you’ll notice how straight lines and curves work together. The heavy steel contrasts with the surrounding greenery, creating plenty of good spots for photos.
Before stepping inside, take a moment to see how the building works with its surroundings. It makes KISWIRE Museum feel quite different from a typical corporate exhibition hall. That transformation of wire from an industrial material into an architectural feature is part of what makes this museum so interesting.

- KISWIRE Exhibition Hall

Once inside, the first space you’ll encounter is the KISWIRE Exhibition Hall on the first floor. The exhibits introduce KISWIRE’s history and show how wire is used in everyday life.
The display on how wire supports buildings is particularly interesting. It explains that wire can hold up structures through tension rather than compression—a detail that may change the way you look at buildings you’d normally pass without a second thought.
You can also learn how KISWIRE’s technology was used in Gwangandaegyo Bridge, one of Busan’s most iconic landmarks. It’s an interesting glimpse into the connection between Busan and the wire industry.

- Wire Museum

On the second floor, the Wire Museum explores the history of wire, how it is made, and how it is used across different industries through videos, models, and kiosks. But the exhibits aren’t the only thing that catches your eye here: at the center of the space is a spiral steel staircase.
Its gently curving shape sets it apart from an ordinary staircase. Its curves seem to spiral upward, bringing the building’s structure and the image of wire together in a sculptural form.
The open space around the staircase makes the climb especially enjoyable. As you go up and look down, you get a clear view of the building’s interior. It’s a place to slow down and enjoy the architecture as well as the exhibits.
KISWIRE Museum isn’t particularly large, but there’s plenty to see, from the building’s exterior and interior staircase to the exhibition spaces, so I recommend taking your time to explore. If you’re interested in architecture or design, look beyond the exhibits and see how the building’s design draws on wire.

Q&A

Q. What other places can I visit near KISWIRE Museum in Busan?

F1963 is just nearby. After exploring KISWIRE Museum, stop by F1963 to visit its cafés and other cultural spaces! Together, they make a great day out for a date centered on art and culture in Busan.

records.name: Cinema Pop-up: Music On - An immersive festival that blurs the line between film and reality
records.address: Outdoor lawn (Forest of Imagination) at the Busan Cinema Center
records.hours: October 31 (Fri), November 1 (Sat), November 2 (Sun), November 7 (Fri), November 8 (Sat), November 9 (Sun)
records.description:
The heart of Korea's movie city, Busan, comes alive on the outdoor lawn of the Busan Cinema Center, where Cinema Pop-up: Music On is now in full swing.
Held over six days—October 31 to November 2 and November 7 to 9—Cinema Pop-up: Music On is an immersive festival that brings scenes from the screen into the real world. Visitors step right into the spotlight with a lineup of interactive experiences. The Game Zone, Photo Zone, Experience Zone, Food Zone, Market Zone, and an outdoor stage come together to create a lively, cinematic playground.

Game Zone
 
On the grassy lawn of the Busan Cinema Center, the Game Zone is where laughter and excitement never stop. It’s more than an entertainment area—it's a hands-on playground where you can literally step into the world of film. Complete and verify three or more game or photo-zone missions, finish a quick survey, and you’ll earn an adorable festival goodie.
Try your aim like a sniper from Assassination., pitch like the ace in The Perfect Game., or take on a mini-hoop challenge inspired by a scene from Rebound.
The “Movie MBTI Test” booth is also a crowd favorite, offering film recommendations tailored to your personality. And with the AR app Soomple, the lawn transforms into a treasure hunt—track down AR treasure chests, answer the quiz, and collect digital badges as you explore.

Movie Set Zone
 
Step beyond the screen and into the story at the Movie Set Zone—a space where iconic Korean films come to life through full-scale, hands-on sets. It’s an immersive experience that makes visitors feel as if they’ve stepped straight into the frame.
At the Train to Busan set, clear acrylic windows and a recreated train interior create the illusion of being onboard. During scheduled times, zombie performers appear, turning the scene into a pulse-pounding escape sequence. The photo spot inspired by the Badass Girl poster is also a hit. Stand where the lead character would be, and suddenly, you become Na Ae-ri. You can even walk into a courtroom from The Attorney, meticulously recreated to capture the film's atmosphere. Once inside, it feels as though you’re standing in the middle of one of its most powerful moments.

Experience Zone
 
In the Forest of Imagination, the Experience Zone offers six movie-themed programs. For 50 minutes, you step into the story yourself—an experience that just might become a scene you’ll never forget.

Film Screening (GV)
 
After the special screening of No Other Choice , film critic Lee Dong-jin will lead a GV session. When the 3:40 p.m. screening concludes, stick around for a relaxed conversation where you can dive deeper into the film and hear candid insights from behind the scenes.

Cinema Concert & Performance
 
On the outdoor stage, music and film merge seamlessly. Busking, Korean traditional music, and musical-theater performances unfold throughout the day, each creating its own unique atmosphere. Settle into your seat under the soft lights, let the movie music wash over you, and before long, you'll feel as if you’ve stepped into a scene of your own.

Food Zone
 
On one side of the Forest of Imagination, a row of food trucks fills the air with mouthwatering aromas. Burgers, tacos, hot dogs, croffles, coffee, desserts—there’s something for everyone, and the whole setup feels like a street scene straight out of a film. Wander around all day, and you’ll find that every path somehow leads you back here.

Market Zone
 
The Market Zone is where film and art come together. Each booth is filled with treasures that draw you in—handmade movie-inspired pieces, miniatures, beaded accessories, character keyrings, knotted bracelets, and more. With creations that glimmer like props from a film set, the Busan Cinema Center transforms into a vibrant arts market.
This isn’t just another festival—it’s a place where film and reality meet. Cinema Pop-up: Music On lets you step beyond the screen and experience it firsthand.
Join us this fall at the Busan Cinema Center for a cinematic moment you'll never forget.

records.description:
As night falls, Busan glows brighter – thanks to Starry Night spots in Busan!
﻿The Starry Night in Busan Venues are the first night-tourism–specialized spaces selected by the Busan Tourism Organization for 2025, showcasing the city’s unique character and its charm after dark.Let’s take a look at top 7 spots that make Busan sparkle brighter at night!

﻿Night-View Attractions

﻿Songjeong Jogaeholic

﻿Located right in front of Songjeong Beach, Jogae Holic is a popular spot specializing in grilled shellfish.
﻿Head up the stairs to the second floor and you will be greeted by a refreshing panoramic ocean view. The interior features wide floor-to-ceiling windows that create an open, airy atmosphere, while the outdoor terrace lets you enjoy the cool sea breeze along with Songjeong’s beautiful nightscape.
﻿Their signature Holic Special Grilled Shellfish is a must-try comes with fresh scallops, abalone, pen shells and more, all grilled over charcoal. They also offer side dishes such as fish-roe rice, ramen, and even pasta. Thanks to the staff’s warm and attentive service, you can enjoy your meal comfortably from start to finish.
﻿The spacious interior and group seating make it convenient for larger parties and parking is available for easy access.
﻿If you want to savour freshly grilled shellfish with a sweeping view of Songjeong Beach, Jogae Holic is a must-visit while you are in Busan!
﻿Songjeong Jogaeholic
Address : 2F, 50 Songjeonghaebyeon-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Operating Days and Hours : Sunday-Thursday 12:00-24:00, Friday-Saturday 12:00-02:00
Closing Days : Open All Year Round 
Website : @jogaeholic
Transportation : From Exit 2 of Songjeong Station (Busan Donghae Line) →17-minute walk 
Inquiries : +82-507-1367-8480

﻿Caelrium

﻿Caelrium, a massive multi-cultural complex in Mandeok-dong, lives up to its name: “a place where the sky meets emotion.” With its wide-open mountain views, the venue offers coffee, baked goods, brunch by day and live jazz performances in the evening.
﻿Located above the Mandeok Tunnel, Caelrium stands out with an exterior reminiscent of the Colosseum.The view through its expansive windows is striking, especially as night falls and the indoor lighting softens, creating a cozy atmosphere paired with smooth jazz.
﻿The jazz pub on the 4th floor hosts regular live performances. The intimate distance between the stage and the audience allows you to enjoy a rich, immersive sound, alongside simple dishes like gorgonzola pizza or gambas.
﻿By day, Caelrium serves as a brunch café; by night, it transforms into a full-fledged jazz venue.
﻿It’s the perfect place to end your day—enjoying music, night views and a cool evening breeze.Be sure to visit Caelrium for a memorable night in Busan.
﻿Caelrium
Address : 97 Jungni-ro, Buk-gu, Busan
Operating Days and Hours : Caelrium Cafe : Monday-Sunday 09:30-24:00, Cael Lounge Restaurant : Monday-Friday 10:30-20:30, Saturday-Sunday 10:30-21:00 (Break 14:00-17:00)
Closing Days : Open All Year Round 
Website : @caelrium_official
Transportation : From Exit 2 of Mandeok Station (Busan Metro Line 3), transfer to Bus No. 46 or 33-1 at the Mandeokgyocharo stop → Get off at the Seokbulsa Entrance stop and walk for 5 minutes
Inquiries : +82-507-1303-0105

﻿TANTI

﻿Located near Dallamsan in Jeonggwan, TANTI is a massive bakery café spanning over 6,6 00 square meters, perfectly blending delicious drinks, freshly baked pastries and beautiful night scenery.
﻿Perched on higher ground, TANTI offers a sweeping view of Jeonggwan’s cityscape, which becomes even more captivating at night as the lights twinkle below. You can enjoy a peaceful cup of coffee accompanied by daily classical performances—another charming feature of this café. Performance schedules can be found on Naver or Instagram.
﻿The first and second floors serve as the main café area, the third floor offers private rooms and the fourth floor is designed as a cultural complex, giving visitors plenty of flexibility depending on their needs. With ample parking space, it’s an easy and convenient stop for those driving. Inside, TANTI features a modern white-toned interior, high ceilings and a spacious, airy feel.
﻿TANTI is especially famous for its bakery, offering more than 80 types of bread baked fresh every day. You can enjoy a wide range of pastries at reasonable prices, along with popular drinks such as their signature Black Sesame Milk Latte.
﻿If you’re looking to spend a special evening surrounded by classical music and the glow of Jeonggwan’s nightscape, TANTI is the perfect place.
﻿TANTI
Address : 37 Dareumsan-gil, Jeonggwan-eup, Gijang-gun, Busan 
Operating Days and Hours : Monday-Sunday 10:00-01:00
Closing Days : Open All Year Round 
Website : @tanti_daily
Transportation : From Dongwon Royal Duke 1-cha Apartment bus stop → 28-minute walk
Inquiries : +82-507-1317-6798

﻿Culture & Arts Attractions

﻿Yauchulchaek

﻿After riding the Ibagu-gil Monorail, Yauchulchaek is the ideal spot to stop by. A cozy book café offering a breathtaking view of Busan Port.
﻿Take a seat by the window and you will see the Busan Harbor Bridge and the city panorama spread out before you, making it a wonderful place to sip a quiet cup of coffee.
﻿Yauchulchaek is more than just a café; it also operates as an independent bookstore. You will find a curated selection of poetry collections, indie publications, and works by local authors. Throughout the space, handwritten notes, art pieces, and literary displays come together to create a charming atmosphere.
﻿The café’s biggest strength lies in its unique, community-driven programs. They regularly host handwriting gatherings, reading sessions, writing workshops and others interactive events where visitors can meet new people and enjoy conversations centered around books.
﻿Whether you want a quiet place for reflection or a warm spot to engage in thoughtful conversation, Yauchulchaek offers both.
﻿If you are seeking a slow and peaceful moment with the scenery of Busan as your backdrop, Yauchulchaek is highly recommended!
﻿Yauchulchaek
Address : 14 Yeongchowit-gil 26beon-gil, Dong-gu, Busan
Operating Days and Hours : Weekdays 12:00 - 18:30 / Weekends 10:00 - 20:00
Closing Days : Tuesdays and Wednesdays 
Website : @yauchulchaek
Transportation : From Exit 7 of Busan Station (Busan Metro Line 1) → 16-minute walk
Inquiries : +82-507-1427-7103

﻿Adapter Theater

﻿Adapter Theater is a small performance venue located right in front of Gwangalli Beach. 
﻿Located just steps away from Gwangalli Beach, Adapter Theater is a cozy venue where a wide range of performances. Especially stand-up comedy and small-scale plays—take place.

﻿The theater operates with two halls, Hall 1 and Hall 2. Although compact in size, the close distance between the performers and the audience creates an incredibly immersive experience.
﻿Many of the shows incorporate audience participation, making each performance feel fresh and unique. Stand-up comedy and improv theater are especially popular here, thanks to the actors’ quick wit, spontaneous reactions and lively energy that fill the room with laughter.

records.name: Shining Nights Await—Find Your Best Spot at the 2025 Busan Fireworks Festival!
records.description:
In November, Busan glows even brighter as night falls. The autumn breeze turns crisp and the night sky over Gwangalli is ready to burst into color.
Each fall, the Busan Fireworks Festival transforms the sea in front of Gwangandaegyo Bridge into a dazzling stage. This year, the show returns on Saturday evening, November 15, filling the sky with brilliant light and energy.
Now firmly rooted as a signature autumn event, the festival’s breathtaking fireworks feel like a grand finale to the year. Wherever you choose to watch—and whoever you watch with—this unforgettable night will spark pure excitement and awe.
Check out Visit Busan’s recommended viewing spots and find your own perfect place to enjoy the magic of the 2025 Busan Fireworks Festival.

1. Up Close and Unforgettable: The Official Viewing Seats

The official viewing area at the heart of Gwangalli Beach puts you right in the middle of the action, offering a front-row experience from the very first burst to the finale.
Here, the main show unfolds just steps away—music, lights, and fireworks blending into one seamless performance. With designated seating, it’s a safe and comfortable place to relax and enjoy the festival, making it especially popular with families and visitors from overseas.
With Gwangandaegyo Bridge right in front of you, the fireworks spreading across the sky feel even more spectacular. Their glow reflecting on the water brings an added sense of romance to Busan’s night. Each burst sets off waves of cheers, and the lights dancing across the sea turn the evening into something truly artistic—a night that feels like one sweeping open-air installation along the shore.

2. Make the Night Yours: Hotels & Restaurants with Fireworks Views

Image Source (Left) @hwt1987 (Right) @rayo._.film

If you’d like a quieter, more relaxed way to enjoy the festival, booking a hotel or restaurant with a fireworks view is a great option. Open your window and you’ll see Gwangandaegyo Bridge and the sea spread out in front of you, with each flare of fireworks filling the room with light.
Rooftop bars and ocean-view restaurants offer an easygoing way to watch the show—good food, a glass of wine, soft music, and fireworks rising across the sky.
The mix of the sea air, shimmering reflections on the water, and the excitement shared by everyone around you creates a setting that feels truly special, turning the place you stay into its own part of the celebration.
Fireworks-view rooms sell out early, so reserving at least six months ahead is recommended. Make sure to request a “fireworks view” when you book. For restaurants, check their social media or notices in advance to see if reservations are available.

3. A Different World at Sea: Fireworks from a Yacht

Image Source @chaniegraphy

If you want a truly memorable way to enjoy the festival, try watching the fireworks from a yacht out on the water. The moment you step aboard, the night view of Gwangandaegyo Bridge feels remarkably close, and every blaze of fireworks scatters across the surface like shimmering jewels.
With the ocean breeze on your face and the sound of the waves beneath you, the fireworks take on a whole new kind of magic, leaving a lasting impression.
Yacht operators have different prices and options, so check the details before booking. And since November nights can be quite cold, be sure to dress warmly.

4. Where City Lights Meet Fireworks: Busan’s Nightscape Spots

Hwangnyeongsan Beacon Fire Station, Jangsan Mountain, Geumnyeonsan Mountain, and Igidae Park all offer sweeping views of Gwangalli—perfect places to watch the city lights and fireworks blend into one stunning night scene.
From these viewpoints, the fireworks feel more like broad strokes of color across the sky, and the bursts over Gwangandaegyo Bridge sparkle against the city backdrop in a way no photo can truly capture.
If you'd rather avoid the crowded beach, these quieter hillsides are a calmer, more reflective way to enjoy the show.
Arrive early to avoid congestion on the way up, and make sure to bundle up as it gets chilly at night.
5. Joining the Festival from Afar: Online Live Broadcast

Even if you can’t be there in person, you can feel the same excitement from wherever you are. Busan’s official YouTube channel,  'Busan is good', will broadcast the entire show live.
The glow of Gwangalli, the reactions from the crowd, and the fireworks filling the night sky come through clearly on screen, bringing the festival’s energy to you wherever you are.
Whether you’re at home, at a café, or watching with friends, you can look up at the same night sky and share the moment together.

The 2025 Busan Fireworks Festival will take place on Saturday, November 15, along Gwangalli Beach under the theme “The Lights of Busan Blooming in the Sky.” This year’s fireworks aren’t just a performance—they’re a story shaped by the city, the people who gather, and the sky that holds it all.
Some will watch from the beach, others from a yacht, and many from places farther away. Wherever you find yourself that night, we hope the fireworks become a memory you’ll cherish in your own way. And with that, Busan’s autumn once again comes to life, finished in a glow of light.

records.description:
I’ve seen Busan in every season, but there is something about fall here that feels especially magical. The city, which is usually known for beaches, seafood and bright summer energy, suddenly grows soft during November. The air turns crisp, the mountains shift into layers of gold and red, and Buddhist temples seem to glow quietly under the autumn light.
On my most recent little solo day trip, I decided to spend a fall day around Geumjeongsan Mountain and Beomeosa Temple. And honestly, I think it was the most beautiful foliage I’ve seen in Busan so far.

Here’s how my perfect Fall Foliage day in Busan went.
Up the Mountain by Cable Car: Geumjeongsan in Fall
 
I started the day by taking the Geumgang Park Cable Car, which already felt like stepping back in time. It has this slightly vintage look, almost like the cable cars you’d expect in an old travel movie. As it rose slowly over the trees, Busan began to open up behind me.And the view? Truly, truuuuuly breathtaking.
I could see the city stretching all the way to the ocean, the curves of Gwangalli Bridge, even toward Busan Station when the air was clear. Below, the forest was completely dressed in fall colors. Shades of amber, rust, gold and deep red layered against each other like a giant patchwork quilt.
At the top, the path is gentle and peaceful. There’s a small temple tucked among the rocks, quiet and humble, just blending into the mountain like it has always been part of it. Hikers rested on wooden benches, chatting softly. If I would’ve come a bit later, I’m sure I could’ve seen a few hikers enjoying typical Korean mountain snacks like savory vegetable pancakes sizzling on a flat pan, and cups of makgeolli - Korean rice wine.
I didn’t spend much time on top of the mountain, but the cable car ride itself was worth it a million times!

Geumgang Park Cable Car
Address : 175-146, Ujangchun-ro, Dongnae-gu, Busan
Transportation : Take Busan Metro Line 1 to Oncheonjang Station, about a 15 minute walk to Geumgang Park entrance to reach the cable car
Hours : Please refer to the website (operating hours may vary depending on season / closed on Mondays)
Website : - Geumgang Park

Beomeosa Temple: A Calm Autumn Sanctuary
 
From the mountain, I made my way to Beomeosa, one of Busan’s most treasured but also quite hidden temples. I’ve visited a lot of temples in Korea, but something about Beomeosa in fall feels especially serene. The temple sits at the base of the mountains, surrounded by trees that turn all shades of yellow and red in November.
As soon as I stepped through the main gate, I felt the atmosphere shift. The air was quieter here. Visitors spoke softly, the sound of monks chanting carried from inside one of the prayer halls, blending with the rustling of fallen leaves underfoot.
The combination of the golden ginkgo trees, the fiery maple leaves and the soft fall sunlight looked like a painting. Chrysanthemums were blooming around the temple courtyard, adding gentle color to the stone paths. And Lanterns hung lightly overhead, swaying just a little in the breeze. If you walk a little further up through the temple grounds, you’ll find one of Beomeosa’s most beautiful viewpoints, with mountains in the distance, traditional hanok roofs below, and vibrant red maple trees all around.
When visiting, please keep one thing in mind: Beomeosa is an active Buddhist temple, meaning that people come here to pray, meditate and practice their beliefs. Out of respect, I moved slowly, kept my voice low, and did not take photos inside the main hall. It was calm. Beautiful. Peaceful in the kind of way you feel in your chest.

Beomeosa Temple
Address : 250 Beomeosa-ro, Cheongnyong-dong, Geumjeong-gu, Busan
Transportation : Busan Metro Line 1 to Beomeosa Station, then local bus or taxi to the temple entrance
Hours : 08:00~17:00

Lunch with a Valley View at Geumjeongsanjang
 
By early afternoon, I was ready for lunch and headed to Geumjeongsanjang, a traditional Korean restaurant tucked against the mountainside right at the foot of Beomeosa Temple. The view from here felt like sitting above a valley painting, with layers of forest stretching down the slope.
I ordered grilled duck and a Korean chives pancake, and both were perfect for a fall day: Hearty, savory, warm and comforting. The kind of meal that makes your whole body relax.
The restaurant felt like one of those places that hikers have been coming to for decades. Wooden tables, friendly owners serving food, speaking the strongest Busan Dialect, the sound of plates and laughter. Just pure local mountain energy.

Geumjeongsanjang
Address : 1F, 259 Beomeosa-ro, Geumjeong-gu, Busan (Near Beomeosa and the lower hiking trail entrances on Geumjeongsan)
Transportation : Best accessed by taxi or by foot from Beomeosa hiking paths
Hours : Weekdays 10:00–19:00 / Weekends 08:00–21:00

Coffee in the Trees at Café Sup
 

When I was about to leave the restaurant and head back toward Busan Station, a friendly local ahjussi stopped to say hello and ended up inviting me to a café just above the restaurant. He and his wife run a small place called Café Sup, and it sits right at tree-top level, so the windows look straight out into branches filled with autumn leaves. The view felt almost unreal - just quiet forest, warm coffee, and a bit of charming, slightly cheesy local décor. I stayed much longer than I planned, sipping slowly and watching the leaves sway while I tried to change my train ticket to a later time. Sometimes you just follow the moment. In fall, and especially in Busan, it feels like time moves a little softer - like you should keep extending the day forever just to enjoy it a little bit more..

Café Sup
Address : 259, Beomeosa-ro, Geumjeong-gu, Busan
Location : Directly above Geumjeongsanjang Restaurant
Hours : Tue–Fri: 09:30–19:00 / Weekends: 08:00–19:00 (Closed on Mondays)
Website : Café Sup

records.name: Four Light Festivals Illuminating Busan’s Winter
records.description:
In the winter of 2025, Busan lights up with festivals set against bustling streets, the sea, and cultural spaces throughout the city. If you want to truly soak up the year-end atmosphere, why not take some time to enjoy Busan’s winter light festivals?

1. A Festival Lighting Up Busan’s Winter: Christmas Village Busan 2025

Christmas Village Busan 2025, held at the Busan Cinema Center, is one of the city’s signature winter festivals and a perfect way to soak up the year-end mood. A towering Christmas tree and festive light displays turn the entire venue into one expansive photo spot, while hourly snow shows, Santa parades, and other seasonal attractions draw visitors in.
A Taste of Winter from Around the World

Food is one of the festival’s biggest draws. From Christmas dishes from around the world to well-loved local spots in Busan, a wide range of brands come together to create a generous lineup that appeals to families and travelers alike.
Gift Market & Lifestyle Shops

Markets across the festival showcase Christmas gifts, fashion items, and handmade pieces. With local artists and brands taking part, they’re a favorite stop for anyone searching for something a little different. It’s also a perfect place to pick up a travel keepsake or find a meaningful year-end gift for someone special.
A Special Experience for Families, Couples, and Friends

After sunset, the outdoor plaza at the Busan Cinema Center glows with festive lights, revealing a winter scene that’s truly eye-catching. With interactive programs, photo spots, and live performances, it’s a place where you can create memorable moments—whoever you’re visiting with.
Christmas Village Busan
Address : Busan Cinema Center, 120 Suyeonggangbyeon-daero, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Period : November 27 (Thu) – December 25, 2025 (Thu)
Time : 11:00 ~ 22:00
Website : https://www.marketchango.com

2. Haeundae Light Festival 2025: Winter Nights Aglow

Haeundae Light Festival 2025 is Busan’s signature winter night festival, themed “STELLAR HAEUNDAE: Waves of Starlight.” Taking place from November 29, 2025, to January 18, 2026, the festival unfolds across Haeundae Beach and Gunam-ro. With free admission, visitors can enjoy a variety of light installations and media displays set against the winter sea of Haeundae—a defining highlight of the festival.
A Place That Shines with Every Step

Festival spaces are filled with illuminated installations and media art inspired by starlight, flowing light, and ocean waves. Following the theme “Waves of Starlight,” Haeundae turns into a striking nighttime landscape, where luminous scenes unfold seamlessly as you walk—much like a leisurely evening stroll.
Tips to Make the Most of Your Visit

During the festival, the area around Haeundae is lively with nearby shops, late-night bites, and cafés that add to the atmosphere. Crowds tend to build up on weekends and during the year-end season, so public transportation is the most convenient option. Because it can feel colder by the sea, it’s best to dress warmly, and if you’re visiting with children, be mindful of busy areas around the main photo spots.
Haeundae Light Festival
Address : Haeundae Beach and the Gunam-ro area
Period : November 29, 2025 (Sat) – January 18, 2026 (Sun)
Time : 18:00 ~ 23:00
Website : @haeundae_light

3. A Winter Highlight in Busan: Gwangbok-ro Winter Light Tree Festival

A year-end favorite in Busan, the Gwangbok-ro Winter Light Tree Festival returns in 2025 to brighten the city once again. From December 5, 2025, to February 22, 2026, festive illuminations light up the Gwangbok-ro and Gwangbokjungang-ro areas every evening from 5:30 p.m. to 10:00 p.m., filling downtown Busan with a warm winter glow.
This Year’s Theme: “K-Nuri (From Gwangbok to the World)” 

The 2025 festival is themed “K-Nuri (From Gwangbok to the World).” Sculptural installations inspired by Korean patterns and designs appear throughout the area, enhanced by layered lighting that brings tradition and modern style together. With its strong sense of Korean identity, the illuminated streets feel especially engaging for both local visitors and international travelers.
A Spectacular Main Tree and Streets of Light

A large signature tree, the symbol of the festival, is installed, with a lighting ceremony and countdown event held on opening day. Gwangbok-ro is lined with illuminations throughout, offering vibrant night views in every direction, while well-placed photo spots make it easy to capture memorable year-end moments.
Weekend Performances and Hands-On Programs

Weekends bring added energy to the festival with busking performances by local artists and interactive lighting events open to the public. On December 20–21, visitors can also enjoy hands-on programs such as Christmas cooking classes and mini tree-making—ideal for families and couples looking to create special memories.

Image Provided by: Jung-gu SNS Supporters 해마쌤

Gwangbok-ro Winter Light Tree Festival
Address : Gwangbok-ro and Gwangbokjungang-ro areas, Busan
Period : December 5, 2025 (Fri) – February 22, 2026 (Sun)
Time : 17:30 ~ 22:00
Website : https://litt.ly/gwangbok_treefestival

4. A Place Filled with Winter Charm: Village de Ananti Tree Village 

Set along Busan’s Gijang coast, Village de Ananti Tree Village transforms its outdoor spaces with festive lights and tree displays for the winter season. The event takes place at Ananti Square near the shoreline and is open for anyone to visit freely. Across the square, clusters of trees arranged like a winter grove are enhanced with soft lighting, creating a warm and inviting seasonal atmosphere.

records.name: Christmas in Busan: 4 Must-Visit & Insta-Worthy Christmas Themed Cafés
records.originalName: 12월 어권특화 영문_부산의 크리스마스: 꼭 가봐야 할 인스타 감성 크리스마스 카페 4곳
records.description:
Busan is one of those cities in Korea that will make you fall in love with it the moment you arrive. The big “Busan is good” sign and the cute Boogi 부기 (Busan’s mascot) at Busan Station make you feel like the city is welcoming you with open arms. For BTS ARMYs, it is a must-visit place since it is the hometown of Jimin and Jungkook, while others visit to enjoy the capsule ride beside the sea, explore beautiful cultural villages, or surf during the summer. It does not matter what time of the year you come, Busan will always have something exciting to offer that will make you not want to leave the city. But if you ask me about the best time to visit Busan, I would say during the holiday season.

Busan during Christmas is honestly something special. The city feels prettier, cuter, and somehow warmer even when the air is cold. You see sparkling lights and decorations on every corner, hear Christmas songs wherever you go, and above all, feel the cozy Christmas vibes while sipping something warm inside a café. And if there is one area where you can feel this the most, it is Jeonpo Cafe Street.
Today, let me show you my personal café hopping experience through Jeonpo Cafe Street. I decided to visit a few cute Christmas-themed cafés that truly capture the season and that you should also add to your must-visit list. From beautifully decorated Christmas trees to seasonal drinks that warm your hands and your mood, these cafés will make your Busan winter unforgettable.

Warning
Please bring an extra portable battery and make sure you have enough storage space on your phone because you will end up taking a lot of videos and photos in all of these cafés.
1. Cup of Joy

If Christmas in café form had a face, this café would be it. From the moment you walk toward it, you can tell this place is serious about the holiday season. The menu at the entrance is so cute that you literally cannot resist going inside. The entrance is decorated with Christmas lights, and once you step inside, it feels like entering a warm Christmas world.
When you enter, you are greeted by the sweetest staff (they were also wearing cute Christmas hats), and the first thing you see is a giant Christmas tree inside, which makes you realize how much effort went into every detail. 
The tree is filled with warm lights, cinnamon sticks, red berries, heart-shaped ornaments, and tiny cozy decorations that instantly make you feel calm. It is the kind of Christmas tree you want to stand in front of for a long time and take as many pictures as you can for your Instagram stories.
Menu
The menu board itself is fun to look at, with illustrated drinks and desserts that already put you in a good mood before ordering. Their menu includes Cocoa Bar hot drinks, toast and sandwiches, desserts, coffee, tea, ice cream, and more. In short, you have to come here with an empty stomach and enjoy all of their delicious options.
I really wanted to try Cup of Joy’s seasonal Cocoa Bar menu. Trust me, this is not your regular hot chocolate. The drinks come in the cutest Christmas mugs that look like tiny houses, topped with whipped cream, candy canes, and peppermint pieces. Holding that mug in front of the Christmas tree honestly felt like a movie scene. It is sweet, cozy, and very Christmas.
If you want a café that fully embraces Christmas from the entrance to the interior, this is the place. It feels warm, joyful, and exactly like its name. Highly, highly recommended.
Cup of Joy
Address : 45 Seojeon-ro 68beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan (2F)
Timing : 12:00 - 23:00 (last order 22:30)
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/cupofjoy_coj/

2. Moody Bread Market

Who would not want to visit Europe during the holiday season? But what if I told you that you could enjoy a European-style Christmas café experience right in Busan? Moody Bread Market has you covered.
This café feels like stepping into a European winter street. The exterior alone is stunning, especially during Christmas, and it literally makes you say “WOW” and "Omo, neomu yeppeuda. (Oh my, it’s so pretty.)". The brick building is decorated with large wreaths, red ribbons, and ornaments that instantly catch your eye. You end up standing outside for a while, just looking at the building and appreciating its beauty. It honestly looks like something straight out of a Christmas postcard.
Once you walk inside, the atmosphere changes completely, in the best way. The interior is warm, cozy, and smells amazing because of all the freshly baked bread. The café has two floors, and each floor has its own charm. The Christmas decorations are subtle but perfectly placed, with greenery, red accents, and soft lighting that makes the entire café Instagram-worthy.
Menu
Their signature items are their buns, especially the cinnamon bun, butter salt bun, blueberry cream cheese bun, and more. What I loved most here is the bakery setup. The breads are displayed beautifully, and you can see a variety of twist buns with different toppings. 
It feels homey since you can grab whatever you want, as much as you want, all by yourself and then pay at the counter.  Sitting here with a warm drink while sunlight pours in through the windows feels like the perfect winter afternoon, European style.

Moody Bread Market is truly the perfect escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. It makes you feel like you are far away in Europe, enjoying hot coffee with delicious buns. No rush, no noise, just good bread, warm light, and quiet European Christmas vibes surrounding you.
Moody Bread Market
Address : 22 Jeonpo-daero 216beon-gil, Busanjin District, Busan
Timing : 11:00 - 21:00
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/moody_bread_market/ 

3. State Bakery 

If you want to feel like you are in a Christmas movie set in Busan, State Bakery is the place to go. 

While walking along Jeonpo Cafe Street, I stumbled upon this café and could not resist going in. It is so pretty even from the outside that I literally spent about 20 minutes taking photos and filming reels of the snowy Christmas trees lined up in the courtyard. 
They look like they have been dusted with fresh snow, tall, fluffy, and softly glowing with warm lights. It instantly sets the mood, calm, festive, and very winter in Busan. Honestly, I did not see Christmas decorations at this level anywhere else.

records.name: A Journey in West Busan Along the Sanctuary of Migratory Birds
records.originalName: 겨울, 멀리서 날아온 풍경 - 철새 도래지 따라 서부산 여행
records.address:
Eulsukdo Ecological Park・Migratory Bird Park: 1240, Nakdongnam-ro, Saha-gu, Busan
Amisan Observatory: 77, Dadaenakjo 2-gil, Saha-gu, Busan
Dadaepo Beach: 14, Morundae 1-gil, Saha-gu, Busan (Dadae-dong area)
records.description:
When winter sets in, the western side of Busan reveals a quieter, more distinctive side.
As the season turns cold and visitor numbers dwindle, the skies and rivers of West Busan come alive in a whole new way. Migratory birds travel thousands of kilometers to reach the Nakdonggang Estuary, which becomes their home for the winter.
We invite you to spend a day walking through West Busan, taking in the seasonal landscapes and rare winter scenes shaped by these passing visitors.
Eulsukdo Ecological Park・Migratory Bird Park

Eulsukdo Island is a key area of the Sanctuary of Migratory Birds at Nakdonggang River Estuary, Natural Monument No. 179. 
Situated where the Nakdonggang River meets the sea, it is defined by wide tidal flats and extensive reed wetlands shaped by the estuary’s natural environment.
From late October through March each year, the island serves as a seasonal refuge for migratory birds. 
Around 100,000 wintering birds from more than 50 species—including whooper swans, bean geese, northern pintails, mallards, common shelducks, and black-headed gulls—gather here to rest, earning the place its reputation as a well-known haven for winter migrants.
Whooper swans drifting in long lines across the water, other birds skimming through the reeds as they take flight, and moments when the sky is suddenly filled with the synchronized movement of migratory flocks—these winter scenes define Eulsukdo Island.
This landscape becomes even more vivid as you walk along the perimeter trail that traces the island’s edge. 
Along the long, continuous path, the movements of migratory birds and the changing textures of the wetlands unfold naturally within view. 
The more you slow down, the more clearly you sense that this place is not simply a park, but a living habitat in motion. 
In winter, Eulsukdo Island feels less like a sightseeing spot and more like a place to walk in step with the rhythm of nature shaped by the river, the tidal flats, and the migratory birds.
Eulsukdo Ecological Park・Migratory Bird Park
Address : 1240, Nakdongnam-ro, Saha-gu, Busan
Inquiries : +82-51-209-2000
Website : https://www.busan.go.kr/wetland/index

Amisan Observatory

Amisan Observatory sits along the Dadaenakjo-gil, Saha-gu, Busan, offering panoramic views of the Nakdonggang Estuary, Eulsukdo Island, and nearby sandbars such as Doyodeung and Baekhapdeung, where migratory birds gather.
Inside, exhibitions explain the formation and ecology of the Nakdonggang Estuary. 
From the third floor, visitors can observe migratory birds’ routes and flocking behavior through floor-to-ceiling windows and telescopes.
After seeing migratory birds up close on Eulsukdo Island, Amisan Observatory lets you step back and take in their movement from a wider perspective. 
From the lookout, the focus shifts away from individual birds to vast flocks moving across the Nakdonggang Estuary, spreading out in panoramic formations.
Standing here, it becomes clear why this landscape has long served as a resting place for migratory birds.
As sunset approaches, the outlines of the river and tidal flats sharpen, and the birds become more active. 
Moving flocks and changing light overlap, shaping a scene that feels distinctly of this hour.
Amisan Observatory
Address : 77, Dadaenakjo 2-gil, Saha-gu, Busan
Admission : Free
Opening Hours : 09:00-18:00
Closed : Mondays

Dadaepo Beach

Dadaepo Beach sits where the Nakdonggang Estuary meets Namhae, or “South Sea”. 
Its broad, west-facing shoreline is one of Busan’s most reliable places to catch the sunset. 
As evening falls, red light stretches across the water, and the sky shifts color at an unhurried pace. 
Winter brings clearer air, sharpening the edges of the horizon and deepening the contrast of the fading light, giving dusk here a quieter, more layered mood.
With well-maintained seaside paths, parks, and viewing areas, the beach remains easy to visit even in winter. 
After spending the day following migratory birds, your gaze naturally shifts toward the sea and sky, and a tranquil walk at sunset—accompanied by the sound of waves—offers a calm way to bring the day to a close.
Dadaepo Beach
Address : 14, Morundae 1-gil, Saha-gu, Busan (Dadae-dong area)

records.name: This Lunar New Year, Busan Is Good
Busan Unique Venues—Discover One-of-a-Kind Spaces in Busan
records.description:
With the rise of bleisure travel—where business meets leisure—MICE cities are no longer seen as just places to host events, but as destinations worth exploring. In turn, expectations for event spaces are shifting, with growing interest in venues that not only offer convenience and functionality, but also capture the unique character and atmosphere of the local area.
The “Unique Venues” go beyond standard convention centers or hotel ballrooms. They are shaped by local culture, history, and stories, offering memorable and distinctive experiences. Busan, a global tourism city where the ocean meets the metropolis and nature blends with culture, is an ideal destination to experience them at their best. From seaside exhibition and performance spaces to cultural spots steeped in the city’s history, and modern multi-purpose complexes, Busan offers a diverse range of sites that bring a unique edge to any MICE event.
Busan Unique Venues offer more than just a place to host events—they allow participants to experience Busan’s scenery, culture, and lifestyle up close, and connect with what makes the city truly special. Begin your experience of Busan here, where business meets travel seamlessly.

 Haeundae-gu

Nurimaru APEC House

Nurimaru APEC House is a combination of ‘nuri’, meaning ‘world’, and ‘maru’, meaning ‘summit’, meaning a house where world leaders gather, and is characterized by the unique beauty of traditional Korean architecture. After the APEC Summit attended by world leaders, it is used as a memorial hall and a representative unique conference venue in Busan, hosting CEO and new product presentations, investment meetings, and the Supreme Government Council.
Nurimaru APEC House
Address : 55, APEC-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Inquiries : +82-51-740-7515
View Details : Go to Page

MUSEUM 1

Museum 1 is a contemporary art museum specializing in media art located in Centum City, Haeundae-gu, Busan. We mainly hold events in the form of receptions and after-party. Museum 1 is the largest modern art museum specializing in media art in Korea with 80 million LED displays in a structure of about 700 pyeong. It will be a unique event to enjoy with various works of art, including media works as well as installation, painting, sculpture, ceramics, and photography.
Museum 1
Address : 20, Centum seo-ro, Haeundae-gu
Inquiries : +82-70-4256-8432
View Details : Go to Page

Busan X The Sky

Busan X the Sky is the largest observatory in Korea, located at the ‘Haeundae L City Landmark Tower’, the second height in Korea (411.6m). In addition to Busan landmarks (Gwangan Bridge, Marine City), you can see the ocean view and city view of Busan, and it aims for the best premium services such as spectacular media facilities in the observatory, Busan’s highest restaurant Sky99 Grill & Pasta, and the world’s highest Starbucks.
Busan X the Sky
Address : 98-100F, 30, Dalmaji-Gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Inquiries : +82-70-7730-3744
View Details : Go to Page

Jung-gu

NOTICE

Cafe Notice is a multifaceted cultural space that reinterprets a rice warehouse built in 1950 with a modern sensibility. The first floor serves as a lively venue for a variety of cultural events, welcoming those passionate about art and culture. The second and third floors feature cozy café spaces, offering visitors a relaxing retreat with warm coffee to enjoy.
Cafe Notice
Address : 135, Daegyo-ro, Jung-gu, Busan
Inquiries : +82-70-4114-8232
View Details : Go to Page

Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum

The Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum showcases the city’s history during the modern and contemporary periods. Busan embodies the dynamic essence of Korean history, marked by significant events such as the establishment of the port, the Japanese colonial era, the Korean War, industrial growth, and the journey toward democracy. The city’s modern and contemporary history is deeply intertwined with its residents, continuing to shape our story today. Our goal is to establish the museum as a guardian of citizens’ memories, ensuring that they are not confined to the past.
Busan Modern & Contemporary History Museum
Address : 112(Main Building)/104(Annex), Daecheong-ro, Jung-gu, Busan
Inquiries : +82-51-607-8043
View Details : Go to Page

Yeongdo-gu

Unknown Diary

‘Unknown Diary’, located in the warehouse district of Yeongdo, Busan, where modern harbor warehouses stand in rows, is a cultural space that breathes new life into an old warehouse built in the 1950s. Through careful renovation, it offers tangible and intangible content rooted in contemporary lifestyles and culture.
