As a brand dedicated to preserving unrecorded moments of daily life, Unknown Diary invites you to discover your personal tastes and shares the warmth of sunlight within its rugged, industrial charm.‘Unknown Diary’ serves a variety of beverages, signature desserts, and brunch dishes infused with the local stories of the region. 
Unknown Diary
Address : 178, Bongnaenaru-ro, Yeongdo-gu, Busan
Inquiries : +82-70-7347-8069
View Details : Go to Page

Space OneZ

Space OneZ, located in the Mulyangjang in Yeongdo-gu, Busan, is a complex cultural space that adds modern sensibility while retaining its original form from 100 years ago. It consists of a total of 1,100 pyeong of 3 Bonded Warehouses and 1 F&B Place, providing an experience that combines the past and the present. F&B Place is a Western restaurant and cafe, offering a variety of food and culture content. The spacious and pleasant space can be used in a variety of ways, from casual meetings to large-scale banquets. We also have alcoholic beverages such as handmade beer and wine, so we have a wide range of menu choices.
Space OneZ
Address : 214 Bongraenaru-ro, Yeongdo, Busan
Inquiries : +82-51-412-4500
View Details : Go to Page

P.ARK(PLATFORM OF ARK FOR CREATORS)

P.ARK(PLATFORM OF ARK FOR CREATORS) is a multi-cultural space where you can experience creators and branded content based on the lifestyle of today’s era, including F&B, culture, art, exhibitions, and activities.
Designed with the structure of a large ship as a motif, various cultural events are held in each space according to seasonal themes. It is a cultural hub that connects past and present, industrial areas and art spaces, sellers and consumers, locals and tourists, by providing special experiences in collaboration with new lifestyle brands.
P.ARK(PLATFORM OF ARK FOR CREATORS)
Address : 180, Haeyang-ro 195beon-gil, Yeongdo-gu, Busan
Inquiries : +82-70-4628-0011 
View Details : Go to Page

records.name: Enjoy K-POP in Busan, the 「B-POP」 'Local' Course
records.description:
Busan is far too vibrant to be defined only by its ocean views and night skyline. From old alleyways and hillside roads to small villages by the sea, beaches glowing beneath the sunset, and art-filled streets alive with creativity, the entire city unfolds like one emotional stage. Just as K-POP has become a global culture loved by fans around the world, Busan also draws travelers in with its own unique rhythm and atmosphere.

And now, Busan is evolving into a new kind of emotional travel experience through its connection with K-POP.
A travel project that combines Busan and K-POP — B-POP.

This is a journey where you walk through the city with your favorite playlist playing, experiencing Busan’s scenery and emotions like a flowing rhythm. Like listening to an album from beginning to end, each destination naturally connects through its own distinct mood and vibe.

The first theme introduces the “Local” course, where you can discover the most authentic side of Busan.
Beginning from the hillside roads of Northern Busan, continuing to the sea and art villages of Western Busan, and ending in the cinematic alleyways of Yeongdo, this is a slow and immersive journey through the daily life and emotional landscape of Busan.

B-POP “Local” Course at a Glance

Northern Busan
Mandeok Lego Village → Seokbulsa Temple

Western Busan
Dadaepo Beach → Gamcheon Culture Village → Yeongdo Huinnyeoul Village

‧Emotional hillside roads and local alleyway vibes unique to Busan
‧Scenery and photo spots reminiscent of K-POP music videos
‧A sentimental journey where the sea, art, and sunsets come together
‧A travel route closest to the everyday lives of Busan locals
1. Mandeok Lego Village
The Beginning of Busan’s Local Charm

The first scene of the B-POP Local Course begins along the hillside roads of Mandeok-dong in Busan’s Buk-gu district.
The narrow alleys, stairways, and rows of stacked little houses resemble colorful toy blocks piled together. That is why people affectionately call this place “Lego Village.”
The greatest charm of this place is that it is not an artificially created tourist attraction. Real residents continue their everyday lives here, and Busan’s ordinary moments naturally flow through the old alleyways. The sounds of daily life echoing between walls and the city views appearing at the end of each alley vividly capture Busan’s unique local atmosphere.

Recently, its emotional and nostalgic mood has also attracted younger travelers and K-POP fans. The colorful scenery and the distinctive ambience of the hillside village feel like scenes from a youthful K-POP album jacket or music video.

Put on your earphones and slowly walk through the alleys with music playing.
Before long, an ordinary day in Busan begins to feel like a special cinematic moment.

Travel Information

Location : Around Mandeok-dong, Buk-gu, Busan Recommended 
Highlights : Hillside alleyway atmosphere, local-style photography 
Recommended Time : Morning to late afternoon
2. Seokbulsa Temple
Another Rhythm of Busan Found in Quiet Serenity

As you pass through the alleys of Mandeok and head further up the mountain, the atmosphere becomes noticeably calmer. The busy rhythm of Northern Busan slowly fades away, replaced by the sound of gentle wind and the refreshing air of the mountains.
Nestled along the slopes of Geumjeongsan Mountain, Seokbulsa Temple is one of Busan’s hidden temple gems. The majestic Buddha carvings engraved into the cliffside and the tranquil scenery create a completely different atmosphere from Busan’s bustling tourist attractions.

As Korean aesthetics and traditional spaces continue to appear in recent K-POP content, places like this have become emotionally captivating for international travelers as well. At Seokbulsa, where nature, tradition, and stillness coexist beautifully, pausing for a moment to overlook the city of Busan makes even the city noise feel distant.

And from here, the rhythm of Busan that once flowed through the hillside roads slowly descends toward the western coastline, unfolding into broader and more relaxed scenery.

Travel Information

Location : 143-96 Mandeokgogae-gil, Buk-gu, Busan 
Recommended Highlights : Cliff-carved Buddha statues, mountain temple scenery, peaceful healing atmosphere 
Recommended Time : Morning to early afternoon
3. Dadaepo Beach
The Western Busan Sea Where Sunsets Meet Music

If the mountains and alleyways of Northern Busan reflected the everyday lives of Busan locals, then the sea of Western Busan reveals the city’s most romantic moments. And it all begins at Dadaepo Beach.

The wide sandy beach, gentle waves, and slowly reddening sunset create scenery that feels straight out of the ending scene of a K-POP music video. Especially at sunset, walking along the shoreline allows you to naturally feel the relaxed rhythm that defines Busan.
The charm of Dadaepo lies not in flashy attractions, but in its atmosphere.
Unlike crowded tourist destinations, this is a place where you can enjoy the sea, the sunset, and the music at a slower pace.

As your playlist reaches its chorus, the sunset before your eyes begins to glow in its most beautiful colors.
In that moment, the sea of Dadaepo feels like one enormous concert stage.

Travel Information

Location : Dadae-dong, Saha-gu, Busan 
Recommended Highlights : Sunset views, seaside walks, emotional photography spots 
Recommended Time : Around sunset
4. Gamcheon Culture Village
An Alleyway Filled with the Colors and Art of Busan

Known as the “Machu Picchu of Busan,” Gamcheon Culture Village is one of Busan’s most iconic artistic travel destinations. The colorful houses stretching along the hillside and the mural-filled alleyways create a uniquely charming atmosphere found nowhere else.
If the sunsets of Dadaepo revealed Busan’s romantic side, Gamcheon Culture Village showcases the city’s imagination and vibrant colors. Every alley reveals a completely different scene, and even the smallest stairway feels like a work of art.

Today, K-POP has expanded beyond music into fashion, visual aesthetics, and artistic culture. In that sense, Gamcheon Culture Village perfectly embodies Busan’s artistic atmosphere. Its distinctive colors are also why the village continues to be loved as a filming location for photoshoots and videos.

Walking slowly through the alleys feels like traveling through an art film.
And now, the final scene of the journey continues toward a small village perched beside the sea cliffs.

Travel Information

Location : 203 Gamnae 2-ro, Saha-gu, Busan 
Recommended Highlights : Photo zones, mural alleys, craft shops & café tours 
Recommended Time : Afternoon
5. Yeongdo Huinnyeoul Village
A Cinematic Ending to the B-POP Local Journey

The final stop of the B-POP Local Course is Huinnyeoul Village in Yeongdo.
The scenery created by the blue sea beneath the cliffs, white walls, and narrow alleyways forms one of the most cinematic atmospheres in all of Busan.
Once home to refugees rebuilding their lives after the war, this village has now become one of Busan’s signature emotional travel destinations. The seaside walking paths and quiet cafés make the final moments of the journey even more memorable.

Huinnyeoul Village still holds the deep emotional essence of Busan’s local culture, so much so that it has been used as a filming location for numerous movies and dramas. Thanks to its dramatic ocean cliffs and atmospheric alleyways, it is also frequently mentioned as a filming spot for K-POP-style visual content. Even now, countless travelers visit to experience scenery that feels straight out of a movie scene.

Sit beside the window of a quiet café at the end of the coastal cliff path, gaze out at the sea, and play the final track on your playlist.
The lingering emotions of Busan’s local charm will stay with you long after the journey ends.

Travel Information
 
Location : 605-3 Yeongseon-dong 4-ga, Yeongdo-gu, Busan 
Recommended Highlights : Coastal cliff paths, emotional cafés, seaside walks 
Recommended Time : Sunset to evening 
B-POP Local Course Travel TIP

‧Walk Along with a K-POP Playlist
This journey is less about sightseeing and more about experiencing the atmosphere. Walking with music will allow you to feel Busan’s emotional charm even more deeply.

‧Prepare Comfortable Sneakers
Since there are many hillside roads and stairways, comfortable shoes are highly recommended for long walks.

‧Check the Sunset Time
Dadaepo Beach and Huinnyeoul Village are at their most beautiful around sunset.

‧Travel Slowly
The key to this B-POP Local Course is not moving quickly from place to place, but walking slowly while experiencing the rhythm of Busan’s everyday scenery and atmosphere.

records.name: Enjoy K-POP in Busan, the 「B-POP」 ‘Romance’ Course
records.description:
Busan is a city that feels charming both day and night.
During the day, visitors can enjoy relaxing walks along the beaches, parks, and streets, while at night, the city lights and skyline create an entirely different atmosphere.

If the previous ‘Local’ course focused on Busan’s everyday neighborhoods and local vibes, this second theme introduces the ‘Romance’ course — a journey through Busan’s breathtaking night views, ocean scenery, and emotional city atmosphere.

Starting from a peaceful urban park and continuing through trendy cafe streets, panoramic observatories, coastal scenery, and the night view of Gwangan Bridge, this course takes you through some of the most romantic moments Busan has to offer.

B-POP ‘Romance’ Course at a Glance

Busan Citizens Park → Seomyeon Jeonpo Cafe Street → Hwangnyeongsan Observatory → Oryukdo → Gwangalli Beach
 ‧Emotional cityscapes and famous night-view spots in Busan ‧K-POP-inspired photo & video locations ‧A travel course that flows beautifully from daytime to nighttime ‧A romantic Busan trip featuring cafes, ocean views, and observatories
1. Busan Citizens Park
Starting the B-POP Romance Course with a Relaxing Urban Escape

The B-POP ‘Romance’ course begins at Busan Citizens Park.
Once a former U.S. military base, the area has been transformed into a large public park where visitors can enjoy nature and relaxation right in the heart of the city.
With spacious walking paths, open lawns, and seasonal scenery throughout the year, the park remains a beloved resting spot for both locals and travelers. In the soft afternoon sunlight, the entire park takes on an especially peaceful atmosphere, making it a perfect place for emotional travel photos.

Recently, natural outdoor spaces like this have also become popular settings for K-POP-inspired content and fashion shoots, drawing even more attention to urban park travel experiences.

Take a slow walk away from the busy city streets and enjoy the relaxing start of your Busan journey.

Travel Information

Location : 73 Simingongwon-ro, Busanjin-gu, Busan 
Highlights : Walking trails, open lawns, seasonal scenery 
Recommended Time : Afternoon
2. Seomyeon Jeonpo Cafe Street
Where Busan’s Trendy and Artistic Vibes Come Together

After enjoying the peaceful atmosphere of Busan Citizens Park, head over to Jeonpo Cafe Street, one of Busan’s trendiest neighborhoods.

Jeonpo Cafe Street is famous for its unique cafes, lifestyle shops, and stylish boutiques. Each alley offers a different atmosphere, making it a great place to experience Busan’s modern and creative side.
In recent years, the area has also become popular among K-POP fans as a must-visit photo spot. Its vintage alleyways and stylish interiors create the perfect backdrop for magazine-style photos.

Spend some time relaxing at a cafe, listening to music, or simply wandering through the streets to discover your own side of Busan’s charm.

After experiencing the romantic mood of downtown Busan, it’s time to head somewhere with an even wider view of the city.

Travel Information
 
Location : Jeonpo-dong area, Busanjin-gu, Busan 
Highlights : Trendy cafes, lifestyle shops, alley photography 
Recommended Time : Afternoon to Evening
3. Hwangnyeongsan Observatory
The Most Romantic Place to Enjoy Busan’s Night View

The next stop after Jeonpo Cafe Street is Hwangnyeongsan Observatory.
Known as one of Busan’s most famous night-view spots, the observatory offers panoramic views of the city skyline, the coastline, and surrounding districts.
As the sun slowly sets, the city lights begin to blend with the ocean, creating Busan’s signature romantic nighttime scenery. Once night falls completely, the dazzling lights of the city spread out below, making the observatory an even more atmospheric destination for visitors.

The observatory has also gained popularity among travelers who enjoy taking photos and videos inspired by the cinematic city-night aesthetics often seen in K-POP live clips and visual content.

Standing here with the cool evening breeze while overlooking Busan’s skyline, it becomes easy to understand why the city is often described as one of Korea’s most romantic destinations.

Travel Information
 
Location : 391-39 Hwangnyeongsan-ro, Nam-gu, Busan 
Highlights : Panoramic city view, Busan skyline, night drive course 
Recommended Time : Sunset to Nighttime
4. Oryukdo
A Moment to Experience the Romance of Busan’s Ocean Up Close

After taking in the night view from Hwangnyeongsan, it’s time to experience Busan’s ocean scenery even more closely.

Oryukdo is one of Busan’s most iconic coastal landmarks, known for its dramatic seaside cliffs, wide-open ocean views, and refreshing walking trails.
The sound of the waves and the endless coastal scenery create a completely different atmosphere from the city center. On clear days, the blue sea and sky come together to showcase Busan’s refreshing seaside charm.

Thanks to its emotional ocean scenery, Oryukdo has recently become a popular location for K-POP-style travel photography and video content. In particular, the Oryukdo Skywalk is a perfect photo spot with stunning ocean views in the background.

Visiting during the transition from late afternoon to sunset allows travelers to experience Busan’s coastline at its most romantic.

Travel Information
 
Location : 137 Oryukdo-ro, Nam-gu, Busan 
Highlights : Oryukdo Skywalk, coastal walks, ocean scenery 
Recommended Time : Afternoon to Sunset
5. Gwangalli Beach
The Most Atmospheric Way to Enjoy Busan at Night

The final stop of the B-POP ‘Romance’ course is Gwangalli Beach.
As one of Busan’s most famous nighttime destinations, the beach transforms into a spectacular scene after dark, with the illuminated Gwangan Bridge and ocean views creating Busan’s signature romantic atmosphere.
What makes Gwangalli truly special is that visitors can enjoy not only the beach itself, but also the music, nightlife, and lively atmosphere surrounding it. Cafes, pubs, and busking performances along the beachfront complete Gwangalli’s free-spirited and emotional vibe.

Recently, short-form videos and travel content featuring the night view of Gwangan Bridge have also become popular among K-POP-inspired creators. Walking along the beach while listening to music can feel like stepping into a scene from a music video.

Busan’s romance is not defined only by its dazzling night views.
It becomes truly special when the ocean breeze, music, and travel memories come together in one unforgettable moment.

Travel Information
 
Location : 219 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro, Suyeong-gu, Busan 
Highlights : Gwangan Bridge night view, beach walks, emotional cafes & busking performances 
Recommended Time : Evening to Nighttime 
B-POP ‘Romance’ Course Travel Tips

‧Start Around Sunset
This course becomes even more beautiful after sunset, so it’s recommended to enjoy both the evening glow and the nighttime scenery.

‧Prepare a Relaxing Playlist
Busan’s ocean views and night scenery feel even more special when paired with music.

‧Check Your Camera or Phone Battery
There are many scenic photo spots throughout the course, so you’ll likely take plenty of pictures and videos.

‧Take Your Time
With plenty of cafes and walking spots along the way, this course is best enjoyed slowly and at your own pace.

records.name: Enjoy K-POP in Busan, the 「B-POP」 ‘Healing’ Course
records.description:
Busan is like a giant playlist in itself. If the 'Local' course introduced earlier was like the heavy, authentic music of an indie band, and the 'Romance' course was like a glamorous city pop or R&B track, the third theme, the 'Healing' course, resembles a warm acoustic ballad that comforts a weary heart.

In our busy daily lives, there are moments when we want to plug in our earphones, block out the outside noise, and simply find our own tempo. This is much like how recent K-POP songs, beyond their flashy performances, are receiving immense love for carrying messages that comfort and heal the inner selves of listeners.

The B-POP 'Healing' course is a journey that steps slightly away from the bustling city center to follow the warmth of forests, water, quiet traditions, and kind-hearted people. Starting from a tranquil reservoir, passing through mountains and a temple, and leading into everyday walking trails and friendly market alleys, you will soon experience the tight tension in your heart melting away as you walk this path.

B-POP 'Healing' Course at a Glance

Hoedong Reservoir → Geumjeongsan Mountain → Beomeosa Temple → Oncheoncheon Stream → Seodong Maze Market

‧ Natural landscapes with an acoustic K-POP vibe that slow down your heart's tempo
‧ Perfect visual and auditory relaxation where forests, mountains, and water harmonize
‧ The quiet, hidden charm of Busan that fills your inner self instead of offering mere glamour
‧ A time of comfort to lay down your emotional burdens and meet your true 'self'
1. Hoedong Reservoir
A Calm Intro to Slow Down Your Heart's Tempo

The first track of the B-POP Healing course plays at Hoedong Reservoir, a hidden gem in Geumjeong-gu, Busan. The clear, expansive lake and the lush forest surrounding it prove that Busan is not just a city of beaches.
Passing through the refreshing bamboo forest and stepping barefoot onto the moist red clay path of Ttangmoesan Mountain, you feel as if you've become one with nature. Following this path, the fresh air from the dense cypress forest and the sound of gently rippling water tickle your ears like a natural ASMR track, soothing your weary mind.

Your mind becomes infinitely calm, just like the intro of an acoustic K-POP song that starts with a single guitar melody, free of flashy electronic sounds. If you have complex thoughts or heavy worries, sit quietly on a bench here and listen to some soft music. The tranquility of the lake will calm even the complicated waves in your heart.

Travel Information

Location: 352-3, Oryun-dong, Geumjeong-gu, Busan
Recommended Points: Walking the cypress forest path, waterside trail, zoning out by the water (mul-meong)
Recommended Time: Early morning to late morning
2. Geumjeongsan Mountain
Majestic Comfort Brought by Open Landscapes

If you've calmly opened your heart at Hoedong Reservoir, it's now time to head to Geumjeongsan Mountain, the guardian mountain of Busan. Recently designated as a national park, once again proving its outstanding value, Geumjeongsan offers a wonderful time of healing just by walking along its open ridges with the fresh air emitted by the forest.
As you slowly climb the fortress trail through the dense trees, it feels as if your daily stress evaporates along with the beads of sweat forming on your forehead. When you finally reach a mountain pass or the fortress wall where the view opens up, you can feel a sense of liberation, much like the bursting chorus of an emotional K-POP healing song. Looking down at the wide world spread beneath your feet and taking a deep breath, this moment will serve as the most magnificent and refreshing pause in this course.

Travel Information

Location: Geumjeong-gu, Busan (towards Geumjeongsanseong Fortress)
Recommended Points: Walking the Geumjeongsanseong forest path, taking a phytoncide shower in nature
Recommended Time: Late morning
3. Beomeosa Temple
Quiet Emptiness Like the Traditional Aesthetics in K-POP

Following the embrace of the mountain, you will reach Beomeosa Temple, a place that holds a thousand years of history. Nestled at the foot of Geumjeongsan Mountain, this ancient temple possesses a magnificent yet uniquely neat beauty.
Recently, the sounds of Korean traditional instruments like the gayageum and haegeum, or the curves of traditional Hanok houses, have often appeared in global K-POP stages and music videos, captivating the world. Beomeosa Temple is a space where you can most vividly feel the depth and the beauty of empty space that such traditions provide. Listen closely to the sound of the wind brushing through the bamboo forest and the gentle ringing of the wind chimes hanging from the eaves. A profound and warm comfort, which cannot be felt in the latest pop songs, melts into the tranquil air of the temple.

Travel Information

Location: 250 Beomeosa-ro, Geumjeong-gu, Busan
Recommended Points: The tranquility of the temple, the bamboo forest path, a time for contemplation
Recommended Time: Noon to early afternoon
4. Oncheoncheon Stream
A Pleasant Medium Tempo Seeping into Daily Life

If you have had a deep time of healing in nature, it is now time to slowly approach the daily lives of Busan citizens. Oncheoncheon is a long ecological stream that crosses through the city center, and it is a beloved walking trail year-round where blooming flowers and green grass harmonize each season.
The sight of people riding bicycles and walking their dogs is as refreshing as a scene from a bright and relaxing medium-tempo K-POP music video. Sit at the cafe street established along Oncheoncheon, enjoy a warm cup of coffee, and play some light music. Even without any special events, simply watching the vibrant energy of ordinary daily life fills you with small but certain healing.

Travel Information

Location: Oncheoncheon area, Yeonje-gu to Dongnae-gu, Busan
Recommended Points: Walking the waterside trail, touring the Oncheoncheon Cafe Street
Recommended Time: Late afternoon
5. Seodong Maze Market
A Warm Hidden Track that Concludes the Album

The charm of a well-made album lies in the 'hidden track' that offers unexpected warmth. The final destination of the B-POP Healing course, Seodong Maze Market, is exactly that kind of place. Tangled with maze-like narrow alleys where only one person can barely pass through, this place is full of a strong human connection that you cannot feel in glamorous large supermarkets.
Walk between the alleys as if you're exploring, and try some warm street food, including the local specialty, 'Egg Dumplings'. The laughter of the merchants, though rough but full of affection, along with the delicious smells, will warmly melt even a traveler's frozen heart. Because it is not a perfectly polished tourist spot, it feels more welcoming, and even if you get lost while walking, it's fun in its own right. Let's pleasantly wrap up the final track of this healing album in these warm alleys.

Travel Information

Location: 16 Seodong-ro 141beon-gil, Geumjeong-gu, Busan
Recommended Points: Local street food like Egg Dumplings, exploring the maze alleys
Recommended Time: Evening
B-POP 'Healing' Course Travel TIPS

‧ Prepare an Acoustic & Indie Playlist
Rather than intense dance tracks, indie music featuring acoustic guitar melodies or gentle R&B pop fits this course well. Prepare some songs in advance where you can fully focus on the lyrics.

‧ Comfortable Clothes and Sneakers are a Must
Since you'll be walking on forest trails, fortress paths, and long promenades, comfortable sneakers and clothes that are easy to move in are not optional, but essential.

‧ Try a Digital Detox
Capturing beautiful scenery on your camera is great, but at Beomeosa Temple or Hoedong Reservoir, we recommend putting your smartphone down for a moment and fully absorbing the scenery with your eyes, ears, and heart.

‧ Enjoy Some Alone Time
While walking and chatting with someone is nice, this course is also the perfect route to walk alone and have a deep conversation with your inner self.

records.name: K-POP in Busan, The 「B-POP」 ‘Art’ Course
records.description:
A highly perfected album is bound to be accompanied by equally striking visuals. Following the diverse rhythms through Busan's alleys, nightscapes, and tranquil forests, the final theme of the B-POP tour is the 'Art' course, which will serve as the grand finale. If the previous journeys played Busan's hidden melodies, this course offers the experience of walking directly into a meticulously crafted and 'Conceptual K-POP Art Film' that captures both your eyes and ears.

Today, K-POP has moved beyond just music to listen to; it is recognized worldwide as a complete 'comprehensive art' combining fashion, visual beauty, and unique universes. The same goes for Busan. An abandoned factory is reborn as a sensational cultural space, cinematic imagination seeps along the coastline, and trains in pop-art primary colors run above the blue sea.

This B-POP 'Art' course is a journey that follows the various forms of aesthetics that Busan embraces. From the inspiration of contemporary art to cinematic landscapes and retro vibes resembling an album jacket. Experience a magical day where every step you take becomes a perfectly set music video shooting location.

B-POP ‘Art’ Course at a Glance

F1963 → Busan Museum of Art → Movie Street → Dongbaekseom Island → Blueline Park

‧ An overwhelming sense of space as if walking through a K-POP music video set
‧ Diverse visual delights including industrial, cinematic, and pop art themes
‧ A route where you can capture both artistic inspiration and aesthetic verification shots
‧ A Busan landmark tour that completes a perfect concept album
1. F1963
A Powerful Opening Track with an Industrial Vibe

The spectacular first track of the B-POP Art course begins at 'F1963,' a wire factory reborn as a complex cultural space. Coexisting with cold steel structures and warm cultural arts, this place exudes an overwhelming atmosphere the moment you step in, instantly captivating travelers' eyes.
When you watch music videos of K-POP groups featuring intense beats and performances, rough and vintage 'Industrial' concept backgrounds frequently appear. F1963 is a space that simultaneously boasts that raw charm and modern sophistication. Look around the exhibition halls where the traces of the old factory remain intact, and take photos in the courtyard or the large bookstore, which showcase sensational regenerative architectural beauty. As you enjoy the diverse art exhibitions and a fragrant cup of coffee, you will feel inspired as if you've become the main character of a trendy photoshoot or an artistic film.

Travel Information

Location: 20 Gurak-ro 123beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan
Recommended Points: Grandeur of regenerative architecture, viewing exhibitions, industrial vibe photography
Recommended Time: Morning
2. Busan Museum of Art
A Time for Artistic Inspiration to Awaken Inner Senses

If you tasted the rough texture of art at F1963, it's now time to dive into the refined world of contemporary art. The Busan Museum of Art is the center of Busan's visual arts where you can view the flow of domestic and international contemporary art at a glance. It is an attractive space where you can enjoy deep contemplation in tranquility.
Recently, numerous K-POP artists have been touring art museums around the world to gain inspiration, incorporating it into their music and visual arts. Now that the boundary between art and pop culture is blurring, time spent at an art museum is more than just viewing; it is a process of awakening your inner senses. Put on your earphones in front of various contemporary artworks and listen to a mysterious and dreamy K-POP track. You can experience a special synesthetic moment where the empty space of the artwork is filled with music, and two-dimensional paintings approach you like three-dimensional videos. (※ Depending on the time of visit and remodeling schedules, it is also great to utilize the outdoor sculpture park or the annex space.)

Travel Information

Location: 58 APEC-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Recommended Points: Contemporary art exhibitions, Space Lee Ufan, artistic relaxation
Recommended Time: Noon ~ Early Afternoon
3. Movie Street
Into a Cinematic K-POP Universe

Your steps, now filled with artistic inspiration, lead to 'Movie Street' right next to the Haeundae sea. The coastal promenade, where the dizzying skyscrapers of Marine City and the dazzling sun glints on the water harmonize, is engraved with records of numerous films set in Busan, adding joy to your walk.
Recent K-POP delivers a thrill similar to watching a movie by incorporating meticulous storytelling and a solid universe into each song. Standing on Movie Street with the Gwangan Bridge in the background, the surreal cityscape unfolding behind you feels like the climax set of a blockbuster music video. With the cinematic scenery as your backdrop, it is highly recommended to lift your camera and direct a dramatic shot containing your own storytelling. Utilizing the movie sculptures and trick art photo zones installed along the promenade will help you leave even more witty and aesthetic travel records.

Travel Information

Location: U-dong, Haeundae-gu, Busan (Marine City Coastal Road)
Recommended Points: Marine City skyscraper views, movie sculptures, coastal walk
Recommended Time: Afternoon
4. Dongbaekseom Island
A Grand Orchestration Created by Nature and the City

Walking along the coast from Movie Street naturally leads you to Dongbaekseom Island. Covered entirely with lush pine and camellia trees, this island is a representative healing spot in Haeundae where you can simultaneously feel the charm of forest trails and sea paths.
The intense contrast created by the Nurimaru APEC House met at the end of the forest path and Haeundae's high-rise building forest is truly a masterpiece. This dramatic contrast brings to mind a crossover K-POP song that gives an unexpected charm by sampling a grand orchestra sound over a sophisticated pop beat. A place where you can view Busan's most modern skyline while retaining the most natural form of a forest. Walk along the wooden deck lining the coastal cliff and listen to the crashing waves overlapping with a grand melody. Enjoying the dizzying thrill on the suspension bridge and looking out at the open sea from the observatory in front of the lighthouse will unfold an electrifying harmony of sight and sound that can only be felt on this course.

Travel Information

Location: 710-1 U-dong, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Recommended Points: Coastal promenade, Nurimaru APEC House view, harmony of nature and city
Recommended Time: Late Afternoon
5. Blueline Park
A Refreshing Album Jacket Shooting Location Where Retro Meets Pop Art

The finale of the B-POP Art course is decorated by Haeundae Blueline Park, the hottest visual landmark in Busan. This eco-friendly redevelopment of the abandoned old Donghae Nambu Line railway is a top tourist destination that satisfies both the fun of riding and the joy of viewing.
The sight of Sky Capsules and Beach Trains in vivid primary colors like yellow, red, and green passing over the endless deep blue sea is breathtaking. These popping colors emit a 'Pop Art' sensibility, looking exactly like a teen concept or Y2K retro concept album jacket of a K-POP idol brought to life. Around sunset, capture the passing capsule trains against the orange-tinted sea, or board the train yourself to admire the view outside the window, which looks like a moving picture frame. Looking at the colorful sculptures blending with the sea, you can perfectly conclude the playlist of this art course with the most refreshing and fairy-tale-like photo of your Busan trip.

Travel Information

Location: 116 Cheongsapo-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan (Cheongsapo Station, etc.)
Recommended Points: Sky Capsule & Beach Train, primary-colored pop art photo zones
Recommended Time: Around sunset ~ Evening
B-POP ‘Art’ Course Travel TIPS

‧ Prepare an OOTD that Matches the Concept
The Art course features distinct colors and vibes emanating from each space. Try a monochromatic or chic look at F1963, and a retro look with prominent primary colors at Blueline Park to challenge yourself for an album jacket-like photo.

‧ Cinematic & Dreamy Playlist
When appreciating contemporary art and overwhelming cityscapes, conceptual songs by idols with distinct universes, or electronic pop tracks with heavy bass, will further maximize the mood of your trip.

‧ Advance Reservations are Essential for Blueline Park
The Sky Capsule and Beach Train are extremely popular, making on-site ticketing difficult. To enjoy the sunset at your preferred time or reduce waiting times, be sure to make an advance reservation through the official website before visiting.

‧ Utilize Various Camera Angles
This is a route where massive senses of space (F1963, Movie Street) intersect with dense, detailed colors (Blueline Park). Use your smartphone camera's wide-angle mode to capture expansive landscapes, and properly utilize the portrait mode to direct various artistic compositions.

records.name: Three Dessert Cafes Loved by Locals and International Visitors
records.originalName: 외국인들에게도 사랑받고 있는 부산 디저트 카페 3
records.description:
Busan has become a hotspot for dessert lovers. If you’re looking to satisfy your sweet tooth, here are three signature dessert cafes that have become favorites among international visitors.

Subheading: 1. Kim Mochi – Giant Fresh Fruit Mochi You Have to Try

Kim Mochi is a trendy dessert cafe that opened just two months ago in Gwangalli. Its signature menu item is oversized fruit mochi filled with fresh, sweet fruit wrapped in delightfully chewy mochi.

Choose from a variety of fruits, including sweet mangoes, melons, strawberries, blueberries, and tangerines. In addition to its giant fruit mochi, the cafe also serves cream-filled mochi with specialty tapioca pearls, classic chewy mochi, and a variety of beverages.
Although it has only recently opened, the cafe has quickly gained popularity on social media, hosted a number of pop-up events, and continues to attract both local and international visitors.
Store InformationAddress
#103, 1F, 166 Gwangnam-ro, Suyeong-gu, Busan
Phone
+82-51-711-5516Hours
12:00 PM–8:00 PM (Closed on Tuesdays)

2. Busan Bada Sand – A Signature Busan Souvenir

Busan Bada Sand has become one of Busan’s signature dessert souvenirs and is a must-buy for many visitors. With locations in both Haeridangil Street and Gamcheon Culture Village, it’s easy to stop by while exploring some of Busan’s most popular attractions.
Its signature product is the Busan Bada Sand—butter sand cookies made with honey produced in Busan and premium French butter. They’re even more delicious when served chilled. In addition to Busan Bada Sand, the shop also offers Busan Bada Candy, Busan Bada Caramel, and Busan Bada Cookies.
Store InformationAddress
- Original Location: 1F, 21 Udong 1-ro 20beon-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan
- Busan Bada Sand Hills: 127 Gamnae 2-ro, Saha-gu, Busan
Hours
- Original Location: 11 AM–7 PM
- Busan Bada Sand Hills: 9:30 AM–6:00 PM

3. Keveren House – Soft and Creamy! Charming Dessert Gifts from Busan

Keveren House is a dessert cafe located in Haeridangil Street. From its vintage European-style storefront to its cozy, charming interior, the cafe offers a distinctive atmosphere that’s as delightful as its desserts. Its signature menu item is Duplit Bread, available in a variety of flavors filled with rich, creamy fillings.
Duplit Bread is sold in gift boxes of six or eight, making it an ideal souvenir or gift to bring home after your trip to Busan. Because the bakery itself is quite small, visitors who wish to dine in can enjoy their desserts at the nearby Duplit Cafe in Haeridangil Street.
Store InformationAddress
1F, 14-5 Udong 1-ro 38beonga-gil, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Signature Menu
Duplit Bread
Hours
11:00 AM–8:00 PM

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q1. Which dessert cafes in Busan are popular with international visitors?
A. Many dessert cafes in Busan are popular with international visitors. Kim Mochi in Gwangalli is known for its giant fresh fruit mochi, while Busan Bada Sand and Keveren House in Haeridangil Street are famous for their signature Busan desserts and beautifully packaged gift sets, making them excellent places to pick up souvenirs.

Q2. What are some good dessert souvenirs from Busan?
A. If you’re looking for dessert souvenirs that represent Busan, Busan Bada Sand and Keveren House’s Duplit Bread are excellent choices. Both shops offer attractively packaged gift sets that are perfect for bringing home or giving as gifts.

Q3. Are there dessert cafes near Gwangalli and Haeundae?
A. Yes. You can visit Kim Mochi near Gwangalli Beach, and Busan Bada Sand and Keveren House in the Haeridangil Street area near Haeundae Beach. Each cafe offers its own unique desserts and atmosphere, making them worthwhile stops during your visit to Busan.

records.name: Only Been to Haeundae? Here Are Three Busan Beaches to Visit This Summer
records.originalName: 해운대 말고 여기 어때요? 올여름 가볼 만한 부산 해수욕장 3곳
records.description:
When you think of Busan, one thing that comes to mind is the beach, the highlight of summer water fun. Once again, seven beaches in Busan, including Haeundae Beach, have opened for the season this year.

Haeundae Beach may be the best known, but Busan is home to beaches with unique charms all across the city. How about going on a special trip to another beach in Busan this summer to cool down?

2026 Busan Beach Opening Schedule

Let us start with the opening announcement and schedule for Busan’s beaches in 2026. Check the opening period before you visit to enjoy a safer and more pleasant summer getaway.

-	Haeundae Beach: June 26–September 15, 2026
-	Songjeong Beach: June 26–August 31, 2026
-	Gwangalli, Songdo, Dadaepo, Ilgwang, and Imnang Beaches: July 1–August 31, 2026

Where Should You Go Other Than Haeundae? Three Recommended Beaches

1. Gwangalli Beach, Where You Can Enjoy Night Views and Entertainment

Gwangalli Beach is one of Busan’s signature beaches, loved for its beautiful night views with Gwangandaegyo Bridge in the background.
Every Saturday night, a drone show lights up Gwangalli’s night sky, offering a special spectacle. Along the beach, cozy cafes and restaurants, as well as a rich selection of food and entertainment options, create a lively atmosphere from day to night.

Visitor InformationAddress
219 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro, Suyeong-gu, Busan

2. Songdo Beach, Perfect for Swimming and Fun Activities to Remember

Songdo Beach is Busan’s first public beach, known for offering a variety of experiences and activities.
In addition to swimming, there is plenty to enjoy, including the Songdo Marine Sea Car (Busan Air Cruise) crossing over the sea, Songdo Yonggung Suspension Bridge, and Amnam Park, making it a recommended destination for family travelers.

Visitor InformationAddress
100 Songdohaebyeon-ro, Seo-gu, Busan

3. Dadaepo Beach, the Beach with the Most Beautiful Sunset in Busan

Dadaepo Beach, known for its wide sandy beach and gentle shallow waters, is one of Busan’s signature sunset spots. After swimming, be sure to take in the coastal scenery turning red at sunset.
You can also visit nearby Dadaepo Beach Park, the Morundae Walking Trail, and the Gowooni Ecological Trail, making it a great destination to leisurely enjoy nature. Set apart from Busan’s urban landscapes, Dadaepo Beach offers visitors an encounter with serene and beautiful shores.

Visitor InformationAddress
Dadae-dong, Saha-gu, Busan

Creating an Enjoyable Beach Culture Together

Clean and safe beaches are created by the joint efforts of tourists and local residents. Please practice these small acts of consideration so everyone can enjoy Busan’s beaches comfortably!

 Beach Etiquettes for Everyone

-	Sort and dispose of trash in designated areas.
-	Follow no-smoking area guidelines.
-	Respect the privacy of others when taking photos.
-	Keep the volume of audio devices low to create a comfortable environment for everyone.
-	Use the beach with consideration for residents and other visitors.

This summer, we hope you experience the different charms of the sea at Busan’s many beaches and help create a healthy beach culture that everyone can enjoy together.

records.name: Discover Three Hidden Reading Spots in Busan
records.originalName: 부산에서 즐기는 책멍 여행, 이색 책 공간 3곳
records.description:
Summer heat is now in full swing. Why not escape indoors and quietly relax with a good book? Discover three reading spaces in Busan that go above and beyond. Each brings together cultural experiences, striking architecture, and quiet relaxation. Let’s take a closer look at each space.

Immerse Yourself in Film at the Library of Busan Cinema Center

Library of Busan Cinema Center is located on the fourth floor of the Double Cone at Busan Cinema Center in Centum City, Haeundae. Visitors can explore a wide range of specialized film resources. Browse Korean and international books on cinema and screenplay, or relax in the seating area.
The collection also includes film magazines and soundtrack LPs. Plus, DVDs can be watched free of charge.
The library also hosts screenings, film courses, and other cultural programs. Travelers seeking a deeper appreciation of film will find the library well worth a visit.

Visitor InformationAddress
4F, Double Cone, Busan Cinema Center, 120, Suyeonggangbyeon-daero, Haeundae-gu, Busan
Hours
10 AM–7 PM, Tuesday to Sunday (Closed on Mondays)Parking
Paid parking available (8 AM–11 PM / Cash not accepted)

Take a Break Near Busan Station at Bookdoochilseong Library

Only a five-minute walk away from Busan Station, Bookdoochilseong Library is a great place to stop by before beginning your trip or leaving Busan.
Soaring ceilings and tiered bookshelves give the interior a striking look, while readers of all ages can settle in with a book. During summer break, hands-on programs for children make this library especially popular with families.
Local souvenirs inspired by Busan are also available. Choose from postcards, magnets, T-shirts, and more. Travelers can also stop by for souvenirs before heading to or from Busan Station.

Visitor InformationAddress
1F, Building B, Hyupseong Marina G7, 160, Chungjang-daero, Dong-gu, Busan
Hours
10 AM–8 PM on Weekdays / 10 AM–8:30 PM on Weekends (Closed every Tuesday)Directions
Follow the pedestrian deck connected to Exit 6 of Busan KTX Station (less than a five-minute walk)
Parking
Paid underground parking available (₩500 per 10 minutes)

Where Books Meet Greenery, Jongno Books Square Garden

Jongno Books Square Garden recently opened at BIFC2 in Munhyeon Finance Complex. This cultural space brings a bookstore together with inviting places to relax. Warm wood interiors and spacious bookshelves create a welcoming environment. Visitors can browse stationery and lifestyle goods before continuing through an indoor moss garden to the outdoor Square Garden.
After reading in the bookstore, visitors can take a stroll through the garden or take a short break on the rooftop. The peaceful setting provides a welcome pause from the city after a good read. A food court and on-site café make the complex ideal for a half-day visit.

Visitor InformationAddress
3F, BIFC 2 Commercial Floor, 40, Munhyeongeumyung-ro, Nam-gu, Busan
Hours
10 AM–9 PMParking
Paid underground parking available

records.name: Two Breathtaking Sunset Destinations in West Busan to End Your Day
records.originalName: 부산에서의 하루를 아름답게 마무리하는 방법, 서부산 노을 명소 2곳
records.description:
Not only is Busan beautiful during the day, but it also reveals a different kind of charm after sunset. End your day by watching the sky glow in shades of orange, creating a truly unforgettable view. Explore these two special U to enjoy Busan’s breathtaking sunsets! Let’s explore two of West Busan’s most beautiful sunset destinations: Eulsukdo Island and Dadaepo Beach. Let’s discover Busan’s spectacular sunsets!

1. Eulsukdo Island, Where Sunsets Meet Nature

Eulsukdo Island is one of Busan’s premier ecotourism destinations. With its expansive reed fields and silver grass, Eulsukdo offers a different kind of beauty in every season. It is also well known as a winter habitat for migratory birds.
Visitors can enjoy a leisurely stroll or bike ride through Eulsukdo Ecological Park. The spacious lawns also make the park an ideal place for a relaxing picnic.
At sunset, the river, sky, and reed fields are bathed in warm shades of orange, creating a truly picturesque scene. Because the island’s natural environment has been carefully preserved, the scenery blends seamlessly with the surrounding landscape, making it an even more remarkable destination. Not too far from the city, Eulsukdo Ecological Park offers a peaceful escape where you can relax and reconnect with nature.

Visitor InformationAddress
1207 Hadan-dong, Saha-gu, Busan

2. Dadaepo Beach, Busan’s Signature Sunset Destination

Dadaepo Beach is one of Busan’s most iconic sunset destinations. Facing west toward the sea, visitors can watch the sun slowly sink below the horizon, where the crimson sky meets the wide sandy beach in a breathtaking display.
Try exploring the Gouni Eco Trail by the beach. Lined with silver grass and reeds, the boardwalk offers beautiful scenery throughout the year. As the sun begins to set, it becomes an especially atmospheric place for an evening walk. If you have extra time, be sure to visit Dadaepo Beach Park and the Morundae Peninsula as well. With the beach, forest trails, and beautiful sunsets all in one place, it’s an ideal destination for a half-day trip.
The 2026 Busan Sea Festival will take place at Dadaepo Beach from August 7 to 13. Visitors can enjoy various events, hands-on activities, and spectacular fireworks by the sea. Don’t miss this unforgettable summer festival by the sea!

Visitor InformationAddress
14 Morundae 1-gil, Saha-gu, Busan
Information
- Dadaepo Beach (July 1–August 31, 2026) 9 AM–6 PM
- 2026 Busan Sea Festival: Friday, August 7–Thursday, August 13, 2026 (7 days)

records.name: An Indoor Exhibition to Visit in Gijang-gun, Busan: Alice Dalton Brown: The Light Within
records.originalName: 부산 기장 가볼만한 실내 전시 추천, 부산 앨리스 달튼 브라운전
records.description:
Looking for an indoor attraction in Busan? The Alice Dalton Brown retrospective is currently on view at LP Crystal in Gijang-gun. The venue is part of the Ananti at Busan Village complex, with the exhibition spread across the first floor and basement level.

Set against the seaside landscape of Busan, the exhibition showcases works infused with light and the feeling of a gentle breeze. From visitor information to guided tour schedules, here’s everything you need to know.

Helpful Tips Before Your Visit

The exhibition is currently on view at LP Crystal, part of Ananti at Busan Village. The first floor and basement level feature spacious galleries for a relaxed viewing experience.

- LP Crystal Parking Information & Tips

The Ananti complex is quite large, so choosing the right parking entrance can save you a long walk to the exhibition. Use the second parking entrance rather than the first.
Parking: After your visit, register your vehicle at the gift shop for two hours of free parking.

- Exhibition Highlights from My Visit

1. From Everyday Moments to Expansive Seascapes

Alice Dalton Brown’s early works capture the warmth of everyday life, from light reflected off toys at home to sunlight falling across a farmhouse roof. A turning point came in 1994, when Dalton Brown saw curtains billowing in the breeze through a friend’s window. Her later works drew inspiration from a cottage on Cayuga Lake. These works beautifully showcase the remarkable precision and delicacy of Dalton Brown’s oil painting technique.

2. Calming Light and Shadow (1F & B1)

The galleries on the first floor and basement level feature different wall colors, ranging from warm orange to muted purple and cool blue. Each color scheme complements the works and draws you further into the exhibition. The large paintings of the sea seen through white curtains billowing in the breeze are especially striking. The translucent fabric and gentle ripples are rendered with such realism that you may find yourself standing there for quite some time.

3. Visiting on the Weekend? Special Guided Tour Information

If you’re planning a weekend visit, consider timing your trip around one of the guided tours. Art Director Kim Jong-won leads a special program titled “The Man Who Reads Paintings.” The tour explores the artist’s childhood and the stories behind Dalton Brown’s use of light and space.

- Days: Every Saturday and Sunday
- Hours: Session 1 (1–2 PM) / Session 2 (4–5 PM)
- Fee: KRW 10,000 per person (exhibition admission not included)

Before you leave, be sure to stop by the gift shop. You’ll find a selection of exhibition-related items, including postcards, fans, notebooks, and magnets. Let the exhibition stay with you a little longer.
The quiet mood of the works blends naturally with Ananti’s laid-back setting. It’s a peaceful place to slow down and take a break. For anyone looking for a different kind of exhibition or a date idea in Busan, it’s well worth a visit.

Visitor InformationExhibition
Alice Dalton Brown: The Light Within
Dates
May 23–Sep. 27, 2026
Venue
LP Crystal (1F & B1), Ananti at Busan Village
Public Transportation
- By Donghae Line: Take Exit 1 at Osiria Station and transfer to Bus 139, 185, or 1001. Get off near Yonggungsa Temple or the National Institute of Fisheries Science, then continue on foot.
- By Taxi: If the weather is hot or you’re traveling as a group, taking a taxi from Osiria Station is another convenient option. The ride takes about 5–10 minutes.

records.name: Great Spots for a Night Walk! 3 Places to See Gwangandaegyo Bridge in Busan
records.originalName: 야경 산책 명소 추천! 부산 광안대교 뷰 여행지 3
records.description:
Written and Photographed by: Kim Hee-won and Han Jin-hee, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators

(Source: Kim Hee-won, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

Busan has plenty of places known for great night views, including Hwangnyeongsan Observatory, Yeongdo Cheonghak Reservoir Observatory, and Gwangalli Beach. This time, I’d like to introduce three less familiar spots where you can take in beautiful views of Gwangandaegyo Bridge in the cool evening breeze.

Shall we head out together on a summer night walk in search of beautiful nighttime views?

(Source: Kim Hee-won, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

Dongsaengmal Observatory in Igidae Park is a great spot for a nighttime drive with views of Gwangandaegyo Bridge. It sits at the starting point of the Igidae Coastal Trail in Yongho-dong.

The coastal walking trails are also well maintained, making the area worth visiting even during the day.
 
(Source: Kim Hee-won, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

Parking at Dongsaengmal Observatory is free and available at all times.

Many visitors stop briefly to take in the night view and then leave, so even when there was a wait, it was no more than about 10 minutes. Parking was not difficult, making this a great spot for a nighttime drive in Busan.
 
(Source: Kim Hee-won, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

The name Dongsaengmal means “the eastern end of the mountain.”

I arrived by car, and the moment I rounded the corner, the sea opened up before me with Gwangandaegyo Bridge glowing in the distance.

I have visited many places known for nighttime views of the bridge, but the view from Dongsaengmal Observatory felt refreshingly different.
 
(Source: Kim Hee-won, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

Dongsaengmal Observatory also marks the starting point of the Igidae Coastal Trail and Haeparang Trail, with convenient facilities and a well-maintained wooden deck path.

The views of Gwangandaegyo Bridge and Haeundae Marine City framed by the photo zone installation were truly romantic, making the Dongsaengmal Observatory the perfect spot for a romantic night.

Plenty of benches let you stop and rest, making it a pleasant place to take in the scenery while enjoying a cool breeze on a hot summer evening.

Visitor InformationLocation
San1 Yongho-dong, Nam-gu, Busan
Hours
Open 24 hours
Nam-gu Office, Parks and Greenery Division
051-607-4544

(Source: Han Jin-hee, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

The walking route begins in Centum City and follows the Suyeong River to Millak Waterside Park. Much of the route is flat, making it great for running or a leisurely walk with views of Busan along the way.
 
(Source: Han Jin-hee, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

As you follow the riverside path, the fresh scent of the sea gradually begins to fill the air. The mix of river and city views keeps the walk interesting from start to finish.
 
(Source: Han Jin-hee, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

Once you reach Millak Waterside Park, you can take a break and cool off in the sea breeze. The impressive nighttime view of Gwangandaegyo Bridge is a nice bonus. If you get hungry, fresh sashimi at the nearby Millak Hoe (Raw Fish) Center makes a perfect way to finish the walk. 
 
(Source: VISIT BUSAN; photo was taken during the Millac Luce Festa)

The flat, well-maintained path makes this an easy route for a casual walk at any time.

Visitor InformationLocation
110-9 Millak-dong, Suyeong-gu, Busan
Admission
Free / Open year-round with no restrictions

(Source: VISIT BUSAN)

Hwangnyeongsan Observatory is one of Busan’s best-known spots for night views. As the sun sets and the city lights begin to come on, panoramic views of downtown Busan and the sea unfold below. The observatory is especially popular in summer, drawing plenty of visitors who stay late into the evening to take in the view.
 
(Source: VISIT BUSAN)

A 360-degree skyline stretches across the city, with impressive views in every direction.
 
(Source: Han Jin-hee, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators)

Several viewpoints along the way to the observatory let you stop and take in the view of the Gwangandaegyo Bridge below. As you near the summit, more of Busan’s nightscape comes into view, giving you a preview of the panorama waiting at the top.
 
(Source: VISIT BUSAN)

Hwangnyeongsan Observatory is one of the few places where you can take in both the sea and the city at once. With Gwangandaegyo Bridge sparkling in the distance, Gwangalli Beach below, and the city lights filling the view, the observatory is well worth a stop during a trip to Busan!

Visitor InformationLocation
San50-18 Jeonpo-dong, Busanjin-gu, Busan
Admission
Free / Open year-round with no restrictions

Q&A

Q1. What other place in Busan would you recommend visiting on the same trip as Dongsaengmal Observatory?
A. I recommend Oryukdo Sunrise Park. It is about a 15-minute drive from Igidae Park. You can also visit Oryukdo Skywalk for sweeping views of Busan. 

Q2. Of the three night-view spots, is there one that is good for running?
A. I recommend the route to Millak Waterside Park. Most of the route is flat, making it an easy course for walking or running. It is a great choice for a light run or walk, especially if you want to see Gwangandaegyo Bridge up close at night.

records.name: Recommending a Hidden Observation Deck in Busan! The Donggu Library’s Chaengmaru Observatory
records.originalName: 부산 숨은 명소, 전망대 추천! 부산 동구도서관 책마루전망대
records.address: 54 Seongbuk-ro 36beon-gil, Dong-gu, Busan
records.hours:
9 AM–10 PM / Closed Mondays and public holidays (except Sundays)
(The library is closed when a Sunday coincides with another public holiday.)
records.description:
Written and Photographed by: Han Go-un, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators

Looking for a place in Busan where you can enjoy beautiful scenery and a refreshing breeze this fall? There’s a unique observation deck in Dong-gu, Busan, that’s perfect for enjoying the changing season. It’s a wonderful place to read a book, take in the scenery, and enjoy the arrival of autumn. Shall we go check it out together?
If you drive along Busan’s hillside roads and pass Webtoon Ibagu-gil, a street lined with cartoon murals, you’ll find Donggu Library nearby.
Free parking is available in the dedicated parking lot in front of Donggu Library. Because the library is located on high ground and can be difficult to reach on foot, many visitors come by car. As a result, the parking lot can get somewhat crowded on weekends. Even so, there was plenty of parking space during my visit, as cars can park all the way up to the entrance of the parking lot.
A walking trail called “Chaekmaru-gil” connects the lower road to Donggu Library. On a spring or autumn day when the weather is neither too hot nor too cold, it’s lovely to take a leisurely walk along the trail while enjoying the murals and tile artwork. And you don’t even have to make it all the way to the Chaengmaru Observatory to enjoy a breathtaking panoramic view. You can already see an impressive view from right beside the parking lot.
There are two ways to reach the Chaengmaru Observatory. The first is to use the outdoor elevator located to the right of Donggu Library when facing the building. This elevator takes you directly to the observation deck. It operates only between the first and fourth floors and does not pass through the library interior. The elevator takes you directly to the observation deck, making it convenient for visitors with strollers or wheelchairs.
The second option is to enter Donggu Library, take the elevator to the third floor, and then use the stairs to reach the rooftop observation deck. If you need to use the restroom or water purifier, be sure to use the facilities inside the library.
When you arrive at the Chaengmaru Observatory, you’ll be greeted by an expansive view of the open sky. The observation deck opened recently, so it has a clean, modern feel. The entire rooftop has been transformed into an observation deck, providing plenty of open space to explore.
You’ll also find a variety of sculptures that perfectly complement the name Donggu Library Chaengmaru Observatory. There is a photo zone featuring a book-shaped sculpture, while cute characters reading books are placed throughout the surrounding wooden deck.
One particularly thoughtful feature is the smartphone holder on top of the yellow pencil-shaped sculpture. Place your phone in the holder, and it lines up perfectly with the book sculpture in the photo zone! So even if you’re visiting alone or don’t have a tripod, you can simply set your phone’s timer and take a lovely photo to remember your visit.
On one side of the observation deck, you’ll find a large pencil sculpture surrounded by circular steps. Climb the steps, and you’ll discover a sculpture shaped like an old-fashioned television, along with a bench shaped like a book.
Stand behind the television sculpture, and you can take a fun photo that makes it look as though you’re actually inside the TV! With cute sculptures and photo zones scattered throughout the observation deck, there’s plenty to discover as you explore.
Spectacular views unfold in both directions from the observation deck. In front of you, you can see the Busan Harbor Bridge and Busan South Port. Behind you lies a more authentic, unfiltered side of Busan, with views of neighborhoods such as Beomil-dong and Hocheon Village, known for their charming and picturesque residential scenery. The area is also well known as a filming location for TV dramas. While the scenery is beautiful during the day, it is particularly famous for its stunning nighttime views. I highly recommend taking an evening drive to the Donggu Library Chaengmaru Observatory and enjoying the beauty of Busan after dark!
Because this spot has not yet attracted large crowds, it’s a great place to visit at a leisurely pace. Come by yourself to read a book, admire the scenery, and quietly take in the sights of Busan. Best of all, admission is free, so you can stop by without hesitation!

Q&A

Q. Is the Chaengmaru Observatory at Donggu Library open at all times?
A. The Chaengmaru Observatory, located on the rooftop of Donggu Library, is not open 24 hours a day, so be sure to check the operating hours before your visit. We also recommend reviewing the visitor guidelines in advance. Drones, pets, food, and smoking are not permitted.

records.name: Places to Visit at Night in Busan: From the Sunset Fountain of Dreams to Dadaepo Beach and Gouni Eco Trail
records.originalName: 부산 야간 가볼만한 곳, 다대포 꿈의 낙조분수부터 해수욕장·고우니생태길까지
records.address: 14 Morundae 1-gil, Saha-gu, Busan (Sunset Fountain of Dreams)
records.hours:
Through September 30, 2026 (Closed Mondays)
- August: Weekdays (8 PM), Weekends (8 PM & 9 PM)
- September: Weekdays (7:30 PM), Weekends (7:30 PM & 8:30 PM)
- Duration: 20 minutes
records.description:
Written and Photographed by: Kim Yong-beom, 6th Batch of GoBoogi Creators

These days, the weather is still hot when the sun is out, yet staying indoors all day can feel stifling. At times like these, you may find yourself looking for somewhere to go as the sun begins to set. If you’re wondering where to go and how to spend your evening, I recommend Dadaepo Beach.
Dadaepo Beach is the perfect destination for an itinerary that stretches from sunset into the night. You can stroll along the expansive beach at sunset, then, after dark, enjoy the Gouni Eco Trail and the Sunset Fountain of Dreams, where music, water, and lights come together in harmony.

Sunset Fountain of Dreams: A Harmony of Music, Water, and Light

(Source: Busan Tourism Archive)

One of the most famous attractions at Dadaepo Beach is the Sunset Fountain of Dreams.
The Sunset Fountain of Dreams is a musical fountain where jets of water move in sync with music, accompanied by colorful lighting effects.

This ground-level fountain features a circular design with a diameter of 60 meters and a circumference of 180 meters, with water jets reaching a maximum height of 55 meters. It is a popular attraction enjoyed by visitors from around the world!
 
During the performance, jets of water rise and fall in sync with the music, blending seamlessly with dynamic lighting effects to create a captivating show that keeps you entertained from beginning to end. Best of all, admission is free, making it a great place to enjoy a refreshing evening.

Take a Walk Along Dadaepo Beach at Sunset

I recommend arriving at Dadaepo Beach a little early rather than timing your arrival just for the Sunset Fountain of Dreams Show. That’s because there are plenty of great places to explore nearby.

I especially recommend visiting Dadaepo Beach before the performance. Personally, I think the greatest charm of Dadaepo Beach is its sunset scenery.
As the sun slowly sinks beyond the expansive sandy beach, the colors of the sea and sky gradually change, creating a beautiful moment that makes you stop and take it all in.

Experience a Different Side of Dadaepo Beach on the Gouni Eco Trail After Sunset

If you visit Dadaepo Beach, don’t limit yourself to the beach—be sure to explore the nearby Gouni Eco Trail as well.
This trail offers a different atmosphere from walking while looking out at the sea. The Gouni Eco Trail is a walking path that offers close-up views of the wetlands and natural surroundings of the Dadaepo Beach area.
 
It’s a wonderful place to take a leisurely stroll while enjoying the scenery after sunset. In particular, as the sun begins to set, the colors of the sky blend with the reeds and wetlands to create an atmosphere unique to Dadaepo Beach.

Once it gets dark, the lights along the Gouni Eco Trail come on, adding another layer of beauty to the trail and making it an even more enjoyable place for an evening walk.
 
If you’re visiting Dadaepo Beach, don’t just time your arrival for the fountain show. Try to get there a little early so you can explore Dadaepo Beach and the Gouni Eco Trail as well.
Take in the sea, watch the sunset, and finally enjoy a fountain show where music, water, and light come together. If you want to spend a special evening in Busan, Dadaepo Beach is a romantic choice!

Q&A

Q1. What are the operating hours for the Sunset Fountain of Dreams?

In 2026, the Sunset Fountain of Dreams will operate from April 24 through September 30 and will be closed every Monday.
In September, performances are scheduled for 7:30 PM on weekdays and for both 7:30 PM and 8:30 PM on weekends and public holidays.

Q2. What is a good itinerary for visiting Dadaepo Beach in Busan?

GoBoogi recommends the following itinerary: Dadaepo Beach (one hour before sunset) → Enjoy the sunset → Gouni Eco Trail (after sunset) → Sunset Fountain of Dreams (arrive and take your seat 10 minutes before the show)

For the perfect evening itinerary, arrive before sunset to enjoy the sea and beautiful sunset views, take a leisurely stroll along the Gouni Eco Trail, and wrap up your day with the musical fountain show.

records.name: Inside the Busan Biennale 2026 Opening Ceremony: A Guide to “Dissident Chorus”
records.originalName: 2026 부산비엔날레 개막식 참석 후기, ‘불협하는 합창’ 전시정보까지
